Results indicate that while values such as individual rights, the common good, and accountability are regularly invoked, additional guidance around public values like citizen engagement, workplace standards, and responsiveness may be necessary to prevent public value failure. The study further categorizes governance strategies in AI policy documents into regulatory, service‐based, and informational instruments, and finds that regulatory policies are most likely to engage with public values.

papers.title: Responsible Algorithmization in the Public Sector: A “Natural Perspective” Based on Ethnographic Research in Regulation, Policing, and Healthcare
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Responsible algorithmization refers to the use of algorithms in the public sector while safeguarding public values. Approaches to responsible algorithmization suggested by the EU, OECD, and others depart from a rational perspective and highlight formal structures and procedures. This paper complements this perspective by adding a “natural perspective,” which emphasizes sense‐making and actual practices. This natural perspective is used for a set of ethnographic studies of algorithmization in three domains in the Netherlands: regulation, policing, and healthcare. Our findings show that algorithmization of government organizations is an emergent, political, open, and fragmented process, rather than, as assumed by rational approaches to responsible algorithmization, pre‐structured, neutral, closed, and simple. This means that rational approaches fall short of providing a comprehensive basis for establishing responsible algorithmization. We conclude that not only passive responsibility but also active responsibility for algorithmization in the public sector needs to be addressed to safeguard public values.

papers.title: Advantages of a Two-Stage Randomized Trial Design to Evaluate Antimicrobial Treatment Strategies: a Simulation Study
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Antimicrobial prescribing policies affect not only treated patients but also their contacts. Two-stage randomized (2SR) designs can be used to estimate these spillover effects, yet this study design has not been widely applied to evaluate antimicrobial strategies. Methods We developed a stochastic agent-based model that simulates a hospital ward with two competing bacterial strains (drug-A-susceptible and drug-A-resistant). We used the simulation to emulate a 2SR trial: six hospital ward clusters were randomized 1:1 to either a 90/10 (90% Drug A, 10% Drug B, drug B was assumed to have no known resistance) or 50/50 treatment allocation strategy; individuals within clusters were then randomized to Drug A or Drug B following the assigned cluster-level allocation strategy. We estimated direct, indirect, total, and overall causal effects on incident infection and mortality. Sensitivity analyses varied the treatment effect, transmission rate, mortality structure, and number of clusters. Results The direct effect of drug choice showed that Drug A recipients had higher mortality (due to non-concordant treatment of resistant infections). This effect varied over time as the ward’s strain ecology diverged between strategies. There was also an indirect effect for Drug A recipients—reflecting spillover from higher resistant-strain prevalence under 90/10—but it was approximately null for Drug B recipients, whose broad-spectrum coverage insulated them from changes in the ward strain distribution. The overall effect—the policy-level comparison—showed that the 50/50 strategy reduced total mortality, but this net benefit concealed a redistribution: resistant-strain deaths decreased while susceptible-strain deaths increased, a consequence captured by the overall effect but invisible to the direct effect. These findings were qualitatively consistent across all sensitivity scenarios. Conclusions We demonstrate that antimicrobial prescribing produces spillover effects not captured by conventional individually randomized trials. These effects can substantially alter treatment outcomes in a population. We propose that the 2SR design, grounded in a formal causal framework for interference, is better suited for evaluating population-level effects of antimicrobial strategies—whether implemented as a randomized trial or emulated with observational data.

papers.title: Effects of a parenting intervention on child maltreatment among Filipino families: Testing mechanisms of change
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Masayang Pamilya para sa Batang Pilipino (MaPa) program is an evidence-based, culturally adapted parenting program designed to reduce child maltreatment in Filipino families. In a randomized controlled trial, families who received MaPa had significant reductions in child maltreatment compared to control families, both at post-intervention and at one-year follow up. However, the mechanisms by which the reduction in child maltreatment is sustained has yet to be established. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated overreactive parenting and positive parenting as potential mediators of the sustained effects of MaPa on reducing child maltreatment. PARTICIPANTS: Parents (N = 120) of children aged two to six were randomly allocated to either the MaPa program or treatment as usual (TAU). All parents were recruited from a community setting and were enrolled in the government's conditional cash transfer program. METHODS: A latent-variable parallel mediation model was tested using parent-report data measured at baseline, immediate post-intervention, and at one-year follow-up. Measures were included on overreactive parenting, positive parenting, and child abuse. RESULTS: Those who received MaPa exhibited reduced overreactive parenting post-intervention compared to TAU, which in turn marginally mediated the sustained effects of MaPa on child maltreatment occurrence at follow-up. Positive parenting, however, did not mediate the effects of MaPa on risk of child maltreatment. CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that MaPa effectively reduces overreactive parenting, which in turn may be among the mechanisms that reduces child maltreatment in families with young children. Findings provide evidence that reducing overreactive parenting may be an effective pathway towards reducing violence against children.

papers.title: Building food security from the periphery: a study of adaptation and social innovation in the Natuna border region, Indonesia
Impacts of farm electrification on irrigation costs and food crop yields in India’s smallholder agriculture
papers.abstract: Abstract Irrigation costs constitute a substantial share of crop production costs, which often hamper cash-strapped smallholders from applying sufficient water to achieve better crop yields. In Bihar, one of India’s major agrarian states characterized by smallholder-dominated cereal-based cropping system, a mega government-led intervention is transforming irrigation system by replacing costly diesel-powered irrigation pumps with electric ones. We evaluated the farm-level impacts of electrification on energy costs for irrigation, water management, and crop yields of the two principal food crops of the region, i.e., rice and wheat. Using survey data from 600 farmers, we applied propensity score-based Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting (IPTW) to estimate causal impacts. Irrigation electrification reduced irrigation costs by three-fourths for rice and two-thirds for wheat. Irrigation cost reductions for wheat exhibited spatial heterogeneity, with larger benefits in areas where groundwater levels were deeper than 4.4 m. Lower irrigation costs led to increased irrigation intensity for both crops, with more pronounced effects for rice. Rice yields increased by 8% (382 kg ha −1 ) on average, with higher yield gains (> 500 kg ha −1 ) in areas with groundwater levels above 3.6 m. Wheat yields increased more uniformly across the state, by 6% (203 kg ha −1 ). These findings provide quantifiable evidence on the linkages between irrigation costs and agricultural productivity for key staple in smallholder systems, highlighting the moderating role of groundwater conditions within the context of the study area.

papers.title: Harnessing digital capabilities and human capital to strengthen food security under climate stress: evidence from a global dynamic panel
The effect of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy on sexual self-esteem in women with breast cancer after mastectomy: a randomized controlled trial
Absenteeism and Presenteeism in Times of Change: The Role of Stress and Job Satisfaction
papers.abstract: This study investigates sickness absenteeism and sickness presenteeism in the context of organizational development (OD) changes in the police force, focusing on health-related and motivational pathways. Using panel data from 407 employees from 36 Danish police units (1,021 observations), we analyze attendance patterns before the change, immediately after, and 1 year later. Findings reveal that sickness absenteeism is primarily influenced by the type of OD change rather than by job satisfaction or stress, while sickness presenteeism decreases with higher job satisfaction independent of the change type. Notably, employees experiencing an OD change aimed at supporting a long-term vision exhibit reduced sickness absence in the change period. OD changes focused on distributed leadership and enhancing employee motivation did not have the same effect on sickness absenteeism. These results underscore the importance of considering both motivational and health-related dynamics, as well as the type of change, in understanding attendance during OD change.

papers.title: Optimizing rooftop–façade ratio for enhancing stability of building-integrated photovoltaic system in the Asia-Pacific region
papers.abstract: Solar energy is a promising renewable energy source for achieving net-zero carbon emissions because of its low cost and ease of installation, including in buildings. However, the variability of solar energy is currently the main issue affecting the reliability of its implementation and integration into power grid systems. Understanding how solar power generation behaves when installed in a building with a monitoring system is important. Highly spatiotemporal information is required to visualize the detailed behavior of generated solar power. This study integrated a high-temporal geostationary satellite-derived product with 10 min observations and building-height information to obtain high-spatiotemporal solar power observations for a geospatial-based analysis in the Asia-Pacific region. Compared with the existing PV site, this integration showed a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.791 for 10 min observations and 0.917 for daily average observations. Rooftop and façade solar power observations were then used to calculate the optimal rooftop-to-façade ratio for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) to achieve greater stability and lower fluctuations than rooftop-only systems. This study used 3 years of observation (2022–2024) and was conducted across 55 cities in the Asia-Pacific region, covering diverse climatic conditions. This study used a minimally constrained optimization algorithm, with stability index (SI) as the main objective function, to determine the optimal ratio. Optimizing the rooftop-façade ratio can increase daily stability by approximately 5%–30% and decrease daily fluctuation by approximately 15%–30%, with the greatest gains in tropical regions. The proposed framework is generic and can be applied to other cities worldwide where geostationary satellite and urban 3D building data are available, providing a scalable tool for assessing and planning urban BIPV. This approach provides a robust tool for urban BIPV assessment and planning, supporting the large-scale deployment of stable solar energy to achieve net-zero carbon emissions and mitigate climate change.

papers.title: High-efficiency full-spectrum solar utilization via a novel continuous spectral splitting concentrator: design, optical validation, and system-level performance assessment
papers.abstract: Spectral Beam Splitting (SBS) is a promising technology to precisely manage the solar spectrum and cascaded utilization of solar energy. However, conventional discrete SBS techniques experience an exponential rise in optical loss with successive splitting, thereby constraining the maximum number of feasible divisions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Novel Continuous Spectral Splitting Concentrator (CSSC) based on a refractive prism array. The CSSC enables an approximate spatial separation of spectral splitting and light concentration along orthogonal directions, generating a continuous “rainbow-like” spectrum with improved spectral resolution. A comprehensive optical-electrical model was developed and validated against experimental results, showing a Root Mean Square Deviation of 8.2% in energy flux distribution. Through a comprehensive parametric study, we identified the trade-offs between the spectral splitting coefficient and optical efficiency, determining an optimal prism apical angle limit of 21.5°. The optimized CSSC achieves an optical efficiency of 85.2% in the present configuration. The system achieved a high spectral resolution with a Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) of approximately 110 nm. A coupled optical-electrical case study indicates that integrating the proposed CSSC with a laterally arranged InGaP/GaAs/Ge cell array could achieve a photovoltaic efficiency of 37.0% under 400× concentration. These results suggest that the CSSC can serve as a promising optical platform for spectrum-selective solar-energy utilization.

papers.title: From border carbon penalties to domestic action: can domestic carbon pricing provide a fairer solution to carbon leakage?
papers.abstract: Amid the rapid reconfiguration of the global climate governance regime, border carbon adjustments (BCAs) are reshaping the international allocation of mitigation costs through trade and extraterritorial policy effects. Carbon charges based on embodied-emission estimates affect international competitiveness and may impose additional adjustment pressures on developing economies. Using a recursively updated multi-regional computable general equilibrium model based on the GTAP-E database, combined with input–output accounting to derive bilateral, sector-specific ad valorem trade shocks, this study evaluates the economic, environmental, and welfare effects of alternative carbon-pricing regimes, including unilateral border adjustments, coordinated domestic pricing, and cost-equity-based differentiated pricing. The results show that border-only measures achieve modest global emissions reductions while redistributing trade and welfare effects across economies, without uniformly benefiting all implementing countries. Uniform domestic pricing achieves the largest emissions reduction but also the greatest welfare loss, whereas differentiated pricing retains a substantial share of mitigation with lower welfare costs. China's domestic pricing response strengthens its mitigation relative to reliance on foreign border measures alone, although its global effects remain limited. These findings inform the comparative design of carbon-pricing policies and China's carbon-footprint governance.

papers.title: Strategic pathways for decarbonization: a data-driven typology to strengthen climate policy
Renewable energy droughts under high variable renewables penetration: meteorological drivers, system impacts, and planning uses
An Atmospheric Perspective on Emerging Water Microdroplet Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Microdroplets, as tiny liquid particles, are ubiquitous in Earth’s atmosphere. They serve as dynamic microreactors that drive atmospheric processes, with profound implications for air quality, climate regulation, and atmospheric chemical cycles. Despite its importance, microdroplet-driven chemistry remains inadequately represented in global climate and air quality models. This perspective synthesizes emerging evidence on how microdroplet interface-enhanced multiphase chemistry modifies atmospheric processes including amplifying atmospheric oxidation capacity and accelerating the transformation of key reactive species. Advances in aerosol and microdroplet chemistry highlight the central role of the microdroplet interface in initiating accelerated kinetics and in enabling unprecedented chemical pathways distinct from those in macroscopic bulk solutions. We outline the current knowledge gaps and future directions for advancing the research in microdroplet chemistry from an atmospheric perspective. The concerted coordination among microdroplet chemistry and atmospheric communities across field, laboratory, and modeling has significant implications for understanding the critical role of microdroplet interface-driven chemistry in the atmosphere and climate change.

papers.title: Exposomic Assessment of Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals Using Hair: A Cross-Matrix Comparison with Serum and Urine by LC-HRMS and Metabolite Profiling
papers.abstract: Abstract Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are increasingly implicated in chronic diseases, yet their biomonitoring in human studies still relies mainly on urine and serum, which capture only short-term exposure to these fast-elimination compounds. Here, we evaluated hair as a complementary and long-term biomonitoring matrix for EDC mixtures by integrating it into an LC-HRMS exposomics workflow together with paired serum and urine samples. We developed and validated a method targeting 44 endocrine disruptors from five chemical families (benzophenones, phthalates, parabens, bisphenols, and organophosphate esters), combining quantitative analysis with suspect screening and semi-quantification of phase II metabolites. Applied to samples from 20 postmenopausal women, the hair-based approach provided the broadest coverage and highest concentrations (31/44 compounds), up to about three orders of magnitude higher than in urine or serum, consistent with distinct accumulation mechanisms and temporal integration windows. In hair, EDCs were present in unconjugated form (>99%), whereas urine was dominated by conjugated metabolites and serum showed limited detection. Overall, these findings demonstrate that integrating hair into multimatrix exposomics designs substantially expands both the chemical and temporal resolution of human exposure assessment.

papers.title: Industrial-Scale Production of Photocatalytic Hydrogen in China: Life Cycle Environmental and Economic Assessment in Comparison with Other Solar and Conventional Technologies
papers.abstract: Abstract This study evaluates for the first time the sustainability of photocatalytic hydrogen production in China utilizing a 26-faced polyhedron SrTiO3/Rh/Co/Cr photocatalyst. Life cycle assessment and costing are used to estimate the impacts and levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH). These are compared via multicriteria decision analysis with alternative solar-driven hydrogen technologies (water electrolysis, photoelectrochemical, and thermochemical), as well as with conventional methods (steam methane reforming and coal gasification). The outcomes are used to identify optimal regional configurations in different provinces that minimize both the impacts and production costs. Photocatalytic hydrogen substantially outperforms conventional methods, reducing most impacts by 21–93%, including climate change (67–93%). However, several impacts are significantly higher, increasing from 48% to 20 times. Economically, photocatalytic hydrogen is competitive with conventional methods (1.58–2.42 k$/t H2 vs 1.18–2.38 k$/t H2). Enhancing photocatalyst stability, optimizing solar-to-hydrogen efficiency, integrating renewable electricity, and valorizing oxygen as a coproduct can further improve environmental performance and cost-effectiveness. In comparison with the other solar and conventional methods, photocatalytic hydrogen is the most sustainable option, along with the perovskite/silicon photoelectrochemical alternative. The findings provide critical guidance for scaling up solar-driven hydrogen production and inform policy, research, and regional deployment strategies.

papers.title: Joint Effects of Water Quality Degradation and Non-Native Fish Invasion on Estuarine Biodiversity and Ecosystem Stability
papers.abstract: Abstract Water quality degradation and biological invasions represent major drivers of global ecosystem degradation, yet their interactive effects remain poorly understood, especially in anthropogenically disturbed estuarine ecosystems. Here, we employed environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding to characterize multi-trophic biological communities in a subtropical estuary and to assess how water-quality degradation influences the invasion success of non-native fishes. The results show, firstly, the relative sequence abundance of non-native fish, rather than their species richness, emerged as the primary factor negatively associated with native fish diversity. Based on the observational dataset, we identified a statistical breakpoint, and the transition from low to high invasion pressure corresponds to a unimodal (hump-shaped) diversity pattern. Secondly, non-native fish primarily compete for food resources, thereby constraining the ecological niches of native species. Thirdly, a strong interactive effect exists between water quality degradation and non-native fish invasion. Water quality degradation acts not merely as a direct environmental stressor, but also indirectly weakens native communities. Collectively, these findings provide new insights into how declines in water quality interact with biological invasions and highlight the need for integrated invasion management strategies that simultaneously improve water quality and mitigate the impacts of invasive species in estuarine ecosystems.

papers.title: PM2.5 Constituents and Cardiopulmonary Dysfunctions in Older Adults: A Multiomics Approach Unveiling Molecular Pathways
papers.abstract: Abstract The cardiopulmonary risks of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) are linked to its constituents, yet key constituents and underlying molecular pathways driving cardiopulmonary dysfunctions in older adults remain elusive. In a longitudinal panel study of 313 measurements, we assessed associations between PM2.5 constituents and cardiopulmonary functions and explored mediation effects by DNA methylation and gene transcription using personal monitoring data. We combined a linear mixed-effects model with three machine-learning methods to identify key PM2.5 constituents, and employed mediation analysis and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis to explore potential epigenetic and transcriptional mediators and biological pathways. Our findings revealed that chloride ion (Cl–), nickel (Ni), barium, and selenium were the key constituents of PM2.5 inducing cardiopulmonary dysfunction. Interquartile range (IQR) increases in Cl– and Ni were associated with a 3.48% (95% CI: 1.50%, 5.46%) increase in diastolic blood pressure and a 0.09% (95% CI: 0.05%, 0.12%) decrease in FEV1/FVC, respectively. Mediation analysis identified 212 cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites that regulated both cardiovascular and pulmonary dysfunctions, and 7 genes mediating more than two distinct constituent-function associations. Neurotransmission, metabolism, and cardiovascular function-related pathways were primarily enriched, among which 22 CpG sites (e.g., cg07115148, cg26409134, and cg26613778) were identified as key epigenetic mediators. Expression quantitative trait methylation analysis revealed that these CpG sites were associated with 14 protein-coding genes including CERS6 and LRCH3. Our findings suggest that short-term exposure to PM2.5 constituents triggers cardiopulmonary dysfunctions via DNA methylation-gene transcription axes and related disruption of neurotransmission, metabolism, and cardiovascular signaling pathways.

papers.title: Rethinking In-Cloud Aqueous-Phase Nitrogen Chemistry: High-Molecular-Weight Carbonyls as Major Counterparts to Low-Molecular-Weight Dicarbonyls
papers.abstract: Abstract Aqueous-phase reactions between carbonyls and reactive nitrogen species (e.g., ammonia/amine) are critical for forming secondary nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs) and brown carbon (BrC). However, current atmospheric chemical paradigms center almost exclusively on low-molecular-weight carbonyls such as glyoxal, leaving the role of high-molecular-weight carbonyls (HMWCs, with 4 ≤ C ≤ 30) unexplored. Here, we utilize advanced nontargeted molecular fingerprinting (PFBHA derivatization and FT-ICR MS) to unveil an unexpected and highly diverse pool of 1,242 unique carbonyl formulas in cloud water. These HMWCs, predominantly distributed in the C8–C20 range, exhibit a disproportionately high signal intensity (up to ∼35%) despite representing only a small fraction (5.4–13.9%) of the total signal diversity. Using a mechanistic “precursor-product pair” framework, we demonstrate that these HMWCs contribute to nearly one-third of the total NOC diversity (including various light-absorbing N-heterocycles) via Maillard-like reactions. This contribution is strikingly comparable to that of well-studied low-molecular-weight dicarbonyls, i.e., glyoxal and methylglyoxal. We further show that this HMWC-driven pathway covaries with precursor availability and cloud water pH. These findings suggest that incorporating HMWC-mediated NOC formation into future atmospheric models may improve the representation of secondary BrC formation and its associated climate effects.

papers.title: Non-Target Analytical Workflow for Gas-Phase Atmospheric Chemicals Collected on XAD Resin and Application to Passive Samplers
papers.abstract: Abstract The atmospheric gas phase is underrepresented in non-target screening of environmental organic chemicals, partly due to limited evidence on sorbent suitability. Here, we developed a workflow for non-target analysis (NTA) of styrene-divinylbenzene copolymeric (XAD) resin-based air samples that involves both gas (GC) and liquid chromatography (LC) high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). More than 60 000 features were detected in passive air samplers (PAS) deployed over 4–48 weeks. Of ∼34 000 features retained after blank filtration, ∼14 000 (41%) showed an increasing signal with deployment time, suggesting that they represent substances with volatility and degradability sufficiently low for accumulation on XAD without substantial re-evaporation or degradation during the prolonged sampling period. Such linear uptake is a prerequisite for comparing PAS-derived signals across deployments and chemical classes. Chemical identification by reference standards (level 1) and spectral library matching (level 2) initially identified/annotated 116 compounds, many of which were bioactive and/or brown carbon species. Combining advanced downstream computational workflows of feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) and in silico prediction (Network Annotation Propagation/MetFrag) allowed for the structural annotation (level 3) of >8300 LC-HRMS features, including several compounds of natural and anthropogenic origin which were not previously reported in the atmospheric gas phase. Several long-chain fatty acids showed rapid early increases implausible with atmospheric origins and are likely to originate from microbial growth on the resin. Overall, our results demonstrated that XAD is a sorbent compatible with comprehensive NTA and suitable for time-integrated passive sampling of a diverse range of gas-phase organic chemicals from the atmosphere.

papers.title: Peer-to-peer energy sharing and storage strategies for potential positive energy Districts: A case study of a purely commercial district
Remote sensing and artificial intelligence integration for seabed seagrass distribution and probabilistic seagrass biomass carbon potential
papers.abstract: The Seto Inland Sea (SIS), Japan's largest semi-enclosed coastal sea, hosts seagrass meadows that form an important and quantifiable reservoir of biomass-based carbon. Reliable mapping of these meadows is therefore essential for ecosystem assessment and coastal management. This study integrates a multiband depth-invariant bottom index (BI) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery with machine learning and deep learning classifiers to map seabed seagrass distribution and estimate the probabilistic seagrass biomass carbon potential of the inner SIS between 2019 and 2025. Sentinel-2 imagery was processed in Google Earth Engine, and Bands 2 (blue), 3 (green), and 4 (red) were combined into three BI configurations ( 𝐵 ⁢ 𝐼 2 − 3 , 𝐵 ⁢ 𝐼 3 − 4 , and 𝐵 ⁢ 𝐼 2 − 4 ). Of nine classifiers tested, Random Forest (RF) performed best, reaching 92.31% accuracy and 𝜅 = 0.81 under a single stratified split. More conservative validation across 50 repeated random splits gave 87.4 ± 9.5% accuracy and 𝜅 = 0.686 ± 0.225, while spatial leave-one-site-out (LOSO) validation gave 77.4% accuracy and 𝜅 = 0.50, indicating reduced transferability to unsurveyed sites. Among the three band-pair configurations, 𝐵 ⁢ 𝐼 2 − 3 was the dominant predictor (variable importance = 0.93). Building on this classification, seagrass biomass carbon potential was estimated by combining satellite-derived seagrass probabilities with field-based biomass distributions through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation. The resulting estimate reflects standing seagrass biomass carbon only, excluding sediment organic carbon, burial, decomposition, and lateral carbon export, and should be read as a biomass carbon potential rather than a total blue carbon stock. Monthly carbon potential followed a clear seasonal cycle, rising from winter into spring and peaking in May–June. Together, these results show that combining a multiband BI with artificial intelligence (AI)-based classification enables site-specific seagrass mapping and biomass-based carbon assessment in optically complex coastal waters, while underscoring the need for spatially independent validation before extrapolating beyond surveyed sites.

papers.title: Probabilistic health risk assessment and source-specific risk analysis of potentially toxic elements in metropolitan surface soils using PMF, geo-detector, and KDE-based Monte Carlo simulation
papers.abstract: Metropolitan soils are increasingly affected by multiple anthropogenic inputs, resulting in complex patterns of potentially toxic element (PTE) accumulation. However, the mechanisms linking pollution sources, spatial heterogeneity, and the resulting ecological and human health risks remain insufficiently understood. To clarify PTE contamination characteristics and associated risks, 1122 topsoil samples were obtained across the studied metropolitan region in southwestern China. The results revealed that all PTEs, except As and Cd, exceeded their local background values. Spatially, Hg, Pb, Cu, and Zn exhibited localized enrichment hotspots in the east-central urbanized areas. Combined APCS-MLR and PMF receptor models identified five potential sources, including natural background (25.54%), atmospheric deposition (15.13%), agricultural activities (18.64%), industrial manufacturing and urban emissions (19.14%), and mixed traffic–industrial sources (21.55%). PMF provided better model fit and spatial separation than APCS-MLR under the study conditions. Geo-detector analysis revealed that soil type and land use were the dominant factors controlling PTE spatial heterogeneity, with nonlinear interactions further enhancing their explanatory power. According to the potential ecological risk index, low to moderate ecological risk levels were identified in 83.07% of the samples. Hg and Cd were the major contributors to ecological risk, whereas atmospheric deposition represented the highest source-specific ecological risk contribution. Deterministic health risk assessment indicated higher risks for children, with 7.93% of samples exceeding the acceptable non-carcinogenic risk threshold. Carcinogenic risks were acceptable for both population groups. As was the dominant contributor to both carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic risks, and soil ingestion represented the major exposure route. KDE-optimized Monte Carlo simulation further showed that 9.47% of children may experience unacceptable non-carcinogenic risk, while accounting for the empirical distribution and uncertainty of exposure-related variables. Although the health risk assessment was based on total PTE concentrations without considering metal bioavailability, the proposed framework still provides a scientific basis for source-specific pollution control and risk-prioritized soil management in rapidly urbanizing metropolitan regions.

papers.title: NSF moves to overhaul funding approach in line with White House priorities
Sabotage as Industrial Policy
papers.abstract: Abstract We characterise sabotage, exemplified by recent US policies concerning China’s semiconductor industry, as trade policy. For some (but not all) goods, completely destroying foreigners’ productivity increases domestic real income by shifting the location of production and improving the terms of trade. The gross benefit of sabotage can be summarised by a few sufficient statistics: trade and demand elasticities and import and production shares. The cost of sabotage is determined by countries’ relative unit labour costs for the sabotaged goods. We find important non-monotonicities: for semiconductors, partially sabotaging foreign production would lower US real income, while comprehensive sabotage would raise it.

papers.title: Pushing the Boundaries: Studies on Consumers and Food Demand in the Journal of Agricultural Economics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We summarize the development of consumer economics and food demand in the Journal of Agricultural Economics over the past 100 years. Even from an early stage, the role of marketing agricultural products in a thriving agricultural sector was recognized within the works published in the Journal. Early papers focused on the demand for specific commodities and consumer trends more generally. Over time, analyses became more advanced, diving into the development of theory and methods for the estimation of demand systems. While this trend has continued, other topics have come to the forefront, such as consumer demand for food quality and safety, consumer acceptance of novel technologies, the demand for sustainable food products, and the role of nutrition and health in consumer studies. Methods were developed concurrently to address the new challenges that the agricultural sector faced, from secondary data analysis to primary data collection and experimental methods.

papers.title: Ancestral origins of democratic preferences: The role of state experience
Corporate contributions and political selection: Evidence from Brazil
Quantifying informational illiquidity in corporate bond markets
papers.abstract: We develop a structural credit-risk model to quantify the impact of information asymmetry on corporate bond pricing. In the model, bondholders (i) sell their bonds either to meet liquidity needs or to exploit informational advantages and (ii) have the option to credibly reveal their true trading motives to buyers at a cost. Our model generates qualitatively distinct patterns in the relationship between yield spreads and turnover rates across different levels of default risk. This feature enables us to match the observed cross-sectional relationship between these two variables more flexibly in calibration. The calibrated model indicates that information asymmetry accounts for 10.8%–20.5% of overall liquidity costs for investment-grade bonds and 30.1%–37.7% for speculative-grade bonds. The model also offers new policy insights into bond market liquidity.
papers.journal_name: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money

papers.title: The causal effect of agricultural landscape simplification on Germany's grasslands during a compound drought and heatwave in 2018
The Importance of Treatment Adherence and Long‐Term Outcomes in Health Economic Impact Evaluations
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wydick et al. recently estimated the impact of Ponseti clubfoot treatment on human flourishing in Ethiopia, providing important evidence for scaling clubfoot programs in low‐ and middle‐income countries. However, their definition of “treated” warrants scrutiny. Considering children in the final stages of casting as treated, only captures outcomes during the early stage of a 4‐year treatment course, implicitly assuming full bracing adherence and no relapse. This is inconsistent with relapse rates of 30%–40% and two‐year discontinuation rates exceeding 50% in comparable settings. This choice of definition likely underestimates late‐initiated treatment impact and overestimates early‐initiated treatment impact. Modeling the clubfoot care pathway as a probabilistic value model incorporating dropout, non‐adherence, and relapse, I re‐estimate population‐level functional outcomes at mid‐childhood. In settings without additional surgical care availability the mean level of functionality is estimated at 55.2% of normal function (95% CI 54.6%–55.9%), showing that enrollment expansion alone cannot achieve impact at the scale implied. Achieving clubfoot treatment's full potential at scale requires comprehensive, longitudinal care beyond initial Ponseti treatment, and stronger collaboration between clinical and health‐economics communities to ground future estimates in clinical reality.

papers.title: Who Pays the Most to Trade? Cross-client Dispersion in OTC Liquidity Prices
papers.abstract: Abstract This study analyzes the wide dispersion in bid-ask spreads across clients in over-the-counter (OTC) markets. Our data detailed data comprise a dealing bank's complete trading record in a major OTC contract and include client IDs, seven client types, and precise markups. Average spreads are lowest for hedge funds (<1 basis point, bp) and highest for individuals and for small and medium enterprises (>50 bps). Regression results suggest that the primary source of variation is clients’ execution efficiency, meaning their ability to minimize execution costs. Efficient trading, which can require investments in knowledge and technology, has three dimensions: reliance on low-cost platforms; familiarity with market technologies, conventions, and negotiating strategies; and breadth of dealing relationships. Relations between proxies for client execution efficiency and client incentives to invest, such as trade frequency, are consistent with rational inattention.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Governed Capability System for Sustainable Supply‐Chain Management: A Systematic Review, Taxonomy and Research Agenda
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to forecast demand, evaluate suppliers, optimise production and logistics and support sustainability reporting. Yet much of the literature treats AI as a collection of techniques rather than as a capability embedded in organisational and interorganisational systems. This systematic review synthesises 53 studies at the intersection of AI, supply‐chain management and sustainability‐related outcomes. It separates three analytical products: descriptive findings from the corpus, an abductive theory‐building interpretation and a normative governance extension. The descriptive synthesis identifies a concentration in planning and tactical decision support, with limited attention to delivery, returns, social sustainability, resilience and implemented governance. The theory‐building contribution conceptualises AI‐enabled sustainable supply‐chain management as a governed capability system in which data, models, decision routines, cross‐tier coordination and accountability arrangements jointly shape the conversion of analytical outputs into sustainability outcomes. A process‐mechanism taxonomy links Plan–Source–Make–Deliver–Return activities to sensing, prediction, optimisation and coordination mechanisms. A six‐layer governance architecture is then proposed as a theory‐informed and testable extension rather than as a causal finding of the review. The resulting research agenda focuses on absolute rather than merely relative sustainability gains, evidence provenance, supplier inclusion, labour and distributional effects, resilience trade‐offs and the assurance of generative AI–supported claims.

papers.title: Circular Economy Implementation: A Paradox–Dynamic Capabilities Perspective Under Institutional Pressures
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Why do firms facing similar sustainability pressures differ substantially in circular economy implementation? Existing research provides limited insight into how institutional pressures are internally interpreted and translated into organizational action. Drawing on institutional theory, paradox theory, and the dynamic capabilities perspective, this study develops and tests a multilevel model explaining how institutional pressures shape circular economy implementation through managerial cognition and organizational capabilities. Using survey data from 312 managers across European firms, the findings reveal that institutional pressures positively influence paradox mindset, dynamic capabilities, and circular economy implementation. However, paradox mindset does not directly translate into implementation; instead, its effect operates indirectly through dynamic capabilities. These findings suggest that institutional pressures alone do not explain variation in circular economy implementation across firms. The study advances a microfoundational and process‐oriented explanation of circular economy implementation and offers insights into how firms can strengthen the capabilities needed to translate sustainability pressures into operational change.

papers.title: Uncovering Social Implications of Circular Strategies in the Wine Industry: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The wine industry is increasingly adopting circular economy (CE) strategies to reduce resource intensity, valorise residues and create economic opportunities. Yet, the social dimension of sustainability remains largely overlooked, limiting the understanding of CE's full impact. This systematic literature review of 387 peer‐reviewed articles provides a novel perspective for wine business management, linking circular strategies to potential social implications along and beyond the wine value chain. Findings confirm that social implications are rarely addressed but reveal that CE can influence key social hotspots. The review also identifies major limitations—such as methodological constraints, inconsistent CE terminology and limited use of circularity metrics—that may hinder evaluation and strategic decision‐making. By systematically mapping valorisation pathways for wine by‐products, the study offers structured insights for managers and policymakers to design circular strategies that holistically consider social, environmental and economic effects.

papers.title: Misinterpretation of the ESG Controversies Index: A Critical Flaw in Sustainability Research—Evidence From a Hybrid Review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The ESG Controversies Index provided by Thomson Reuters (Refinitiv) has been widely used in sustainability, finance, and corporate governance research as a proxy for firms' exposure to environmental, social, and governance controversies. However, a number of published studies appear to misinterpret the index by reversing its underlying scale. Specifically, while a score of 100 indicates the absence of controversies and a score of 0 reflects the highest level of controversy exposure, several studies incorrectly assume the opposite interpretation. This methodological inconsistency has the potential to compromise the validity of empirical findings in affected studies. However, the actual consequences depend on the specific empirical context, and our review‐based approach identifies patterns of potential concern rather than demonstrating actual effects. While we cannot establish the magnitude of empirical distortion, our findings highlight the need for greater methodological awareness and transparency in ESG research. In response, this study investigates the extent and implications of the misinterpretation of the ESG Controversies Index through a hybrid review approach combining a systematic literature review and a bibliometric analysis. The study identifies patterns of incorrect index application across the literature, examines their diffusion within academic research, and evaluates the potential methodological and theoretical consequences for ESG scholarship. The findings highlight concerns regarding variable construction, database transparency, and research reliability in sustainability studies. By clarifying the correct interpretation of the ESG Controversies Index, this study contributes to improving methodological rigor, enhancing the credibility of ESG research, and strengthening the reliability of evidence‐based sustainable decision‐making.

papers.title: Mapping and Interrelationships of the Drivers of Sustainable Agricultural Practice Adoption Among Smallholder Rice Farmers: A Multi‐Criteria Decision‐Making Analysis for Climate Resilience
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rice production sustains food security and rural livelihoods across many low‐income countries but remains highly vulnerable to climate‐related hazards, including floods, droughts, salinity intrusion and heat stress, which reduce yields and threaten the long‐term sustainability of rice production. These growing pressures highlight the need for more sustainable and climate‐resilient production approaches. Sustainable agricultural practices (SAPs) represent one such approach to mitigating climate‐related impacts and strengthening the resilience of production systems. Despite their known potential, adoption among smallholder rice farmers remains limited, and the drivers of adoption and their interrelationships are still poorly understood and documented. Using Bangladesh as a case study, this study identified the key factors that influence smallholder farmers' adoption of SAPs, examined their interrelationships and developed policy insights for climate‐resilient rice production. Initially, 44 drivers were identified and validated through a literature review, Delphi process and KIIs. Subsequently, Total Interpretive Structural Modelling established a 17‐level hierarchy, while MICMAC analysis classified the drivers according to their driving and dependence powers. The findings identified four foundational drivers: climate and environmental pressures, NGO and development support, government and legislative backing and access to technology. These factors shaped resource and market access and, consequently, influenced behavioural and social determinants, including perceived behavioural control, subjective norms, social acceptance and farm efficiency. Overall, the study offers a prioritised roadmap for advancing climate‐resilient rice production in Bangladesh and comparable low‐income contexts.

papers.title: A Strategic Governance Perspective on Carbon Accounting Enablers: An In‐Depth Qualitative Examination of Business Strategies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study advances a governance perspective on how firms implement, adopt, and routinize carbon accounting. Although prior research has identified several carbon accounting drivers and enablers, less is known about how these elements interact at the firm level to support the organizational embedding of carbon accounting. Drawing on a qualitative analysis of essay‐based responses from 44 industry experts, this study identifies four interconnected dimensions of carbon accounting enablement, specifically carbon governance, structural sustenance, technological and operational transformation, and external persuasion. This study argues that external institutional pressures are important but insufficient to explain the organizational uptake of carbon accounting. Rather, these pressures become consequential when governance arrangements translate them into capabilities, routines, data infrastructures, and accountability mechanisms. The findings reveal that carbon accounting should not be treated just as a measurement or reporting practice but should be understood as a socio‐technical accountability infrastructure connecting emissions measurement, governance oversight, operational decision‐making, and stakeholder‐oriented legitimacy. The originality of this study lies in shifting attention from isolated enablers to the relational and iterative mechanisms through which carbon accounting is perceived to become embedded at the firm level under conditions of technological friction, supplier dependence, Scope 3 data uncertainty, and assurance pressure. This study contributes to theory by developing an interpretive framework of carbon accounting enablement, to practice by clarifying the governance and capability conditions required for routinization, and to policy by highlighting why regulatory pressure needs to be supported by organizational and assurance infrastructures.

papers.title: Beyond Compliance: Governance and Integrated Reporting as Strategic Systems for Corporate Sustainability
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Information asymmetry between firms and stakeholders remains a persistent challenge because conventional reporting systems often fail to capture the broader dimensions of value creation, while existing studies largely treat corporate governance as a one‐directional determinant of integrated reporting and overlook potential feedback mechanisms. This study addresses this limitation by examining whether corporate governance and integrated reporting operate as complementary mechanisms or as components of a dynamic causal system. Using a sample of 100 NSE‐listed firms in India over the period 2013–2025, the study investigates the simultaneous relationship between Integrated Reporting Alignment Score (IRAS) and key governance dimensions, including board size, board independence, women on board, board meeting frequency, audit committee size, and firm age. IRAS is constructed using content analysis based on the International Integrated Reporting Council framework. Methodologically, the study employs a panel vector auto‐regression (PVAR) model estimated through the generalized method of moments (GMM), enabling all variables to be treated as endogenous and allowing dynamic feedback effects and shock transmission to be captured. The findings reveal significant bidirectional relationships between governance mechanisms and integrated reporting. Board independence and board meetings significantly influence reporting quality, while integrated reporting also generates feedback effects on governance structures. Granger causality results confirm strong dynamic interdependencies, while variance decomposition analysis highlights moderate cross‐variable interactions and substantial own shock persistence. Cointegration findings further indicate a stable long‐run relationship among governance and reporting dimensions. The results suggest that corporate governance and integrated reporting evolve jointly as mutually reinforcing elements within an integrated organizational system.

papers.title: Executive‐Reported Organizational AI Implementation Intention: Evidence From Firms Without Recognized Routine AI Implementation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly considered in organizational decisions involving business processes, resource use, governance, and competitive positioning. This study examines executive‐reported organizational AI implementation intention among firms with no stable, continuous, and organizationally recognized routine AI implementation. This condition does not exclude pilot activity, sporadic experimentation, or informal use. The model includes nine first‐order antecedents drawn from technology acceptance, innovation diffusion, and research on trust, perceived costs, and anxiety. Survey data from 613 top executives in Spain and Portugal are analyzed using PLS‐SEM and necessary condition analysis. Permutation‐based path comparisons identify a between‐sample difference only for facilitating conditions. All seven positively framed antecedents show significant necessity effects in both samples. Cost frictions and AI anxiety are negatively associated with intention in both countries but are not necessary conditions. The study clarifies how established antecedents occupy different net association and necessity roles in executive‐reported organizational AI implementation intention. The findings illuminate a prospective organizational context relevant to sustainable digital transformation, without assessing realized implementation, governance practices, or sustainability outcomes.

papers.title: Beyond the Silos: A Systematic Review Mapping the Spectrum of Innovation in the Circular Economy From a Management Perspective
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The focus on the circular economy ( CE ) has grown recently as a regenerative alternative to the linear economic model, seeking to eliminate waste and enable resource efficiency. Innovation is widely recognized as central to enabling organizational CE transitions; however, the CE innovation literature remains fragmented, with different dimensions examined in isolation. Addressing this gap, this study systematically reviews the management literature on CE and innovation using the PRISMA protocol, complemented by bibliometric and qualitative content analyses. The review maps the intellectual structure of the field and develops an integrated framework that organizes CE innovation into five major categories. The findings show that CE transitions are enabled through multiple pathways, including business model innovation, ecoinnovation, product, process, supply chain, and digitally enabled innovations. A key insight is that Industry 4.0 technologies are emerging as a cross‐cutting driver across each category. The study contributes by moving beyond siloed investigation of CE innovation and providing a structured foundation for theory building and future empirical inquiry. Finally, this paper presents avenues for future research under each theme identified.

papers.title: Navigating blockchain assimilation in supply chain organisations: an integrated institutional and innovation assimilation perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how institutional pressures shape the adoption, assimilation and integration of blockchain technologies in supply chain organisations. By combining Gallivan’s innovation assimilation model with institutional theory, the paper explains why blockchain projects frequently stall or regress. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with blockchain vendors, adopters and ecosystem actors are triangulated with a systematic literature review to map institutional influences across assimilation stages. Findings The analysis identifies four institutional mechanisms; network legitimacy, coordinated uncertainty reduction, institutional paradoxes and cross-organisational cognitive reframing which collectively explain non-linear and uneven assimilation trajectories. Regulative, normative and cognitive pressures function as both enablers and constraints at different stages, particularly during routinisation and infusion. Practical implications The findings provide managers and policymakers with guidance on reducing institutional friction, aligning incentives across supply chain tiers and supporting stable governance and assurance structures required for sustained blockchain integration. Originality/value The study advances supply chain management research by showing how multi-tier governance, power asymmetries and certification regimes shape blockchain assimilation. It offers a multi-level explanation for why blockchain rarely progresses beyond early pilots into embedded, long term practice.
papers.journal_name: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal

papers.title: How non-market collaboration shapes stakeholders' wellbeing through climate-risk management strategies in emerging market B2B firms?
papers.abstract: Climate change poses threats to stakeholders' wellbeing, defined as their satisfaction, value realisation, expectations, and retention with the firm. While research has established that enhancing stakeholders' wellbeing requires cross-sector collaboration, industrial marketing scholarship has paid less attention to the challenges faced by resource-constrained firms in emerging markets that often rely on non-market collaborations with government and regulatory bodies to access critical resources and knowledge. Using a survey of firms ( n = 142) in Pakistan, which is among the most vulnerable country to climate-change risks, this study shows that non-market collaboration with government agencies promotes stakeholders' wellbeing through a serial mediation of climate-risk management strategies and value co-creation with value-chain (upstream and downstream) partners. Furthermore, the influence of non-market collaboration with climate-risk management strategies is more pronounced under high shareholder pressure. Also, the effects of climate-risk management strategies on value co-creation are strengthened by collaborative communication with value-chain partners. Extending industrial marketing literature that cross-sector partnerships are critical for value co-creation, these findings specifically underscore the importance of non-market collaboration in emerging markets, and demonstrate that multi-stakeholder collaborations facilitate sustainable value-chains, thereby generating positive stakeholders' wellbeing.

papers.title: One size does not fit all: Why do some new ventures benefit from participating in accelerators more than others?
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates why some new ventures derive greater benefits from participation in accelerator programs than others. Specifically, we examine how differences in pre-entry core product knowledge shape ventures’ ability to leverage accelerator-based structured learning and mentoring, and how these mechanisms jointly influence venture performance at program graduation (Demo Day) and survival up to 2 years later. We conceptualize learning from the accelerator’s structured program through the lens of absorptive capacity (ACAP), encompassing knowledge acquisition, assimilation, transformation, and exploitation. Additionally, we examine mentoring effects through the intensity of mentor–venture interactions and ventures’ intentional pivoting in response to mentors’ feedback. The analysis draws on a longitudinal dataset of 90 early-stage ventures across 11 cohorts within a single entrepreneurial ecosystem, with data collected at four stages: program entry, midpoint, graduation, and 2-year post-graduation. The findings show that pre-entry core product knowledge strongly predicts both Demo Day graduation performance and short-term survival. However, new ventures with lower initial product knowledge benefit more from a cohort-based, structured learning program, indicating that the learning gained in the accelerator can compensate for limited prior expertise. Moreover, mentoring intensity enhances outcomes only when ventures translate mentors’ advice into intentional pivoting. By integrating initial knowledge endowments, accelerator-based learning, and mentoring dynamics, this study advances accelerator research by highlighting the boundary conditions under which accelerators create value and by identifying pivoting as a key mechanism by which mentoring influences venture performance and short-term survival.

papers.title: Innovative entrepreneurial entry over the business cycle: variation by form of innovation and country economic development
papers.abstract: Abstract While prior studies indicate innovation and product introductions decrease during economic downturns and recessions, the nature of innovative entry by startups is unclear. Furthermore, studies of business entry, which is dominated by non-innovative firms, show mixed results. We build on innovation theories to propose that likelihood of entry varies with business cycle fluctuations, following an inverted U-shape relationship with startup innovativeness and with related contextual variations by level of economic development. Using GEM data to study entrepreneurial entry in 66 countries between 2003 and 2018—evaluating both the recovery from the dot.com crash and Global Financial Crisis—we find evidence supporting our proposed counter-cyclic disruption mechanism for discontinuously innovative entry, pro-cyclic prosperity pull mechanism for incrementally innovative entry, and counter-cyclic recession push mechanism for imitative entry, together with contextual variations with economic development.

papers.title: Language and frames of a reified world: how university actors turn teaching into a number
papers.abstract: The paper adopts the lenses of reification (the objectification of reality in relation to the way things are perceived and structured at the individual level) and framing theory to explore, at different levels, actors' understanding of performance-measurement systems relating to the quality of teaching within the university sector. Individual reification can be seen as the result of a wider process of social alienation, which explores the inherent dangers of commodifying subjects. In a university setting, this potentially encourages individual striving over collegiality and teamwork. The research draws on comparative case studies of four English universities, document analysis and interviews with government officials. The linguistic framing tasks used at the individual level provide evidence of reification and contribute to reinforce it via the deployment of arguments providing reasons for action/inaction (motivational frames) based on efficacy, and through the use of diagnostic and prognostic frames that articulate concepts only within the prevailing ideology. It is suggested that this can decrease the possibility of contestation (de-reification) at the level of individual responses. The paper contributes to our understanding of current theory and literature by exploring the use of individuals' linguistic framing tasks as cues for reification. It voices significant apprehension about the dysfunctional (and likely mission-damaging) effects of extant (reifying) university teaching measurement systems and calls for a more-cautious approach and more critical reflections of current practices that, arguably, appear to have led the sector to the uncritical acceptance of highly-questionable neoliberal tools and ideas.

papers.title: Stock mispricing and myopic marketing management
papers.abstract: We examine whether stock mispricing affects firms’ likelihood of adopting myopic marketing management. Drawing on myopic marketing management theory (Mizik, 2010), we argue that when stock prices deviate from fundamentals, managers adjust marketing and R&D expenditures in response. Using 34,302 firm-year observations from 1980 to 2016, we find an asymmetric effect where overpricing decreases the likelihood of myopic marketing management more than underpricing increases it. Equity issuance weakens this relationship, whereas firm growth strengthens it. Our research extends myopic marketing management theory by showing that the direction of mispricing changes managers’ incentives to maintain or reduce short- and long-term marketing expenditures. The findings also provide guidance for CMOs and CFOs. Marketing responses to stock mispricing should account for whether the firm is overpriced or underpriced, as well as its equity issuance and growth.

papers.title: Reconciling innovation and sustainability through the Triple Helix Twins: A coopetition perspective
papers.abstract: This study examines how knowledge spills over in innovation ecosystems to reconcile innovation and sustainability objectives through coopetition in the Triple Helix Twins (THT) model. Building on the knowledge spillovers, THT, and coopetition literatures, the paper investigates how industry, university, government, and public actors (U-I-G-P) strategically align their objectives, resources, and constraints through coopetitive mechanisms in complex products and systems industries. Adopting a systematic combining protocol, the study focuses on the French aerospace and energy industries through 27 semi-structured interviews complemented by secondary data from informants' organizations and industries. The findings show that knowledge spillovers in the THT model are implicitly oriented by coopetition along three interrelated mechanisms: a strategic alignment triptych, a continuous control feedback loop of knowledge, and conditional sharing shaped by strategic behaviors and path-dependency. These mechanisms determine how knowledge spills over between the U-I-G and the U-P-G helix, under which constraints, and with what consequences for sustainability alignment. A central insight is that limited public integration and selective spillovers from U-I-G to U-P-G may contribute to more fragmented forms of participation and to the emergence of more polarized narratives in ecosystem governance. Indeed, this paper demonstrates that knowledge does not circulates uniformly into an undifferentiated environment; rather, it spills over the two helices of the THT through coopetition mechanisms shaping the multi-level governance of innovation ecosystems. Managerially, it calls for more inclusive and differentiated public engagement to improve knowledge circulation, reduce greenwashing risks, and improve public debate's quality in complex products and systems industries.

papers.title: Eroding operations while elevating innovation: a dual-mechanism model of supplier list disclosure
papers.abstract: Purpose Supplier list disclosure has become a defining feature of contemporary supply chain transparency, yet leading firms exhibit strikingly divergent disclosure choices and the empirical literature reports both benefits and costs. Drawing on the relational view and signaling theory, we develop and test a dual-mechanism framework explaining how proactive supplier list disclosure simultaneously erodes operational performance while enhancing innovation performance, and identify the conditions that amplify each effect. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from Chinese listed firms from 2012 to 2024, we empirically test the relationships between supplier list disclosure and firms' operational and innovation performance. To validate the relational mechanism underlying disclosure's impact on operational performance, we test the moderating roles of supplier concentration and buyer competition. To validate the signaling mechanism underlying disclosure's impact on innovation performance, we test the moderating roles of media coverage and CSR performance. Findings The results suggest supplier list disclosure undermines firms' operational performance but enhances their innovation performance. The negative operational effect is amplified by higher supplier concentration and greater buyer competition, as these conditions increase the criticality and vulnerability of disclosed relational assets. The positive innovation effect is amplified by stronger media coverage and better CSR performance, which improve the visibility and credibility of the disclosure signal. These results are robust across alternative measures, model specifications, and identification strategies. Originality/value Our findings reconcile the longstanding tension between the documented benefits and costs of supply chain transparency by revealing the divergent performance consequences of supplier list disclosure. This study further contributes to the supply chain transparency and buyer-supplier governance literature by identifying key boundary conditions, thereby offering actionable guidance for designing optimal supplier list disclosure strategies.
