There were no significant differences in other sibship characteristics between sexual minority and heterosexual individuals, although other non-heterosexual study groups showed a non-significant FBOE of a magnitude similar to bisexual men. This study contributes to the limited literature on understudied bisexual and asexual populations and indicates that male bisexuality might share a common biodevelopmental origin with male and possibly also female homosexuality.

papers.title: Reform for all? The limits of expertise in producing equitable outcomes
papers.abstract: Administrative reforms often seek to improve performance by changing bureaucratic or professional expertise. Yet technical skills alone may not disrupt the forces that generate unequal outcomes across social groups. We argue that systemic bias shapes professionalization and discretionary judgment, limiting expertise-substitution reforms’ capacity to reduce racial disparities even when they improve average outcomes. We test this using a 2018 Dallas reform that deployed co-response teams pairing police officers with clinicians and social workers on mental health calls. A difference-in-­differences analysis across divisions finds significant reductions in psychiatric holds and arrests, but the gains concentrate among White male citizens; arrests of Black males increase significantly. A complementary incident-level analysis of the conditional probability of a coercive outcome points to a different pattern of heterogeneous effects: White males show a higher post-reform probability of psychiatric holds while Black females and Hispanic males experience lower ones. Both sets of findings shed new light on the scholarship of administrative reform and hold practical implications for both the impact of such programs and the ways in which they are evaluated.

papers.title: Socially oriented contracting and public employees’ job satisfaction: evidence from the federal small disadvantaged business program
papers.abstract: While contracting out is often viewed as having negative consequences for public employees, less attention has been paid to the positive outcomes certain types of contracting may have for them. In particular, recent scholarship proposes that contracting out may improve employees’ work attitudes when it emphasizes pro-social factors in the process. Using the case of the federal Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) contracting program—which emphasizes diversity and equity in procurement—this study examines whether contracting programs that promote social outcomes are associated with public employees’ job satisfaction. Drawing from research on sector differences, person-organization fit, and representative bureaucracy, we hypothesize a positive association between SDB contracting efforts and job satisfaction, with employees from underrepresented backgrounds experiencing a more pronounced increase. Linking U.S. federal government contracting data to the Federal Employee Viewpoint Survey (FEVS), our analyses provide support for the hypotheses. The implications of these findings for government contracting and public human resource management are discussed.

papers.title: Arrested development: how performance regimes constrain changes to public sector performance measurement
papers.abstract: Public sector organizations increasingly operate within broader performance regimes—the wider systems of rules, actors, and practices that shape how performance is measured and managed—yet little research has examined how these regimes enable or block attempts of public sector organizations to redesign their performance measurement (PM) systems. This study addresses that gap by developing an analytical framework built around the concept of lock-in mechanisms, which provides a structured way to identify regulatory, material, behavioral and discursive barriers to the redesign of public sector PM. This framework is then applied to the performance regime governing Danish employment services, where municipal job centers are actively trying to redesign their PM systems to better reflect client experiences and value creation. Our findings reveal that redesign efforts are constrained by lock-in mechanisms operating at three distinct levels: within the institutional context, mechanisms entrench upward accountability as the dominant purpose of PM; at the level of performance actors, mechanisms preserve rigid boundaries between those who are measured and those who do the measuring; and at the level of performance interventions, mechanisms sustain top-down uses of performance information, limiting more bottom-up approaches.

papers.title: Revisiting the venerable debate on strategy content and public service performance
Differentiating distributed leadership: introducing distributed professional development leadership and its motivational consequences
papers.abstract: Traditional hierarchical approaches to governing and leading public professionals have not always proven successful, and integrative and hybrid perspectives on professionalism are therefore receiving increasing attention. This study integrates professional development leadership (PDL) and distributed leadership (DL) theory and introduces the concept of distributed professional development leadership (D-PDL). D-PDL implies that employees without formal leadership responsibilities are engaged in core PDL activities focused on facilitating and realizing a shared understanding of professionalism within the scope of organizational goals. The study theorizes that professionals’ engagement in D-PDL leads to more autonomous motivation than engagement in generic DL, which covers a broad range of leadership activities that are disconnected from the professional core task. Survey data from approximately 2,400 Danish medical doctors support the theoretical framework and show that doctors’ engagement in D-PDL is associated with more intrinsic motivation and public service motivation, whereas their engagement in generic DL is primarily associated with extrinsic motivation. The study emphasizes the relevance of moving PDL beyond a leader-centric concept and of distinguishing between different types of DL activities.

papers.title: Elites by design? How organisational structures shape assignment concentration in local government
papers.abstract: Local government is often celebrated as democracy’s training ground, yet political authority at this level can be far more concentrated than democratic ideals suggest. This article examines how political offices accumulate among a few individuals in Swedish municipalities – a critical case given Sweden’s strong democratic norms and exceptional decentralisation. If oligarchic tendencies emerge here, they are likely to appear anywhere. Using original data from 27 strategically sampled municipalities, we map political assignments across councils, committees, and municipally owned corporations, and introduce a novel measure of ‘assignment inequality’ that captures top-heaviness in local power structures. Our findings challenge the widespread assumption that elite concentration primarily results from small scale or limited recruitment pools. Instead, institutional design – particularly corporatisation – proves decisive. Municipalities with extensive corporate networks exhibit systematically higher concentration and more skewed distributions of political authority. Local elites, we conclude, emerge by design, not default.

papers.title: Interpretable and uncertainty-quantified early remaining useful life prediction for lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols
papers.abstract: Under fast-charging protocols, accurately and interpretably predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries during the initial cycling stage is of great significance for early fault warning and reliability assessment. To improve the interpretability of RUL prediction, this paper proposes a causal learning approach to conduct causal analysis on domain-specific features, identifying key causal variables and systematically uncovering their relationships with RUL. To enhance the model’s capacity to fit complex nonlinear relationships and generalize across various conditions, we propose a neural network based on Legendre polynomial orthogonal bases, termed LegendreNet. Its approximation ability and theoretical validity are rigorously demonstrated. The causally selected domain features are fed into LegendreNet for prediction. In parallel, the original features are fed into a causal convolutional neural network (CCNN) to extract deep representations, capturing both global spatiotemporal dependencies and local feature details. The outputs of LegendreNet and CCNN are then concatenated and fused via LegendreNet to generate the final RUL prediction. Based on this architecture, we propose a novel multimodal prediction framework for early RUL estimation of lithium-ion batteries, named LNCCNN. Finally, to adaptively adjust the bandwidth and quantify predictive uncertainty, we introduce curvature adjustment into the Bayesian bootstrap kernel density estimation (BB-KDE) framework and propose a novel method, called curvature-aware BB-KDE (CA-BB-KDE). Experimental results on two distinct batches from the same fast-charging dataset demonstrate improved early RUL prediction accuracy, reducing RMSE by 2.96% and 7.09% and MAPE by 1.32% and 8.16%, respectively, supporting lifetime monitoring and decision-making in battery management systems.

papers.title: From electrode scaffold to hydrogen-system value: a reverse-boundary qualification framework for direct seawater electrolysis
Semantic-aware robust PV forecasting based on a localized enhanced LLM framework
papers.abstract: High-quality photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is crucial for the operation of modern power systems. However, conventional methods rely heavily on extensive historical data, leading to a significant decline in forecasting accuracy in data-scarce scenarios such as newly built plants or extreme weather conditions. To compensate for this lack of numerical data, incorporating supplementary textual and semantic information offers a promising approach. Current PV forecasting methods have yet to fully exploit the potential of this approach. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong generalization in time-series forecasting. Furthermore, their multimodal reasoning abilities present an opportunity to bridge the inherent gap between numerical data and natural language. Motivated by these insights, we propose a localized enhanced LLM framework for robust day-ahead PV forecasting. By incorporating a semantic self-expansion mechanism and specialized embedders into a fine-tuning architecture, the framework fuses time-series data with textual information, allowing the LLM to adaptively capture forecasting-relevant features, which effectively mitigates the accuracy decline caused by data scarcity. Empirical evaluations across geographically distinct regions in China demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models like Autoformer, PatchTST, GPT4TS, and Time-LLM, highlighting the learning capabilities and robustness of our method under data scarcity.

papers.title: Modeling multicycle anodic degradation in hard carbon-based sodium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Due to abundant raw materials and ecological friendliness, sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are considered a promising alternative to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) for energy storage applications. This assertion is based on the recent advances in technology and the proven capabilities of SIBs. Physics-based modeling (PBM) is a cost-effective approach for understanding the electrochemical kinetics and degradation mechanisms of batteries. In this paper, the authors developed a single-particle model with electrolyte interactions (SPMe) coupled with anodic degradation in a sodium vanadium phosphate fluoride (NVPF)/Hard carbon cell. Stress generation due to intercalation, adsorption, and pore-filling is considered. Degradation due to sodium plating/stripping with dead sodium storage, solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth/fracture, and loss of active material is simulated at a 1C charging rate over 300 cycles. The developed model is shown to be reliable for predicting capacity degradation and discharge profiles. The model provides insight into the suppression of SEI and dead sodium, and their effects on resistance during battery aging. The results show the role of initial SEI thickness variation (1 nm–20 nm) across different levels of dead sodium storage (1%–5%). Ultimately, the capacity degradation is assessed for the simulated cell. The proposed model can serve as a reference for the design of SIBs.

papers.title: Loss visibility versus spatial detail in industrial district-heating dispatch optimisation
Machine learning-accelerated discovery and optimization of thermoelectric materials for energy conversion
papers.abstract: Recently, machine learning (ML) has received growing attention as a powerful tool for accelerating the discovery and optimization of thermoelectric materials. By utilizing large-scale datasets generated from high-throughput calculations and experimental measurements, ML models are able to efficiently predict key properties, identify promising candidates, and guide material design. Herein we summarize the latest progress in this rapidly evolving field and present a comprehensive overview on typical ML workflows, key algorithms and efficient models for predicting thermoelectric properties, including both indirect and direct predictions of electrical and thermal transport characteristics. Subsequently, we discuss how ML facilitates the discovery of novel thermoelectric materials and supports the optimization of composition, synthesis processes, and microstructures. Finally, we explore current challenges and future opportunities for integrating ML into thermoelectric investigation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of ML applications in thermoelectrics, thereby highlighting their potential to accelerate thermoelectric materials development for energy conversion and waste-heat recovery applications.

papers.title: Bridging the environmental and economic gaps: operation reality and sustainability of real-world green hydrogen plants
Advances in microwave-assisted catalytic and plasma conversion of methane: A comprehensive review
papers.abstract: Microwave-assisted methane (CH 4 ) conversion offers a transformative pathway for hydrogen and syngas production. This review systematically examines microwave catalysis and microwave plasma technologies across four key routes: methane pyrolysis (MP), dry reforming (DRM), steam reforming (SMR), and partial oxidation (POM). Microwave irradiation reduces activation energy by up to 45% for MP (from 45.5 to 24.8 kJ/mol) and 29% for DRM (from 90.8 to 64.2 kJ/mol for CH 4 ), while enabling 250 °C lower operating temperatures compared to conventional heating. Microwave plasma achieves CH 4 conversion >90% at near-ambient bulk temperatures, and variable-frequency microwave enables in-situ catalyst reactivation for stable operation >1300 min. Despite these advantages, most microwave-assisted systems remain at TRL 3–7, with key challenges including non-uniform heating, catalyst deactivation, and scale-up. By critically comparing thermal vs. non-thermal effects and microwave catalysis vs. plasma, this review identifies research priorities: microwave-specific catalyst design, reactor engineering for uniform field distribution, and integration with renewable electricity. This work provides a quantitative foundation for advancing microwave-assisted methane conversion from laboratory discovery toward industrial deployment.

papers.title: Plant-derived green nanomaterials: From biosynthesis to biocompatible applications in sustainable agriculture
papers.abstract: Traditional nanotechnology, relying on chemical reagents, generating ecological residues, and showing limited compatibility with plant physiology, faces challenges in meeting the requirements of green and sustainable agriculture. Plant-derived green nanomaterials have therefore emerged as an environmentally friendly alternative. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in their synthesis, focusing on three strategies: plant extract-mediated reduction, agricultural waste-templated synthesis, and plant metabolism-guided in situ synthesis. The differences in plant species, tissues, and metabolic components can influence the formation and regulation of nanomaterials, while plant-derived components participate in reduction, nucleation, growth, and stabilization, contributing to the formation of plant-derived interfacial structures. A multidimensional characterization framework tailored to plant systems is proposed, integrating indicators and methodologies for structural evaluation and biosafety assessment. The mechanisms underlying their roles in seed germination regulation, precise nutrient delivery, and the enhancement of plant stress resistance are systematically categorized and discussed. The ecological implications of their environmental transformation, persistence, and biocompatibility are discussed. Future directions focus on artificial intelligence, value‑added agricultural waste utilization, and full life‑cycle performance evaluation. Overall, this review provides theoretical and practical guidance for advancing plant‑derived green nanotechnology toward sustainable agriculture, food security, and ecological security.

papers.title: Quantifying Spatially Dynamic Transportation Carbon Footprint of New Energy Batteries: The GIS-LCA Based Interpretable Approach
papers.abstract: Abstract This study focuses on the transportation-driven spatial characteristics and dynamics, carbon footprint (CF), and environmental impact of new energy batteries from material acquisition to manufacturing. Based on the life cycle assessment (LCA) method, transportation data are obtained through the GIS-LCA platform to construct a quantification framework for analyzing the railway transportation CF of lithium-ion, solid-state (Li-FeS2, LLZO, LiPON), and hydrogen fuel cells (HFCs). Within a cradle-to-grave life cycle framework, transportation CF varies across battery technologies. NMC batteries show comparatively higher transport-related CF (0.512 kgCO2 eq), while HFC systems show lower values (0.00973 kgCO2 eq), primarily driven by raw material type, transportation distance, and the spatial distribution of production bases. The transportation CF accounts for less than 10% of the production phase, but its path spatial dynamics and regional logistics network differences lead to significant carbon emission (CE) distribution variations, such as PVC transportation CEs in the Shanghai base being over 95% lower than those in Beijing. The study provides scientific support for low-carbon technology pathway selection, supply chain layout optimization, and regional collaborative emission reduction in the battery industry. These findings support localized sourcing and spatially optimized supply chains to reduce the level of transportation emissions.

papers.title: Controlled Ion Dehydration-Driven Catalysis Enabled by Reverse-Mode Nanofiltration
papers.abstract: Abstract Catalysis under nanoscale confinement is widely pursued, but practical systems remain limited by a persistent contradiction: maximizing confinement-enhanced reactivity usually increases the residence time and accelerates pore failure. Here we present a ceramic nanofiltration platform that resolves this trade-off by coupling subnanometer confinement with transient, flow-through ion dehydration. The membrane is constructed by atomic layer deposition on a hierarchical α-Al2O3/γ-Al2O3 scaffold, yielding a robust, ultrathin Al2O3 active layer with tunable nanochannels and minimized transport distance to the reaction interface. During transmembrane permeation, Fe2+ ions are partially dehydrated, exposing vacant coordination sites that immediately react with H2O2 upon emergence to degrade organic micropollutants (e.g., tetracycline). This synergistic process yields a kinetic enhancement ratio of 90.5% for the dehydration group relative to the corresponding rehydration group. The kinetic enhancement ratio obtained with the commercial polyamide nanofiltration membrane NF270 under the same comparison framework was substantially lower. Beyond activity, the inorganic architecture sustains 30 d of continuous backwashing with <3% fluctuation in pure-water permeability and exhibits a kinetic enhancement ratio of 89.6% after backwashing. Importantly, the reverse-mode configuration reduces reliance on prolonged reactant residence within nanopores, thereby lowering the risk of pore blockage. These results establish a membrane-enabled strategy for capturing nonequilibrium ionic states and thereby translate nanoconfinement chemistry into an operationally durable format, with broad implications for water treatment, electrochemical conversion, and selective resource recovery.

papers.title: MiRA: A Multi-Receptive Integration Framework for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Pathways in AOPs─A Case Study of UV and Far-UV Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of pollutant transformation pathways in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) is critical for precise treatment design. However, conventional models inadequately capture global dependencies and key local reaction information, limiting reliable inference of complex multistep pathways. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces the multireceptive integration for reaction-pathway analysis (MiRA) framework. For the first time, it integrates “multi-receptive field chemical semantic capture + learnable fusion decision-making” into AOPdegradation pathway prediction. This enables the collaborative expression of local reaction sites, neighborhood structures, and global conditional dependencies within a single model, yielding information-rich feature representations with superior generalization capabilities. Using ultraviolet (UV) and far-ultraviolet (far-UV) data sets, MiRA framework achieves accuracies of 88.03% and 85.44%, respectively, with BLEU scores of 0.9459 and 0.9325, and Tanimoto similarity scores of 0.9405 and 0.9296, demonstrating robust predictive precision. Attention visualizations reveal that the framework automatically identifies key reaction features of substrates, demonstrating a degree of expert-level chemical reasoning capability. Additionally, an integrated toxicity estimation module provides relative screening of the toxicity potentials of transformation products. Overall, this study provides an intelligent analytical method for predicting pollutant transformation pathways and screening the toxicity potentials of transformation products in AOPs. It offers new methodological support for the precise design of AOPs.

papers.title: Metal–Organic Frameworks with Tunable Metal Node for Selective Capture and Separation of CO2 and CO from Ternary Blast Furnace Gas Mixtures
papers.abstract: Abstract The simultaneous capture of carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO) from complex industrial gases represents a critical challenge. Designing framework sorbents that combine selective molecular recognition with stability is essential. Herein, a series of anthracene-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), M-ABHBs (M = Co, Mg, Mn, and Ni), were successfully synthesized. By regulating metal centers, which leads to different interactions between gases (CO2/CO/N2) and metal–ligand pairs in the framework, excellent CO adsorption selectivity has been discovered. Notably, Mg/Mn-ABHBs allow efficient binary CO2/N2 separation, and Co/Ni-ABHBs enable benchmark ternary CO2/CO/N2 separation by increasing the adsorption affinity toward CO. This unique phenomenon is rare among adsorbents. Such behaviors enable a stepwise separation strategy to selectively capture CO2 and CO from ternary mixtures. Co-ABHB exhibits high selectivity of CO/N2 (13.1), while Mg-ABHB shows high selectivity of CO2/N2 (66.6) and CO2/CO (5.8). In situ DRIFTS and theoretical calculations indicate that the former is the result of the strong interactions of Co-CO in the cavities of Co-ABHB, while Mg sites strongly capture only CO2, not CO. Breakthrough tests show that from a CO2/CO/N2 mixture, M-ABHBs demonstrated excellent separation performance. This work offers a design strategy for efficient carbon capture under complex industrial gas conditions.

papers.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
A two-condenser DHW heat pump for flexible heating: Assessing carbon savings using hourly grid emissions
papers.abstract: Current building decarbonization policies often prioritize on-site renewable energy generation, an approach that is frequently unfeasible for block residential buildings with limited space for photovoltaic (PV) installations, as it is the case of many buildings in Spain. As national electricity grids become increasingly renewable, utilizing hourly grid CO 2 emission profiles rather than annual average provides more realistic results. In 2024, annual average CO 2 emissions in the Spanish grid was 0.096 kg CO 2 /kWh, while hourly CO 2 emission factors calculated month by month ranged from 0.047 kg CO 2 /kWh to 0.180 kg CO 2 /kWh. This article presents an innovative heat pump with two condensers that improves its COP and controls usage times in order to reduce CO 2 emissions associated with consumption. This new design is a solution that allows to pursue the flexibility of the systems, one of the key points of European regulations. Then the performance of the unit with two condensers is compared to a conventional one-condenser unit, results show that while standard annual-average assessments estimate a CO 2 emission reduction of up to 18%, applying an hourly evaluation reveals CO 2 emission savings exceeding 35%. This work highlights the problems with the current evaluation of heat pumps and the need to evaluate their associated CO 2 emissions more accurately, either through the use of electricity obtained from the grid or even by the use of on-site photovoltaic panels.

papers.title: Enhancing rapid removal of iron from recycled aluminium based on reducing interfacial mass transfer resistance by an immersion rotational segregation process
papers.abstract: Recycling of aluminum scrap is a crucial pathway for carbon reduction in the aluminum industry, as its carbon emissions represent only 3%-5% of those from primary aluminum production. However, a great challenge is to further remove trace iron content to a certain range in order to meet the requirements of multi grade high-end aluminum alloys. Herein, a novel immersion rotational segregation process (IRSP) is proposed to remove trace iron content in short time, which effectively reduces interfacial mass transfer resistance due to boundary layer thinning. Kilogram-scale experiments show that a single-stage process achieves a 60% iron removal efficiency within 3 min. By employing a two-stage treatment, the Fe content is successfully reduced from 0.8 wt% to below 0.15 wt%, meeting the stringent purity standards for high-quality aluminum alloy raw materials. This rapid purification is driven by intense shear forces that induce complex fluid interactions within high-speed shear zone and vortex zones, compressing the concentration boundary layer to 0.31 mm and significantly reducing interfacial mass transfer resistance. Furthermore, 100-kg scale-up experiments were performed to validate the industrial viability of the process, achieving an iron removal efficiency exceeding 70% within 20 min. This method provides a efficient pathway for the high-value upcycling of aluminium scrap, significantly reducing reliance on primary aluminum consumption and contributing to substantial carbon emission reductions in the global aluminum industry.

papers.title: Data-driven predictive control for combined-cycle gas turbines by multi-agent reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Fast and reliable load following is increasingly required as variable wind and photovoltaic generation expand. Combined-cycle gas turbines (CCGTs) are widely adopted to provide this flexibility. In a “2+1” CCGT, two gas turbines (GTs) are directly actuated, whereas the shared steam turbine (ST) contributes delayed power through heat-recovery and steam-cycle dynamics. A hierarchical framework combining improved model-free adaptive predictive control (IMFAPC), an extended state observer (ESO), and multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO), termed MAPPO-IMFAPC-ESO, is developed. A data-driven digital twin is formed from dynamic GT surrogates and a history-dependent ST model. Deterministic nominal commands are generated by ESO-enhanced IMFAPC (ESO-IMFAPC). Scaled and bounded residual corrections are allocated by MAPPO from local GT observations and the shared gross-generation error. Under a uniform contraction condition and bounded aggregate remainders, a conditional uniform ultimate boundedness estimate is derived for the exact-solve baseline. The fixed-policy implementation is characterized by conditional input-to-state practical stability under bounded deployment perturbations. Chronological leave-one-dataset-out validation confirms high one-step predictive accuracy of the ST model, with an RMSE of 1.920 MW and R 2 = 0.9874 , while held-out recursive command-replay tests reveal appreciable long-horizon error accumulation in the coupled GT–ST surrogate. Accordingly, the closed-loop results are interpreted as relative controller comparisons within a common learned digital-twin environment. Across five independently trained MAPPO-IMFAPC-ESO policies, the staircase gross-generation RMSE is 0.919 ± 0.014 MW, demonstrating repeatable sub-MW tracking, and a separate 24-hour evaluation shows no progressive growth of tracking error. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed hierarchical framework provides a unified data-driven approach for coordinating fast GT actuation with delayed ST response, while preserving deterministic predictive regulation and introducing bounded multi-agent residual coordination for CCGT load following.

papers.title: Does low-carbon policy improve the environmental performance in China?
papers.abstract: This study examines the impacts and driving mechanisms of low-carbon policy on environmental performance, with a focus on both direct policy effects and the underlying structural drivers. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions and years, the analysis employs a combination of econometric modeling and configurational approaches to capture heterogeneous and non-linear relationships. The results indicate that low-carbon policy significantly improves environmental performance, particularly in terms of emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and pollution control. However, the magnitude and direction of these effects vary across regions depending on differences in economic development, industrial structure, and governance capacity. Further analysis reveals that technological innovation, green investment, regulatory intensity, and public participation are key driving factors that jointly shape policy effectiveness. The study also identifies multiple pathways through which these factors interact to enhance environmental outcomes, highlighting the importance of synergistic policy design. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how low-carbon goals translate into measurable environmental improvements and offer practical implications for policymakers seeking to optimize policy implementation in diverse socio-economic contexts.

papers.title: Spatial associations with estimated net migration in Osaka, 2015–2020: A grid-level machine learning approach
papers.abstract: As Japan faces rapid depopulation, distinguishing net migration from natural population changes is important for understanding local population dynamics at fine spatial scales. This study proposes a data-driven framework to identify factors associated with census-derived estimates of net migration in Osaka Prefecture at a high-resolution 500 m grid level over the period 2015–2020. Methodologically, we first refined the census survival-ratio method by introducing calibration parameters fitted to prefecture-level Basic Resident Register migration totals, thereby improving age-specific aggregate alignment. Subsequently, spatial associations were analyzed using a machine learning pipeline based on LightGBM. To address the multicollinearity inherent in spatial socioeconomic data—a persistent challenge in urban modeling—we integrated variable clustering with Owen values, a game-theoretic attribution method. This approach allowed us to estimate model-attributed contributions while accounting for groups of highly correlated variables. The analysis revealed “mosaic-like” dynamics characterized by sharp intra-regional contrasts. Specifically, we identified spatial patterns among younger populations that were consistent with the “return to the city” phenomenon during the study period and strongly associated with high-rise condominiums, contrasting with estimated net outflows from aging suburban public housing districts. These findings demonstrate that this high-resolution, explainable AI approach can capture complex, non-uniform spatial patterns of estimated net migration and provide an exploratory basis for identifying area characteristics that warrant further investigation.
papers.journal_name: Environment and Planning B: Urban Analytics and City Science

papers.title: Roads and carbon: Suburbanisation versus induced demand in U.S. states
A Review of Building Climate‐Resilient Agriculture in Smallholder Systems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change has increasingly threatened agricultural sustainability and food security, especially in smallholder farming systems where limited resources and adaptive capacity constrain responses to climate shocks. This study systematically reviews the literature on agricultural climate resilience, focusing on resilience measurement, farmer adaptation, organizational support, and government regulation. The review shows that resilience research has evolved from vulnerability‐oriented approaches toward broader frameworks emphasizing resistance, recovery, adaptation, and transformation capacities. Existing studies indicate that farmers’ adaptive behaviors, such as production adjustment and technology adoption, form the micro‐level foundation of resilience. However, smallholders often face constraints in information, capital, technology, and market access, limiting the effectiveness of autonomous adaptation. Organizational support and government regulation therefore play essential roles through information diffusion, resource coordination, infrastructure provision, policy incentives, and collective governance. Nevertheless, current research still lacks theoretical integration, dynamic resilience assessment, cross‐scale governance analysis, and systematic understanding of institutional constraints in smallholder systems. The review highlights that agricultural climate resilience is not solely determined by farmers’ adoption of adaptation technologies, but also by how resource constraints, market barriers, and institutional arrangements shape adaptation decisions and coordination among multiple actors.

papers.title: Economics of Wind Energy: Markets, Policy, and Investment Insights
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wind energy is central to energy transitions, but research on its economics remains fragmented across markets, policy, finance, lifecycle costs, and system integration. This review consolidates the field by applying co‐word analysis, Louvain clustering, and tech‐mining emergence metrics to 2448 publications from 2015 to 2025. The analysis identifies ten thematic clusters covering grid integration, market design, techno‐economic assessment, policy instruments, socio‐environmental impacts, resource optimization, turbine and hybrid technologies, offshore costs, lifecycle and circular economy, and storage‐based sector coupling. The findings show increasing convergence on hybrid systems, uncertainty‐aware modeling, circularity, adaptive regulation, and investment risk management. Persistent gaps remain in quantifying externalities, evaluating lifecycle liabilities, managing revenue volatility, and designing policies that respond to technological and market change. The review offers an integrative economic framework that links energy systems, finance, and policy and provides guidance for policymakers, investors, and researchers seeking to support resilient, competitive, and inclusive wind energy deployment.

papers.title: Banking on Culture: Individualism and Foreign Bank Ownership
papers.journal_name: Journal of International Financial Markets Institutions & Money

papers.title: Is the Gene‐ie Out of the Bottle? The Problems and Perils of Genetics Research in Management
papers.abstract: Abstract In recent years, the field of management research has witnessed the emergence of a stream of research that seeks to identify the genetic determinants of managerial, entrepreneurial, and organizational behaviour. We challenge the reductionist epistemology underpinning this genetic perspective in management research and highlight the inherently weak inferences about human behaviour that follow from its prevailing methods and explanatory models. We further examine the ethical implications that arise from its underlying assumptions and potential future applications. We then propose recasting the role of genetics as part of a broader phenomenon‐driven approach towards studying and explaining human behaviour in management research and outline a conceptual framework aimed at generating stronger and contextually grounded explanatory models of managerial, entrepreneurial, and organizational behaviour.

papers.title: The “She‐Power” in Sustainability: Female Executives, Green Human Capital Investment, and Corporate Green Innovation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Based on data from Chinese A‐share listed companies from 2016 to 2024, we study the impact of female executives on green human capital investment. We find that female executives are positively associated with green human capital investment. Moderating effect analyses show that this positive effect is stronger for green positions requiring higher skills, under weaker environmental regulation, and in less polluting industries. Heterogeneity analyses show that green human capital investment is more directly influenced by senior management than by the board and that the main effect is stronger in firms with high labor intensity. Further analysis reveals that green human capital investment is positively associated with subsequent green innovation. Moreover, our research confirms a critical mass effect of female executives on green human capital investment. Overall, this study reveals how female executives shape firms' investment in green human capital.

papers.title: Green Loans: From Effects to Advantages
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT By conducting a systematic literature review, this study examines the opportunities and threats and thus the economic implications of green loans from banks perspective. The results show a variety of heterogeneous effects of granting green loans (GL) in several areas, as market valuation, lending process, risk or profit. From a purely numerical perspective, we find more opportunities than threats, suggesting banks should provide GL. In this context, reductions in risks and nonperforming loans as well as increases in competitiveness and profits, which are contrasted in particular by increased costs, are specifically notable. However, as theoretical opportunities do not necessarily transform into real benefits, we subsequently use the dynamic capabilities framework to elaborate approaches that will enable banks to achieve long‐term competitive advantages through GL.

papers.title: Interpreting sustainability signals: how brand origin and consumer cosmopolitanism shape CSR inferences and downstream consumer responses
papers.abstract: Purpose As restaurants worldwide increasingly adopt plant-based offerings to advance sustainability goals, understanding how consumers interpret these initiatives has become essential. Drawing from signaling theory and social identity theory, this research aims to demonstrate that plant-based menu promotions function as corporate social responsibility (CSR) signals, with consumers’ interpretations shaped jointly by restaurant brand origin and their level of cosmopolitanism. Design/methodology/approach The research used two online experiments to test the proposed framework across different cuisine types and dining contexts. Findings Consumers low in cosmopolitanism ascribe stronger CSR to domestic (vs foreign) restaurant brands, whereas those high in cosmopolitanism show the opposite pattern. Moreover, these CSR inferences translate into enhanced product-related responses and brand-related outcomes. Originality/value This research contributes to the hospitality literature on brand origin effects, restaurant sustainable practices and CSR communication. It offers insights for hospitality firms seeking to leverage plant-based initiatives to foster positive brand inferences and enhance consumer outcomes.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: The double-edged sword effect of AI-employee collaboration on hotel employees’ digital performance: a job crafting perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the differential effects of artificial intelligence (AI)-employee collaboration on hotel employees’ digital innovation performance (DIP) and digital task performance (DTP) through job crafting, with leadership empathy (LEMP) as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach This study was conducted using multitemporal survey data from 411 hotel employees and their leaders in China. Findings The results indicate that AI-employee collaboration positively affects promotion-focused job crafting (POJC) and prevention-focused job crafting (PEJC). POJC positively affects DIP and DTP, whereas PEJC positively affects DTP but negatively affects DIP. LEMP positively moderates the link with POJC and negatively with PEJC. Practical implications This study deepens understanding of AI-employee dynamics and offers insights for improving digital performance and innovation in the digital era. Originality/value Based on regulatory focus theory, this study distinguishes employee digital performance, unveils the dual pathways of AI-employee collaboration’s influence from a job crafting perspective and expands boundary conditions by incorporating LEMP, offering theoretical insights for effective hotel AI-employee collaboration.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: From inspiration to depletion: the curvilinear effect of spiritual leadership on employee role-based performance
papers.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the too-much-of-a-good-thing (TMGT) effect and conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study aims to investigate the direct and indirect curvilinear effects of spiritual leadership (SL) on employee role-based performance (RBP). Design/methodology/approach This study used a multi-study design combining an experimental study with 136 participants and a time-lagged, multisource field survey of 216 hospitality sector employees. Findings Findings collectively demonstrate that SL exhibits an inverted U-shaped curvilinear relationship with employee RBP, both directly and indirectly through employee resilience. Practical implications Theoretically, the “sweet spot” of SL challenges linear resource–performance assumptions, suggesting that TMGT and CORs theory must account for how resilience shapes the point at which SL ceases to enhance employee RBP. In practice, hospitality managers should calibrate SL to a level that strengthens employee resilience and supports effective performance across their roles. Beyond an optimal level, increasing leadership intensity may weaken these benefits, thus highlighting the importance of balanced leadership and resilience-supportive practices in hospitality management. Originality/value The study advanced hospitality leadership literature by integrating two complementary designs and providing novel evidence of the curvilinear effects of SL on employee RBP as well as the underlying psychological mechanism through which these nonlinear effects occur, thus presenting a multidimensional outcome rarely examined in SL research.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: Tell me about yourself and I might recommend you: a motivation-based explanation of crowdlending investors’ customer citizenship behavior☆
papers.abstract: Competition among entrepreneurial funding platforms has made it more important than ever to attract and retain investors to ensure the sustainability of entrepreneurial ecosystems. In this context, investor recommendations are a key mechanism to generate trust in crowdlending platforms. This paper investigates the existence of necessary and sufficient conditions that explain investor recommendations of crowdlending platforms and explores how the motivations behind investor behavior are linked to investor recommendations of these platforms. Necessary condition analysis (NCA) and qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) were performed using data on 83 investors. Of the intrinsic/self-oriented motivations considered in the analysis, only satisfaction emerged as an individual in-degree necessary condition from the NCA. The analysis also confirmed the synergistic effects of intrinsic/self-oriented and extrinsic/other-oriented motivations as sufficient conditions for explaining investor behavior. Nonetheless, such behavior can still be explained exclusively by intrinsic/self-oriented conditions. The study enriches the knowledge of how investor motivations explain the sustainability of platforms that provide alternative forms of financing for entrepreneurs.

papers.title: Does Biodiversity Risk Matter to Capital Markets? New Evidence from China
VAT Sharing, Fiscal Incentives, and Corporate Financialization
papers.abstract: Under fiscal decentralization, local government interventions driven by tax-sharing incentives are key to understanding corporate financialization. By taking China’s 2016 VAT revenue-sharing reform as a quasi-natural experiment and utilizing panel data of A-share manufacturing firms covering the 2012–2021 period, we employ an intensity DID design to examine its effect. The empirical results demonstrate that a higher local VAT share significantly inhibits corporate financialization, and this core conclusion remains stable across robustness checks. Mechanism tests reveal that strengthened fiscal incentives lead local governments to increase credit support and relax environmental enforcement, thereby mitigating financialization. This effect is more prominent for enterprises with high external financing demands, high-pollution industries, and fiscally stressed regions. The study provides insights into mitigating financialization and enhancing VAT sharing design.

papers.title: Can artificial intelligence accelerate technological progress? Researchers' perspectives on AI in manufacturing and materials science
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) raises expectations of substantial increases in rates of technological progress, but such anticipations are often not connected to detailed ground-level studies of AI use in innovation processes. Accordingly, it remains unclear how and to what extent AI can accelerate innovation. To help to fill this gap, we explore and assess results from 32 interviews with U.S.-based academic manufacturing and materials sciences researchers experienced with AI and machine learning (ML) techniques. We found that AI was primarily used for modeling of materials and manufacturing processes, facilitating cheaper and more rapid search of design spaces for materials and manufacturing processes alike. Benefits included cost, time, and computation savings in technology development. However, AI/ML tools were unreliable outside design spaces for which dense data were already available; they required skilled and judicious application in tandem with older research techniques; and concerns were raised about the potential to detrimentally circumvent opportunities for disruptive theoretical advancement. Based on these results, we suggest there is reason for optimism about acceleration in sustaining innovations through the use of AI/ML; but that support for conventional empirical, computational, and theoretical research is required to maintain the likelihood of further disruptive advances in manufacturing and materials.

papers.title: How to craft a mission? A Theory of Action for the strategic public management of mission-oriented innovation policy
papers.abstract: This paper explores the role of strategic public management within mission-oriented innovation policy. While recent scholarship has emphasised multiple aspects of missions, the distinct relevance of strategic public management in their implementation remains under-explored. To address this gap, the paper performs two complementary tasks. First, it uses a qualitative meta-synthesis of the relevant innovation literature to articulate a new Theory of Action for the analysis of missioncraft: namely, the institutional work public managers perform to create or maintain (disrupt) institutional logics supporting (hinder) their effective implementation. Second, it leverages a pre-study of the extant literature to illustrate the Theory of Action with three historical vignettes showing how the ToA can be applied at different scales and under different institutional logics (US' DARPA; China's NEV Plan programme; and EU's RIS3). Overall, the paper argues that the implementation of mission-oriented innovation policy requires public managers to adopt three critical strategic roles: i) enabling strategic learning across the public sector organisations leading the mission; ii) enabling dynamic accountability in the portfolio of projects supported by the mission; and iii) enabling collaborative innovation among the societal actors partaking the mission. By shifting the focus on the micro-foundations of mission implementation from structural underpinnings (i.e., legal, organisational, managerial) to agentic functions (i.e., strategic roles), the paper provides a new diagnostic lens for innovation policy research and practice – reflecting whether and how public managers can support mission-oriented innovation policy in light of the context-specific opportunities and constraints they face in their institutional work.

papers.title: Design anthropology for transforming power relations in societal transitions
Executive agencies in developing countries: the case of the parastatal organizations in Suriname
Symptom-level associations between childhood trauma and academic defeat: A network analysis of 11,031 Chinese adolescents
papers.abstract: Background Academic defeat represents a critical construct associated with mental health outcomes in East Asian societies with high-stakes competition. However, conventional models obscure symptom-level mechanisms linking childhood trauma to this sense of failure. This study investigated the topological architecture connecting childhood trauma to academic defeat and identified specific bridge pathways. Methods This cross-sectional study included 11,031 adolescents recruited via multi-stage stratified cluster sampling in Shandong Province, China. The Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form and a culturally adapted Defeat Scale were used to assess trauma experiences and academic defeat, respectively. A regularized partial correlation network was estimated via a Gaussian graphical model to map symptom associations. Bridge centrality indices were calculated to identify nodes connecting the constructs, and the Network Comparison Test was used to evaluate structural and expected influence invariance across genders and school types. Results The self-perceived symptom of “Learning failure” exhibited the highest expected influence within the network. “Emotional abuse” functioned as the primary bridge connecting trauma to academic defeat, specifically linking to “Powerless”. “Emotional neglect” served as a robust secondary bridge, strongly associated with “Successful person” and “Basically a winner”. Furthermore, significant structural differences existed between male and female networks, specifically regarding the pathway between “Powerless” and “Emotional abuse”. Conclusions The present study delineates the complex relationship between childhood trauma and academic defeat. Future efforts should focus on targeted interventions that address these identified bridge and central symptoms to effectively disrupt the mechanisms underlying this sense of failure.

papers.title: Motivated to exhaustion? Public service motivation, curvilinear strain, and the buffer of collaborative culture
papers.abstract: Public service motivation (PSM) is widely treated as a resource that strengthens engagement, yet excessive motivation may yield diminishing returns. Integrating the job demands-resources model, conservation of resources theory, and the too-much-of-a-good-thing logic, this study tests a curvilinear relationship between PSM and job exhaustion, and the moderating role of collaborative culture. Using a two-wave survey of 408 Korean public servants with a one-month lag, hierarchical regressions identify a U-shaped pattern: exhaustion declines at low-to-moderate PSM but rises beyond a threshold. Collaborative culture significantly flattens this curve, indicating that supportive, collective norms mitigate PSM-related strain at very high levels of PSM. The findings challenge the assumption that PSM is uniformly beneficial, recasting PSM as a conditional resource that can operate as a demand at high levels. The study clarifies when PSM is sustainable and positions collaboration as an actionable boundary condition, yielding implications for motivation theory and for the collaborative organization of public service.

papers.title: Advances in microchannel flow boiling heat transfer: mechanisms and performance optimization
papers.abstract: Microchannel flow boiling has emerged as a promising technology for thermal management of electronic devices due to its high heat transfer coefficient, low pumping power, and compact cooling architecture. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in microchannel flow boiling heat transfer and performance optimization strategies. The fundamental mechanisms governing microchannel flow boiling are first summarized with emphasis on bubble dynamics, microscale confinement effects, interfacial phase change, and thin film evaporation. Then the effects of channel geometry, surface modification, and working fluid modification on heat transfer performance are further analyzed by elucidating how these strategies regulate the underlying mechanisms of microchannel flow boiling. Furthermore, emerging optimization strategies are discussed in terms of hybrid active passive regulation, coordinated regulation of multiple boiling mechanisms, and artificial intelligence (AI) assisted prediction and optimization. Representative approaches include topology-optimized microchannel structures, adaptive shape memory alloy (SMA)-based regulation, jet microchannel coupled cooling, and AI-assisted prediction and optimization methods. The practical limitations of existing strategies are also discussed in terms of manufacturability, durability, operational stability, cost, packaging compatibility, and system level integration. Finally, the current challenges and future research directions in microchannel flow boiling are outlined. This review provides guidance for the design and optimization of next generation thermal management systems for high power electronic and energy systems.

papers.title: From Destruction to Reconstruction: Substrate-Driven Biosynthesis of Antioxidants from Antibiotic Residues in Hyperthermophilic Composting
papers.abstract: Abstract The accumulation of tetracycline (TC) in organic fertilizers poses severe risks by fostering antibiotic resistance in soil ecosystems. Hyperthermophilic composting effectively mitigates these threats, achieving nearly complete TC removal via thermal selection. Although previous studies have widely characterized the catabolic degradation routes of TC, we propose a novel transformation pathway in which TC-derived intermediates are redirected into secondary metabolism to synthesize antioxidant alkaloids and flavonoids. Integrated abiotic–biotic controls first demonstrated that while heat initiates breakdown, hyperthermophilic microbiota drive the subsequent deep transformation and diversification of products. FT-ICR-MS revealed that this process is underpinned by substrate restructuring, where recalcitrant compounds are depolymerized into bioenergetically favorable low-molecular-weight organic matter (LMW-OM). Cross-feeding assays confirmed that this accessible substrate pool significantly enhances cometabolic efficiency compared to conventional composting-derived substrates. Mechanistically, multiomics indicated that LMW-OM elevates intracellular NADH and ATP within the Thermus-dominated community, shifting metabolism from maintenance to active biosynthesis. Consequently, TC intermediates acting as structural mimics of endogenous aromatic precursors are recruited into these energized pathways to generate antioxidants. Crucially, diverting residues into anabolic networks eliminates the selective pressure exerted by intermediates, explaining the extensive attenuation of the antibiotic resistance genes. This work highlights pivotal substrate-microbe interplay, offering a new paradigm for converting antibiotic-laden waste into functional bio-organic fertilizers.

papers.title: Microbial Bioenergetics and Ecology Govern the Coupled Biogeochemical Cycling of Arsenic/Antimony and Macronutrients
papers.abstract: Abstract Arsenic (As) and antimony (Sb) are toxic metalloids whose biogeochemical cycles are strongly influenced by carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and sulfur (S) through microbially mediated coupled transformations. However, the mechanistic basis of these coupled processes remains poorly understood. In this Review, we synthesize current advances in the interconnected cycling and elucidate their thermodynamic and ecological foundations. Redox-sensitive As, Sb, C, N, and S species serve as electron donors and acceptors in microbial respiratory chains, and the combination of their redox half-reactions results in the coupled cycles. A redox-ladder framework delineates the theoretical electron flow and thermodynamically feasible coupling combinations. Many combinations have been observed in the environments-for instance, NO3– reduction to N2 coupled with As(III)/Sb(III) oxidation. Their realization also depends on microorganisms harboring key genes (e.g., aioA and arrA). The redox-ladder further predicts novel coupling processes, such as As(III)/Sb(III) oxidation coupled to N2O reduction to N2. We finally emphasize the need for quantitative biogeochemical models within global change scenarios. By integrating bioenergetic principles with microbial ecology, this Review provides a new conceptual framework for uncovering the linkages among elemental cycles, deepening our understanding of the mechanisms and environmental implications of As/Sb biogeochemical cycling coupled with macronutrients.

papers.title: Bifurcated Fluorotelomer Carboxylic Acid Biotransformation: Enoyl-Hydration versus Hydroxylation Regulated by Redox Conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract Fluorotelomer carboxylic acids (FTCAs) are important precursors of perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) in wastewater and biosolids, yet their redox-dependent biotransformation remains poorly understood. We investigated 5:3 FTCA biotransformation in microcosms inoculated with activated sludge and anaerobic digester sludge under aerobic, nitrate-reducing, sulfate-reducing, and methanogenic conditions. After correction for abiotic losses, the pseudo-first-order removal rate was 0.074 d–1 under aerobic conditions, over an order of magnitude higher than under nitrate-reducing (0.0045 d–1) and methanogenic (0.0028 d–1) conditions; sulfate-reducing conditions showed minimal removal. Nontarget Nano-ESI-HRMS analysis further revealed ultrashort-chain PFCAs, including PFPrA, and previously unreported intermediates, including keto-5:3 FTCA and 3-F-4:3 FTCA. A bifurcated FTCA biotransformation framework was unveiled, initiated by Cα-centered hydroxylation and Cβ-centered enoyl-hydration. Hydroxylation promoted iterative CF2 moiety removal and progressive chain shortening, accounting for nearly 95% of measured products and 72.8% of fluoride release under aerobic conditions, whereas enoyl-hydration dominated (>60%) under nitrate reduction and favored PFCA formation. These findings provide quantitative and mechanistic evidence for competing FTCA biotransformation routes in wastewater microbiomes and highlight redox control as a critical lever for steering PFAS fate toward either PFCA accumulation or progressive defluorination.

papers.title: Morphology-aware bidirectional state-space model for power prediction in CNC milling
papers.abstract: Accurate power prediction in CNC milling is essential for process-level power assessment, low-carbon process planning, and power-aware scheduling. However, existing data-driven predictors often degrade around trajectory transitions, as they rely on one-way temporal histories and insufficiently represent geometry-induced load variation. This paper proposes a morphology-aware bidirectional state-space model (MA-BiSSM) for CNC milling power prediction. A bidirectional scanning policy exploits historical states and pre-known planned-trajectory context within a machining window, improving prediction around entry, cornering, and exit regions. A material-removal morphology module encodes a Z-map-derived two-dimensional material-removal map together with a removal-height gate, conditioning the cutting-related correction on geometry-induced load variation. Experiments on real CNC milling monitoring data evaluate the prediction of the X -, Y -, and Z -axis powers and spindle power. Compared with the best result among all competing models for each metric, MA-BiSSM reduces RMSE, MAE, Abs Sum Error, and normalized absolute error (NAE) by approximately 33.0%, 19.1%, 15.3%, and 19.1%, respectively (LSTM for RMSE, MAE, and NAE; Mamba for Abs Sum Error). Ablation studies confirm that bidirectional temporal modeling and material-removal morphology conditioning provide complementary gains in transient accuracy and long-horizon power-profile consistency. The resulting power-profile estimates can support comparison of alternative toolpaths and process-parameter settings, peak-load identification, and energy-aware process planning for cleaner machining.

papers.title: Greenhouse gas and economic assessments of biochar-based composite panels from forest residues
papers.abstract: Among other threats to forests across the western U.S., large-scale outbreaks of mountain pine beetle have generated extensive volumes of low-value forest residues that increase wildfire risk while remaining underutilized as a carbon resource. Converting these residues into high-value biochar products offers a pathway for carbon stabilization and value creation, yet most existing markets for biochar remain relatively low value. This study represents the first system-level assessment of biochar-based composite panels that jointly evaluates life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and techno-economic performance for biochar-based panel products at industrial scale. The modeled system integrates distributed biochar production using portable pyrolysis units with centralized panel manufacturing that uses kraft lignin as a renewable binder. In addition to a base-case (BC) configuration representing conventional biochar-lignin composite panel production, five alternative scenarios are modeled in which panels undergo secondary pyrolysis treatments at different temperatures and processing conditions associated with potential adsorption, structural, or fire-resistant applications. Cradle-to-gate GHG emissions range from 311 to 565 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 . In addition, an illustrative 100-year carbon retention scenario based on assumed long-term biochar stability results in net GHG balances ranging from −343 to −750 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 . Minimum selling price values range from 548 to 1101 US$/m 3 depending on panel type and processing conditions. The BC panel configuration falls toward the higher end of conventional particleboard and MDF price benchmarks, while the estimated MSPs of pyrolyzed panel configurations fall within or below the price ranges of selected benchmark materials used in water remediation and fire-resistant composite applications. These comparisons provide market-price context for the modeled MSPs but do not establish functional equivalence or commercial competitiveness, which require experimental validation.

papers.title: Performance analysis and design optimization of modified coal gasification slag-based backfill materials
Janus electrospun MXene-based photothermal membrane for efficient solar-driven interfacial evaporation and simulated radioactive wastewater treatment
Valorization of dredged sludge into sustainable subgrade materials through a novel industrial solid waste-derived stabilizer
papers.abstract: The development of sustainable and cost-effective stabilizers is urgently needed for the valorization of dredged sludge from riparian and lakeside engineering construction. Conventional cement-based methods have high environmental footprints, while traditional alkali-activated systems relying on sodium silicate remain costly. This study replaces conventional alkali activator with a silica fume (SF)-based activator to develop a novel, eco-friendly stabilizer derived from industrial solid wastes (ISW) for stabilizing dredged sludge as sustainable subgrade material. The mechanical, microstructural and environmental characteristics of the stabilized sludge were investigated and compared with the traditional stabilized sludge. Results demonstrate that the ISW-derived stabilized sludge, recommended at 100% compaction degree, 15% moisture content, and 12% stabilizer dosage, meets all mechanical criteria for highway base and subbase courses. Microstructural analyses confirm the formation of calcium aluminosilicate hydrate (C-A-S-H) gel, which densifies the structure and converts harmful pores into less harmful ones. Durability tests further reveal deterioration mechanisms that residual unreacted components undergo secondary reactions that partially mitigate structural damage under dry-wet cycles. In contrast, freeze-thaw cycles lack such secondary reactions, leading to more severe pore coarsening, cracking, and mass loss. Notably, a 16% ISW-derived stabilizer dosage achieves equivalent strength to 20% cement, while reducing cost by 2.36% and CO 2 emissions by 79.62%. This study offers a cost-effective, low-carbon, and high-performance solution for dredged sludge valorization.

papers.title: Seasonal drivers and infrastructure impacts on dissolved oxygen dynamics in complex environmental systems
papers.abstract: Urban streams are increasingly regulated by the interaction of climate-driven thermal stress and episodic infrastructure disturbances, yet their combined influence on dissolved oxygen (DO) dynamics remains insufficiently resolved across temporal scales. This study quantified the combined effects of temperature, hydrology, and combined sewer overflow (CSO) activity on DO across four urban watersheds in Philadelphia, USA, using 12 years of high-frequency monitoring integrated with precipitation, streamflow, and modeled CSO data. A multi-scale framework combining event-stratified comparisons, distributed lag models (0-3 days), and multivariate regression was used to evaluate controls on DO variability. Across all watersheds, DO exhibited a consistent seasonal cycle that reflects background thermal constraints on oxygen solubility and metabolic demand. This seasonal pattern establishes a baseline physical regime, against which shorter-term variability becomes apparent. At event-scales, CSO and wet-weather conditions consistently reduced minimum daily DO relative to dry conditions, with strongest effects observed in more hydraulically connected systems. Distributed lag models further revealed watershed-dependent persistence of CSO impacts, ranging from rapid recovery to multi-day DO suppression in systems with greater retention and reduced flushing capacity. Multivariate models identified temperature as the dominant control on baseline DO conditions, while event-based and lagged analyses showed that CSO activity and hydrologic variability govern short-term deviations and persistence in DO dynamics. Overall, urban DO dynamics are structured primarily by event-scale and lagged CSO and hydrologic responses, with seasonal thermal conditions providing a baseline context for variability.

papers.title: Modeling and optimization of siphon downflow hanging sponge reactor using ASM1 for enhanced nutrient removal in municipal wastewater treatment
papers.abstract: Siphon downflow hanging sponge (siphon-DHS) reactors offer an energy-efficient alternative for biological nutrient removal. However, their performance is highly sensitive to internal configuration. Here, siphon-DHS was modeled using Activated Sludge Model No. 1 (ASM1) to systematically optimize zone volume ratios of the reactor for enhanced municipal wastewater treatment. Four reactor configurations (A, B, C, and D) with varying aerobic, changing, and anaerobic zone volume ratios were operated and evaluated through water quality and microbial community analysis. Reactor D, which had the highest performance index (59%), was selected for model calibration. Zone-specific first-order rate constants derived from experimental data revealed the highest rates for chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal ( k 1 = 0.624 h −1 ) and nitrification ( k 1 = 0.571 h −1 ) in aerobic zones and exceptional denitrification ( k 3 = 1.288 h −1 ) in anaerobic zones. Systematic optimization using equal-weighted and denitrification-prioritized approaches identified an optimal configuration of 0.55:0.10:0.35 (aerobic:changing:anaerobic) for denitrification prioritization, achieving 84% COD removal, 81% nitrification, and 91% denitrification—representing a 68% percentage-point improvement in denitrification over the baseline. Dynamic Simulink simulations elucidated the process distribution and substrate utilization across zones. Meanwhile, sensitivity analysis revealed that minimizing the changing zone to 10% while maximizing sharp aerobic–anaerobic interfaces enhanced overall performance. The calibrated model provides a scalable, energy-efficient framework for siphon-DHS reactor design, offering significant potential for sustainable municipal wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Comparative life cycle assessment and carbon footprint of sodium-ion and Lithium Iron phosphate batteries: A case study in China
papers.abstract: To support China's “Dual Carbon” goals, this study applies a life cycle assessment approach to compare the environmental performance of layered-oxide sodium-ion batteries and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries under Chinese manufacturing conditions. A cradle-to-gate system boundary was adopted, with the production of a 1 kWh battery pack defined as the functional unit. Using foreground inventory data collected through on-site investigations of Chinese battery manufacturers, literature sources, and localized Ecoinvent datasets, a localized endpoint damage-oriented life cycle impact assessment model is applied to quantify the potential environmental impacts and carbon footprints of the two battery systems. The results indicate that the total potential environmental impact of sodium-ion batteries is 9.09 Pt, representing a 27.3% reduction compared with LFP batteries (12.50 Pt). In addition, the carbon footprint of sodium-ion batteries is 56.8 kg CO₂-eq, which is 24.9% lower than that of LFP batteries (75.5 kg CO₂-eq). These findings demonstrate the significant potential of layered-oxide sodium-ion batteries in terms of carbon emission reduction and resource security. Further improvements in their environmental performance will depend on manufacturing process optimization and the adoption of cleaner energy sources, while LFP batteries should prioritize raw material substitution and material reduction strategies.

papers.title: Enhancing methane production from chicken manure mono-digestion: Optimisation of temperature and dilution parameters via response surface methodology
papers.abstract: Chicken manure (CM) is a nitrogen-rich waste stream with significant potential for renewable energy recovery; however, its mono-digestion is often constrained by ammonia inhibition, limiting process efficiency and scalability. This study investigates the optimisation of CM mono-digestion using response surface methodology (RSM) based on a central composite design, focusing on the effects of dilution ratio and temperature on biogas production performance. Biochemical methane potential assays were conducted to evaluate cumulative biogas production, methane composition and chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal efficiency. The developed models were statistically significant ( p < 0.05), confirming the suitability of RSM for process optimisation. Temperature was identified as the dominant factor influencing biogas production, while the dilution ratio significantly affected COD removal efficiency. Optimal conditions were obtained at a CM : water ratio of 1 : 10 and 27 °C, resulting in a cumulative biogas production of 178 mL, a methane composition of 97%, a COD removal efficiency of 78% and an estimated methane yield of 30 mL CH 4 /g VS. The enhanced performance under psychrophilic conditions is attributed to reduced ammonia toxicity and improved process stability. These findings highlight the importance of operational optimisation in improving energy recovery and treatment efficiency from CM. From a practical perspective, the ability to operate at lower temperatures may reduce heating energy requirements, thereby improving the economic feasibility of CM-based biogas systems. Further studies are required to evaluate long-term performance and scalability under continuous operating conditions.

papers.title: Assessing the sustainable development of Chinese wind energy from the inclusive wealth perspective
papers.abstract: The article delineates the system boundaries of wind power projects through life cycle assessment framework, integrates shadow prices and the Inclusive Wealth Index (IWI) to assess the sustainability of such projects in China. The article provides statistical descriptions of the life cycle table, greenhouse gas emissions, and life cycle energy consumption of wind power systems. Additionally, the study estimates the actual shadow prices across different wind power projects to evaluate the IWI. Furthermore, the article employs learning curves to analyze the stock and price of relevant production capital to compare the sustainability characteristics of wind power projects under both static and dynamic conditions based on IWI measurements. Recognizing regional disparities, the article underscores the importance of addressing the “wind curtailment” issue. Finally, the article suggests strategies for developed nations to foster the sustainable development of wind power in China. This study provides a theoretical reference for the feasibility and sustainable development of subsequent wind power projects.

papers.title: Explainable, Uncertainty‐Aware Machine Learning for Maize Land Suitability and Climate Resilience in Lorestan Province, Western Iran
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Maize ( Zea mays L.) is strategically important in Iran, yet its cultivation in the semi‐arid Zagros is constrained by limited and variable water, heat stress and heterogeneous soils, while conventional suitability assessments are deterministic, rarely validated spatially and provide no measure of confidence. The aim of this study was to develop an explainable, uncertainty‐aware machine‐learning framework for maize land‐suitability mapping that is interpretable, spatially robust and climate‐aware and to demonstrate it in Lorestan Province (≈28,300 km 2 ), western Iran. The experimental material comprised harmonised multi‐source geospatial predictors—soil properties (SoilGrids 2.0), climate variables (Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data, CHIRPS; TerraClimate), moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer (MODIS) vegetation indices and shuttle radar topography mission (SRTM) terrain—together with 520 reference sites labelled by applying the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) maximum‐limitation land‐evaluation procedure to explicitly documented land qualities. As the method of investigation, six classifiers (Elastic‐Net, support vector machine, multilayer perceptron, random forest, LightGBM and XGBoost) were trained and evaluated under spatial block cross‐validation; predictions were interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and uncertainty was quantified using predictive entropy and between‐model ensemble variance and then validated against observed classification error. Data collection drew on openly available gridded products resampled to a 250 m grid, with Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) projections under two shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs) used for climate scenarios. Gradient‐boosting models performed best, achieving a macro‐ F 1 ‐score of 0.79 under spatial block cross‐validation against 0.87 under random cross‐validation, confirming that random partitioning inflates apparent skill. Growing‐season precipitation, aridity, heat‐stress frequency, vegetation condition and root‐zone soil properties dominated, with pronounced thresholds; predictive entropy was inversely related to classification accuracy, confirming that the uncertainty surface is diagnostic of error rather than merely descriptive and the most suitable land was not necessarily the most climate‐resilient. We conclude that the framework offers a transparent, probabilistic and transferable alternative to deterministic suitability mapping for climate‐smart dryland agricultural planning.

papers.title: Visuality, temporality, and the uncertain geopolitics of the Russo-Ukrainian war
papers.abstract: This Symposium interrogates the relationship between the spatial, the temporal, and the visual in a war-affected society. Several leading researchers working on Ukraine in multiple disciplinary fields examine how combining the visual and the (unseen) temporal are vital for understanding the new and uncertain spatial configurations that emerge from the displacement and stress of conflict and bordering. These interventions aim to amplify the voices and visions of those who have been marginalised and overlooked. It brings into dialogue perspectives of displacement with those who have remained.
