papers.title: A de facto referendum: how proxy advisors set their standards through director elections
papers.abstract: We study the standard-setting role of proxy advisors when their preferences diverge from regulatory mandates and shareholders’ choices. The say-on-pay (SOP) regulation in 2011 allowed U.S. firms to adopt non-annual voting schedules, whereas proxy advisors strongly preferred annual voting. We show that they leverage negative recommendations in compensation committee member elections (CMEs) as an alternative channel for expressing compensation-related concerns in non-SOP years. Among firms that hold triennial SOP votes, negative recommendations in CMEs are significantly more frequent during non-SOP years. Moreover, proxy advisors promote their standards even more strongly in firms where their preferences are less aligned with the voting choices of shareholders, highlighting their standard-setting role even when unpopular.

papers.title: A Primer on Blue Accounting and Finance
papers.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between blue accounting and blue finance and its implications for sustainable ocean‐based development. Using a conceptual review of the United Nations Sustainable Blue Economy Finance Principles, major financial instruments, and selected cases, the paper shows that blue finance creates demand for standardized and comparable information, while credible blue accounting supports activity eligibility, environmental risk assessment, performance monitoring, and the prevention of bluewashing. It conceptualizes blue accounting as a connected architecture spanning corporate or entity‐level reporting, project‐ and financial‐instrument‐level accounting, and national or subnational ocean accounts. These levels serve distinct but complementary purposes across financial decision‐making, corporate management, public policy, and environmental governance. The analysis finds that existing accounting methods, including SEEA‐consistent ocean accounts, provide an important but incomplete foundation. Persistent difficulties in valuation, reporting boundaries, recognition, measurement, materiality, attribution, data availability, and institutional capacity limit their effectiveness. Addressing these limitations requires combining established approaches with marine‐specific definitions, ecological indicators, valuation methods, and stronger connectivity across accounting levels. Blue finance should therefore be understood as part of a broader institutional transition aligning accounting, governance, and capital allocation with ecosystem resilience.

papers.title: Retail Investor Attention and Voluntary ESG Disclosure: Evidence from Two Investor Interaction Platforms in China
papers.abstract: This study examines the relationship between retail investor attention and firms’ voluntary environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure, drawing on a comprehensive dataset from investor interactive platforms (IIPs) in China. We document a positive association between retail investor attention and firms’ voluntary ESG disclosure, which holds across a wide range of robustness checks. Cross‐sectional evidence indicates that this association is stronger for firms with better ESG performance, larger size, stronger governance, and for those receiving more negatively toned ESG inquiries on the IIPs. The association is also more pronounced under external conditions such as policy initiatives and analyst coverage. Further analyses show that it is primarily linked to information‐seeking as opposed to gambling‐oriented attention, and to inquiries regarding financially material ESG issues. Firms issuing ESG reports during periods of heightened retail investor attention tend to experience favourable capital market outcomes. Overall, the evidence underscores the role of retail investors as a visible demand‐side force associated with voluntary ESG disclosure.

papers.title: Manipulating Statistics to Justify Self-Serving Recommendations
The Transformative Impact of Prosthetics on Well-being of Consumers with Disabilities
Environmental performance feedback and green innovation: The moderating role of organizational slack
papers.abstract: Prior research has highlighted a variety of external and internal drivers of green innovation (GI), yet much less is known about how firms interpret their own environmental performance and adjust GI strategies accordingly. Drawing on the behavioral theory of the firm, this study investigates how environmental performance feedback is associated with firms’ GI decisions. Using panel data from Chinese publicly listed firms, the results reveal a U-shaped relationship between performance below aspirations and GI, and an inverted U-shaped relationship when performance exceeds aspirations. Organizational slack weakens both patterns, reducing firms’ responsiveness to both negative and positive environmental performance feedback. These findings provide new insight into how firms adapt their GI strategies in response to environmental performance feedback signals.

papers.title: The more the better? The nonlinear innovation effect of the big data policy
papers.abstract: Although big data policy has been widely regarded as a key instrument for promoting firm innovation in the digital era, many policies still fall short of expectations, prompting growing scholarly attention to the relationship between big data policy and firm innovation performance. Existing studies offer inconsistent insight because they examine policy effects through linear lenses such as signaling, rent-seeking, or isolated resource provision, while paying insufficient attention to the underlying resource mechanisms embedded in big data policy and how firms' internal and external contexts shape their responses. By integrating the resource-based view and neoinstitutional theory, this study develops a resource-based and institutionally embedded explanation of how big data policy intensity affects firm innovation performance. Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2013 to 2022, this study reveals that the big data policy intensity has an inverted U-shaped effect on innovation performance. Furthermore, the unabsorbed slack and absorbed slack exert heterogeneous moderating effects on this inverted U-shaped relationship. This study further finds that marketization and absorbed slack can jointly moderate the relationship between big data policy intensity and innovation performance. Overall, this study extends the policy–innovation literature by revealing when big data policy facilitates or constrains firm innovation, while offering practical implications for policymakers and firms.

papers.title: Director Expertise and Compliance to Corporate Social Responsibility Regulations
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This paper investigates whether assigning CSR‐specific expertise to the board committee legally responsible for CSR improves compliance with mandatory CSR law and shapes how firms organize that compliance. Research Findings/Insights Using Indian listed companies subject to mandatory CSR regulation, we find that CSR expertise on CSR committees is associated with higher compliance and more concentrated CSR activities across categories and locations. These associations are stronger among firms facing greater competitive or financial pressures and those without prior CSR engagement. High compliance combined with CSR expertise is also associated with higher firm value, improved creditworthiness, and greater institutional ownership. Theoretical/Academic Implications Our findings highlight how directors with CSR expertise help companies improve legal compliance with mandatory CSR regulations and pursue more focused CSR strategies. This research identifies committee‐level CSR expertise as an important governance mechanism shaping both regulatory compliance and the organization of CSR activities. It demonstrates the benefits of embedding CSR expertise within board structures. Practitioner/Policy Implications We provide evidence that directors with CSR expertise and stronger compliance positively affect firm outcomes. Governments and policymakers could use these findings to promote CSR expertise on corporate boards, incentivize compliance, and promote the convergence of financial and social goals. Our study provides empirical support for recent public policies, including the 2020 EU recommendation to appoint sustainability experts on corporate boards.

papers.title: Collaboration or Opportunism? Supplier Equity Stakes in Customers and Audit Fees
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question Based on relational and resource dependence theories, this study investigates the impact of supplier equity stakes in customers (SESC) on audit fees and its underlying mechanisms from the perspective of auditors' behavioral decision‐making. Research Findings The findings reveal that SESC significantly reduces audit fees, supporting the collaboration hypothesis. Mechanism analysis indicates that SESC lowers audit fees by reducing operational risk and audit complexity. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect of SESC on reducing audit fees is weakened when the holding level is high, the duration is short, and the supplier is state‐owned, whereas when the firm's external bargaining power and industry monopoly power are low, this reduction effect is enhanced. Theoretical Implications This study enriches the literature on supply chain characteristics by examining equity relationships and enriches the literature on the influence of supply chain characteristics on auditors' behavioral decisions from the perspective of SESC. Furthermore, this study extends the comprehension of SESC in corporate governance and auditing practices through the theoretical lens of relational theory and resource dependence theory. Practitioner Implications First, enterprises should recognize the strategic role of SESC in modern supply chain management and actively cultivate and develop this innovative relationship to enhance supply chain resilience and security. Second, auditors should pay heightened attention to changes in SESC to effectively evaluate supply chain stability and adjust audit workloads accordingly. Lastly, policymakers should strengthen policy support and incentive mechanisms for supply chain equity holding practices.

papers.title: Turning a private surveillance service into a public disclosure: the case of Amazon's ring doorbell
papers.abstract: This article analyses the interaction between broader political, economic and cultural changes and the local experiences of citizens using the Amazon Ring doorbell. The concept ‘luxury surveillance’ is used to study how citizens engage with the live and recorded images of the Ring doorbell. The paper empirically analyses the impact of the Ring, through (1) observations of platform use, (2) surveys on Facebook, and (3) in-depth interviews (N = 73) with owners of the Ring in four neighbourhoods in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. The findings reveal how the Amazon Ring reframes mundane interactions into mass surveillance opportunities, impacts the presumption of innocence, leads to different forms of perceived privacy, and provides a permanent sense of alertness by the owners.

papers.title: Online activism at odds: Exploring tensions in the everyday practice of ‘professional’ and ‘social media’ activists
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how two groups of activists – ‘professional’ (civil society members) and ‘independent’ activists (using primarily social media for activism) – construct the political power of digital technologies in everyday practice. We focus on how the daily practice of activists draws on both individual experiences and societal macro-discourses to develop a range of discursive resources and subject positions in the symbolic construction of digital activism. Based on a critical discourse analysis of 18 semi-structured interviews, the findings reveal three tensions between discourse and practice, namely: digital activism vs. boots-on-the-ground activism; horizontalism vs. formal organization; and private vs. activist (digital) lives. We argue that despite their persistence, the promises of technology for social justice offered by hegemonic techno-utopian discourses do not neatly fit activist practice. In the complex, messy, and fluid context of everyday life, such promises and ideals are often negotiated, reappropriated, adapted, or rejected by activists. Democratic values are thus not inscribed in technology: local context, organizational structure, and individual factors shape the ways digital technologies help or hinder digital activism. We advise citizen activists to critically consider dominant techno-utopian discourses, particularly their simplified picture of political decision-making processes. Such awareness can better equip citizens when dealing with the tensions generated by their own activist practice.

papers.title: Causal inference of multiple interrelated exposures: Contributions of ischemic placental disease to preterm delivery
papers.abstract: Ischemic placental disease (IPD) involves three obstetrical complications - preeclampsia, placental abruption, and fetal growth restriction - and is implicated in up to 55% of early deliveries. Despite substantial overlap in their etiology and epidemiologic risk profiles, existing studies have assessed their effects independently. Using data from the Consortium on Safe Labor (2002-2008; n = 203, 990), we examined the composite and separate effects of the IPD conditions on spontaneous and indicated preterm delivery (sPTD and iPTD). We systematically specified joint IPD probabilities, corresponding to combinations of hypothetical stochastic and deterministic interventions. Eliminating all IPD reduced sPTD (RR = 0.93; 95% CI = 0.92, 0.94) and iPTD (RR = 0.66; 95% CI = 0.64, 0.67) from observed levels. Eliminating preeclampsia alone reduced sPTD (RR = 0.94; 95% CI = 0.94, 0.95) and iPTD (RR = 0.72; 95% CI=0.71, 0.73). Partially reducing joint IPD co-occurrence among 58% of individuals who met criteria for high-risk, by magnitudes drawn from separate low-dose aspirin meta-analyses, yielded minimal reductions for sPTD (RR = 0.99; 95% CI=0.98, 0.99) and iPTD (RR = 0.89; 95%CI=0.88, 0.89). Preeclampsia drives IPD's association with both PTD subtypes; under the stated assumptions, hypothetically eliminating preeclampsia yielded the largest iPTD reduction.

papers.title: Coordinating fragmented global AI governance: Control, Rights, and Safety as a regime complex
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence governance is often discussed as if it were a single global policy domain. In practice, governments confront a coordination problem across partially overlapping agendas pursued through different instruments and actor configurations. This research note conceptualizes global AI governance as a non-exhaustive regime complex organized around three analytically distinct governance logics: Control, Rights, and Safety. The three are selected because each combines a distinct problem definition, recurrent instrument bundle, actor configuration, and set of portable policy objects. Using an Overton-derived corpus of 198,823 AI-related policy documents and a monthly actor-by-regime panel for 1994–2025, I compare metadata-indexed trajectories, cross-regime overlap, leadership shares, temporal alignment, and OECD-relative post-event salience around three named policy moments. A stratified full-text calibration using 73 documents that were substantively readable by both independent coders, drawn from an initial sample of 100, produced high inter-coder reliability but only partial correspondence between metadata and full-text judgments; correspondence was strongest for Control and weakest for Safety. Within that explicitly documentary scope, Control has the highest metadata prevalence (65.8% of regime-bearing documents) but comparatively unsettled leadership and event-linked uptake. Rights is the clearest IGO-centered regime and shows a short-window post-2019 signal that does not survive stronger interpretations of convergence. Safety has the clearest hybrid public-private configuration. Most metadata-coded regime-bearing documents register one regime, while 13.3% combine two or three, locating candidate interfaces for closer examination. The results imply that coordination, coherence, and integration must be designed differently across regimes rather than pursued through a single omnibus strategy.

papers.title: Galamsey eats our food: Reframing illegal mining as a food systems crisis in Ghana
papers.abstract: Abstract Illegal artisanal and small-scale gold mining ( galamsey ) in Ghana is commonly framed as an environmental or economic issue. This commentary argues that such perspectives are incomplete because illegal mining fundamentally constitutes a food systems crisis. Drawing on a systems perspective, this commentary synthesizes existing literature to demonstrate how galamsey disrupts agricultural production, contaminates water resources, undermines livelihoods, and creates reinforcing cycles of environmental degradation and food insecurity. The commentary identifies key leverage points, including strengthened, politically accountable enforcement; simplified pathways to legal mining; locally viable alternative livelihoods; geospatial environmental monitoring; community participation; and restoration of degraded agricultural land. By reframing galamsey as a food systems challenge, this commentary calls for integrated policy responses that align environmental sustainability with livelihood security.

papers.title: Widening urban-rural gaps amid narrowing regional disparities in cropland footprints of food consumption in China
Classification Drift: Decisions Passing Quietly but Compounding Inequity
papers.abstract: Public-sector classification systems accumulate classification drift, a widening gap between what employees actually do, how their work is described, and how they are compensated. Because classification shapes pay, role comparison, and internal equity at scale, classification drift quietly compounds into measurable inequity. At a large U.S. urban public school district (the District), this drift manifested as 435 employees sharing the title “Specialist” across 24 pay grades ($47,000–$125,000). This article describes PRISM (Progressive Refinement and Intelligence Synthesis Model), a multi-model AI framework developed with a research-university partner’s Data Science Institute that introduces validation friction at high-stakes decision points. Rather than automating approvals, PRISM surfaces disagreement between independent AI models and routes ambiguous cases to human reviewers with a structured evidence package. Across 992 positions, 173 cases (17%) were flagged for escalated review. This article describes what public HR offices, with or without AI, can do to address classification drift.

Recent advances in combustion/explosion hazards and suppression strategies for metal hydride hydrogen storage materials
papers.abstract: Metal hydride solid-state hydrogen storage materials show strong potential for large-scale hydrogen energy applications because of their high volumetric hydrogen storage density, mild operating conditions, and relatively sound inherent safety. However, combustion and explosion hazards remain during preparation, storage, utilization, and disposal. These hazards mainly arise from hydrogen release during endothermic dehydrogenation, subsequent exothermic combustion of released hydrogen and oxidation of active metal residues, formation of combustible dust clouds, and rapid interaction with air. This review examines the process features and associated combustion and explosion hazards of the primary preparation routes for metal hydrides. It further analyzes the combustion and explosion behavior and multiphase reaction mechanisms of representative metal hydrides, with particular emphasis on how the dehydrogenation-oxidation coupling process intensifies flame propagation and explosion severity. In addition, the review summarizes the suppression mechanisms of inert gases, solid inhibitors, and composite inhibitors, highlighting physical dilution and cooling, free-radical scavenging, and protective film formation. The reviewed evidence indicates that preparation process control and appropriately selected suppression strategies can lessen combustion and explosion hazards and provide practical guidance for the safer engineering deployment of metal hydride hydrogen storage materials.

papers.title: Deep underground energy storage solutions for data centers driven by artificial intelligence energy consumption
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has driven an unprecedented surge in electricity consumption by data centers (DCs). Although renewable energy and ground-based energy storage technologies are being widely adopted, they still face inherent limitations in scalability, safety, structure and stability. This review proposes deep underground energy storage (DUES) as a new approach and discusses three specific technologies: hydrogen storage, compressed air energy storage, and flow batteries. Firstly, it is found that DUES can align with AI load curves. The three technologies span storage durations from quarterly to hourly scales and response times from minutes to seconds, matching respectively the sustained high loads of AI model pre-training, the intermittent loads of fine-tuning, and the stochastic loads of inference. Secondly, we further develop a “Source-Grid-Production-Storage-Computing” model, in which DUES serves as the regulating hub bridging the intermittency of renewable energy with the stability of DCs. Subsequently, an economic assessment indicates that the levelized cost of storage for flow batteries ranges 0.340∼0.455 yuan/kWh, while that for compressed air energy storage ranges 0.746∼0.998 yuan/kWh, making them cost-competitive. Although the cost of hydrogen storage is 1.085∼1.658 yuan/kWh, it possesses strategic value. Finally, in view of challenges such as siting and stability of storage facilities, and system conversion efficiency, we recommend launching DUES for DC pilot projects in the short term, advancing multi-scenario applications in the medium term, and achieving industrialization in the long term. In summary, DUES represents a feasible, economically viable, and scalable solution to the energy challenges faced by AI-driven DCs.

papers.title: From cross-border power links to a digitalized regional market: A critical review of the ASEAN power grid as a catalyst for decarbonization
A review and comparative study of spectral correction models for photovoltaic performance under different atmospheric regimes and PV technologies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Spectral effects can cause non-negligible deviations in photovoltaic performance modelling, yet the applicability of existing spectral correction models remains insufficiently understood across different climates, weather conditions, and PV technologies. Most existing spectral correction models have been developed under clear or all-sky conditions, while their performance under cloudy conditions has not been systematically investigated. This limitation is critical, as cloudy conditions account for a substantial fraction of operating periods in many regions, and the spectral distribution varies substantially with cloud cover and cloud properties, introducing additional uncertainty in model accuracy and generalisability. This study provides a comprehensive review of recent advances in PV spectral correction modelling, including spectral variability drivers and characterization approaches, and further conducts a unified benchmarking analysis. Using a public dataset comprising measurements from three climatically distinct sites, eight representative spectral correction models were evaluated for four PV technologies under both clear-sky and cloudy-sky conditions. The results reveal a strong weather-regime dependence in model performance. Under clear-sky conditions, multi-parameter formulations based on precipitable water (PW), particularly f(AMa_PW) and f(AMa_AOD_PW), generally show better prediction performance than the other evaluated approaches. Under cloudy conditions, formulations based on the clear-sky index, generally show improved prediction performance compared with the basic f(AMa) formulation. In contrast, the widely used single-parameter model f(AMa) performs poorly under both regimes, while f(APE) shows mixed performance but may remain useful for specific PV technologies such as a-Si. Cloudy conditions account for a substantial fraction of annual operating periods and should not be neglected in long-term PV performance assessment. Overall, no single spectral correction model is universally optimal across all climates, weather conditions, and PV technologies. Model suitability instead depends on whether its predictors capture the dominant physical processes controlling spectral variability under the corresponding operating regime. These findings provide practical guidance for the development of more adaptive and climate-aware spectral correction methods for PV performance modelling.

papers.title: Creating a Circular Economy Vision for the Data Centre Industry
Entropy as a diagnostic for time-related constraints on circular transition: Evidence from plastic waste management in the OECD–EU countries
papers.abstract: This study examines time-related constraints on circularity by applying Shannon entropy to measure distributional dispersion across end-of-life fates in plastic waste management. Using OECD data for 1990–2018, end-of-life shares for recycling, incineration, landfill, mismanaged, and littered waste are combined with entropy to assess structural change over time. Entropy makes that structural shift visible and comparable across time. During the early 1990s, plastic waste management was highly predictable due to landfill dominance. From the mid-2010s onward, entropy stabilized at a high level despite continued growth in recycling. That plateau is consistent with persistent dispersion across competing end-of-life routes rather than convergence toward recycling dominance.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Hexavalent Chromium Reduction in Fe(II)-Bearing Clay Mineral and Fe (hydr)oxide Binary Systems: Competitive Adsorption versus Mediated Electron Transfer
papers.abstract: Abstract Fe(II)-bearing clay minerals are widespread reductants of hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) in subsurface environments. However, the influences of coexisting Fe (hydr)oxides on Cr(VI) reduction by Fe(II)-bearing clay minerals remain elusive. Here, Cr(VI) reduction was investigated in premixed systems of reduced nontronite NAu-2 (rNAu-2) and various Fe (hydr)oxides. Results showed that coexisting ferrihydrite significantly facilitated Cr(VI) reduction during the quick stage (0–2.5 min) across pH 5.5–9.0. During the subsequent slow stage (2.5–205 min), ferrihydrite inhibited Cr(VI) reduction at pH 5.5–7.0 but enhanced it at pH 9.0. In contrast, coexisting goethite had negligible effects. Without Fe (hydr)oxides, direct reduction by rNAu-2 dominated for Cr(VI) removal. In the presence of Fe (hydr)oxides, competitive adsorption was found to inhibit direct Cr(VI) reduction, yet Fe (hydr)oxide-mediated electron transfer effectively offset this inhibitory effect. Both competitive adsorption and mediated electron transfer were influenced by the type and dosage of Fe (hydr)oxides, as well as solution pH. Kinetic modeling revealed that ferrihydrite-mediated electron transfer contributed 1.8–71.5% of the total Cr(VI) reduction, with greater contributions observed at higher solution pH and ferrihydrite dosage. Our findings provide new insights into mineral–mineral electron transfer and its role in regulating Cr(VI) fate in subsurface environments.

papers.title: Trace Hydrogen Sulfide Enhances Plasmid-Mediated Antibiotic Resistance Gene Transfer under Anaerobic Sewer-Like Conditions: Associations with Contact and Energy-State Responses
papers.abstract: Abstract The dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in sewer systems poses a potential threat to public health. However, it is currently unclear how hydrogen sulfide (H2S) in anaerobic sewers affects plasmid-mediated ARG transfer. Here, we evaluated the effects of environmentally relevant concentrations (1–100 μmol·L–1) of H2S on ARG transfer across different sewer microbial communities. The results demonstrated that H2S significantly enhanced the transfer frequency of plasmid pKJK5 in sediment-derived (2.06–3.06-fold), sewage-derived (1.50–2.81-fold), and bioaerosol-derived (2.42–4.68-fold) recipient communities in standardized liquid anaerobic conjugation assays. In mixed-community models, H2S increased total acyl-homoserine lactone (AHL)-equivalent signals and was associated with selective enrichment of polysaccharides in extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), coinciding with enhanced microbial aggregation and contact. In single-strain models, H2S was associated with reductive-stress-like responses, lowered the NAD+/NADH ratio, enhanced phosphofructokinase and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase activities, strengthened proton motive force, and increased ATP content. Inhibitor experiments and structural equation modeling suggested ATP availability as the strongest intracellular predictor of enhanced transfer, with AHL-associated EPS changes acting as a potential extracellular contributor. These findings identify a concentration-dependent sulfide effect on conjugation under anaerobic conditions and support a testable pathway-level framework for future in situ sewer studies.

papers.title: Elucidating Olivine Carbon Mineralization Behaviors under Weakly Acidic to Alkaline Conditions for CO2 Storage
papers.abstract: Abstract Olivine ((Mg,Fe)2SiO4), an ultrabasic mineral primarily found in peridotite rock, is earth-abundant and thus has great potential to store anthropogenic CO2 at a scale relevant to climate change mitigation. The groundwater from geologic formations composed of peridotite, such as the Samail Ophiolite in Oman, has an ultrahigh pH (>10), which is underexplored as a direct carbonation condition. This study investigated a wide range of initial pH (3–14) to elucidate the roles of pH and alkalinity during the direct carbonation behavior of olivine at a high temperature (185 °C). Despite the expected negative correlation between pH and olivine dissolution kinetics, this study revealed that alkaline pH conditions significantly enhance direct carbonation kinetics. The study also determined the effects of initial total alkalinity and the roles of different alkalinity sources, offering valuable perspectives for estimating direct carbonation behavior across a wide range of reaction conditions.

papers.title: Harnessing the Microbial Iron Redox Chain: Liquid Organic Acid Fertilizer and EDTA-Fe Drive Unexpected Cadmium Passivation in Alkaline Upland Soils
papers.abstract: Abstract The immobilization of cadmium (Cd) in weakly alkaline upland soils, a major agricultural system in northern China, remains a challenge. This study examined whether liquid organic acid (OA) fertilizer and EDTA-Fe could stimulate Fe redox to stabilize Cd. OA fertilizer (active ingredients: citric acid, lactic acid, and glucose) induced microbial Fe(III) reduction and acidification within 1 day, shifting Cd from Fe/Mn-oxide and organic fractions to exchangeable and carbonate forms. Iron reduction and acidification contributed 52.0–55.8% and 44.2–48.0% of Cd activation, respectively. Subsequent Fe(II) oxidation over 60 days reimmobilized Cd into Fe/Mn-oxide and residual fractions. Adding EDTA-Fe enhanced Fe(III) reduction (raising Cd activation by 35.4%) while slowing Fe(II) oxidation and increasing Cd passivation by 31.8%. Such passivation was driven by newly formed secondary Fe oxides and Fe–Al–Si minerals, and ceased when Fe(II) oxidation was inhibited. Simulations supported Cd association with Fe–Al–Si phases, and EDTA-Fe enhanced immobilization via surface complexation/coprecipitation. Unlike paddy soils, Cd dynamics in alkaline soils are distinct despite both being Fe redox-driven, underscoring the need for alkaline-specific strategies. This approach works across diverse soils (pH 7.41–8.43; Cd 1.33–30.06 mg kg–1), reducing available Cd by 19.4–51.6%, and provides new insights into Fe redox-controlled Cd stabilization in upland soils.

papers.title: Single-Cell Insights into Virus–Microbe Interactions in Emerging Contaminant Degradation
papers.abstract: Abstract Viruses are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of microbial ecology, yet their roles in pollutant degradation remain largely unexplored. Here, we integrate Raman-activated cell sorting–stable isotope probing (RACS-SIP) and single-cell genomics to elucidate virus–microbe interactions underlying methylnaphthalene biodegradation in petroleum-contaminated soils. Microcosm experiments demonstrated up to 80% removal of methylnaphthalene within 36 days, accompanied by pronounced shifts in microbial and viral communities. Correlation analyses suggested potential virus–host associations, with Ochrobactrum and an unclassified Caudoviricetes phage emerging as key contributors to degradation. RACS-SIP enabled in situ identification and isolation of active degraders, and single-cell genomic analysis indicated that viral auxiliary metabolic genes, including methyltransferases, aldehyde dehydrogenases, and decarboxylases, may complement host pathways for the multistep conversion of methylnaphthalene to naphthalene. Subsequent mineralization occurs through canonical catechol and gentisate pathways encoded by the host genome. This study provides preliminary evidence that viruses may act as metabolic collaborators rather than passive parasites in pollutant degradation, potentially enhancing host metabolic capacity and influencing biodegradation outcomes. Beyond revealing a virus-inclusive metabolic network, the RACS-SIP framework overcomes key limitations of traditional metagenomic methods by resolving virus–host linkages at the single-cell level. These findings broaden our understanding of viral ecological functions and highlight novel leverage points for bioremediation technologies targeting emerging contaminants.

papers.title: Cross-Radical Knowledge Sharing via Graph Neural Networks for Unified Prediction of Aqueous Organic Contaminant Second-Order Radical Reaction Rate Constants
papers.abstract: Abstract Selecting among hydroxyl (HO•), sulfate (SO4•–), and carbonate (CO3•–) radical advanced oxidation processes requires reliable intrinsic second-order rate constants, yet the corresponding curated data sets contain 1250, 493, and 248 records, respectively. Reframing this imbalance as a cross-radical few-shot learning problem, we introduce maco, a radical-conditioned graph neural network that uses shared molecular representation learning, oxidant/pH cross-attention, residual adapters, and a two-stage curriculum to transfer structural knowledge from the data-rich HO• task to the lower-data SO4•– and CO3•– tasks. On similarity-stratified held-out tests, maco achieved R2 = 0.855 (95% CI 0.711–0.906) for SO4•– and 0.815 (0.269–0.944) for CO3•–; on the more stringent scaffold-disjoint Murcko tests, the corresponding values were 0.652 (0.447–0.779) and 0.715 (0.500–0.825). Temperature-conditioned sensitivity analyses showed no statistically discernible generalization gain under the highly asymmetric temperature coverage. Functional-group attention analysis identified radical- and pH-dependent reactive-site patterns, while applicability-domain assessment and ensemble uncertainty quantified prediction reliability for target-radical scaffold-novel contaminants. maco provides a reproducible screening input for prioritising radical–contaminant measurements and process-specific evaluation. A browser-accessible WebUI further provides single-compound predictions, uncertainty estimates, and applicability-domain flags without local installation.

papers.title: Methanotroph-Derived Reactive Oxygen Species Facilitate Arsenic Oxidation in Paddy Soils
papers.abstract: Abstract Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are increasingly recognized as important oxidants in soil redox processes, with microbially produced ROS contributing broadly to elemental transformations. Given the active methane oxidation in paddy soils, methanotrophs have considerable potential to generate ROS yet their role in As(III) oxidation remains unclear. Here, we identify methanotroph-derived ROS as an important yet previously overlooked pathway for As(III) oxidation in paddy soils. Soil microcosm experiments and pure culture experiments revealed that methane oxidation enhanced ROS-mediated As(III) oxidation, with H2O2 identified as the dominant ROS. Inhibitor assays and functional gene analyses indicated that oxygen activation and respiratory electron transfer were closely associated with ROS generation during methane oxidation. These findings reveal methanotroph-derived ROS as a distinct route contributing to As(III) oxidation beyond dedicated arsenite oxidases. By revealing an overlooked connection between methane metabolism and arsenic transformation, this work expands our understanding of arsenic biogeochemistry and provides a conceptual basis for the coordinated mitigation of methane emissions and arsenic toxicity in agroecosystems.

papers.title: Is Electro-Stimulation Always Effective for Methanogenesis? A Holistic Assessment of Electric Potential and Current Effects in Highly Conductive Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Electro-stimulated anaerobic digestion (EAD) typically relies on voltage-only regulation, neglecting the impacts of the associated response current, particularly in highly conductive systems. Herein, we investigated an EAD system for treating iron-containing sludge digestate. Unexpectedly, under appropriate applied voltages of 0.9 to 1.2 V, the high conductivity triggered excessive currents, which subsequently inhibited methanogenesis. By decoupling the dual potential–current effects, integrated with metatranscriptomics analysis, we revealed that excessive currents induced severe, localized oxidative stress on anodic biofilms (up to 2.3-fold of the CF group) and hindered carbon metabolism. Concurrently, lower cathodic potentials triggered microenvironmental alkalinization, accelerating calcite and ankerite deposition, which increased the mass transfer resistance by up to 1.4-fold. Consequently, the positive biological effects of electro-stimulation (e.g., Geobacter enrichment, upregulated methanogenic genes) were counterbalanced by these current-induced physical and biochemical barriers. This study highlights the necessity of comanaging electric potential and current when deploying electro-microbial technologies in highly conductive systems toward energy-efficient AD facilities.

papers.title: Maternal Epigenetic Signatures Linking Prenatal Serum PFAS Concentrations to Birth Size in an African American Maternal–Child Cohort
papers.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposures have been linked to reduced birth size, but the underlying epigenetic mechanisms remain unclear. Among 296 mother–infant dyads in the Atlanta African American Maternal–Child Cohort (2016–2020), early pregnancy maternal blood samples (8–14 weeks) were processed for serum PFAS assessment and blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) DNA methylation profiling. We assessed birth size using sex-specific birth weight z-scores (BWZ) and small-for-gestational-age (SGA) status. Individual and mixture PFAS methylation associations were estimated by using robust generalized linear regression and quantile g-computation. We also conducted differentially methylated region (DMR), gene ontology, sex-specific, and exploratory mediation analyses. Overall, 132 CpGs were associated with at least one PFAS (FDR < 0.05), including 34, 60, 32, and 10 linked with PFHxS, PFOS, PFOA, and PFNA, respectively. PFOS showed the largest effects and appeared to drive the mixture associations. Six CpGs (annotated to EVA1A, FCRL1, CTIF, ABHD12, and WDYHV1) were associated with PFAS levels and birth size indicators. We identified 2–9 DMRs associated with individual PFASs and their mixture. Sex-specific PFAS methylation associations were observed. The PFAS-associated genes are involved in the inflammatory response, immune activity, and lipid homeostasis. Prenatal serum PFAS concentrations were associated with alterations in maternal DNA methylation, which in turn were associated with infant birth size.

papers.title: Economic and environmental assessment of waste-derived aviation fuels using agent-based modeling under carbon pricing
Innovative synergy coefficient revealed the negative PM2.5–O3 synergistic pollution in China over the past decade
From thermal heterogeneity to equitable heating loads allocation in district heating systems
High-efficiency solar-driven atmospheric water harvesting enabled by foamed hydrogel adsorbents
Researchers as governance actors: How scientific knowledge becomes actionable in transdisciplinary water projects
Evaluating the impact of BRI toward greener energy and carbon neutrality
papers.abstract: Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has primarily been studied for its economic benefits; its role in promoting greener energy transitions and carbon neutrality goals is not well explored. This study examines the effects of BRI across 90 BRI countries from 1995 to 2021 with a focus on greener energy transition and carbon neutrality. Quantile Treatment Effect (QTE) models are used to compare the effectiveness of BRI across quantile levels and groups of countries. In general, results show evidence that BRI has effectively reduced CO 2 emissions and enhanced renewable energy consumption, with the effects being more pronounced in countries that exhibit high CO 2 and renewable energy consumption. The developed countries and countries with high renewable energy potential and high pollution levels are most benefitted from joining BRI. The impact of BRI in the developing and low-income countries is less prominent. In summary, the BRI tends to create the most significant environmental benefits in countries that already have a relatively high level of development, allowing them to leverage new technologies and investments for further decarbonization.

papers.title: Manure Composting as a Strategy to Mitigate Antibiotic Resistance Dissemination in Agricultural Systems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Livestock manure is a valuable agricultural resource but may introduce antibiotic residues and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) into the environment. This review critically evaluates the fate of antibiotics and ARGs during manure composting and identifies the principal factors controlling their attenuation. It integrates composting‐system configuration and phase‐specific operating conditions with antibiotic properties, microbial‐host succession, extracellular DNA, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), post‐application risks, and alternative manure‐treatment technologies. Composting can reduce many antibiotic residues by 80%–90% or more, although apparent removal may reflect degradation, transformation, sorption, or reduced extractability and remains strongly compound‐ and process‐dependent. ARG responses are more variable and often non‐linear. Sustained thermophilic conditions can reduce ARG‐carrying microorganisms and MGEs, but selected genes may persist or rebound during maturation because of microbial recolonization, residual selection pressure, extracellular DNA persistence, and horizontal gene transfer (HGT). Temperature and exposure duration, aeration, moisture, C:N ratio, bulking materials, biochar, and microbial inoculants are therefore key determinants of treatment performance. Composting substantially mitigates antimicrobial‐resistance risks but does not guarantee complete elimination of transmissible ARGs. Standardized monitoring, full‐scale validation, and long‐term assessment of soil and crop compartments are required to support safe agricultural use of composted manure.

papers.title: Asynchronous Response of Plant Productivity and Soil Aggregate Nutrients to Grazing Exclusion Duration in Alpine Steppe
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Grazing exclusion is a critical restoration measure for degraded alpine steppe ecosystems. However, research remains limited on the key factors influencing soil aggregates that affect plant productivity and the mechanisms influencing nutrient distribution across aggregates of different size fractions during long‐term grazing exclusion. We examined alpine steppe ecosystems in northern Tibet with a space‐for‐time substitution approach to analyze dynamic changes in plant productivity and soil aggregate nutrients across different exclusion durations (0, 2, 6, 13, and 18 years). Community aboveground biomass and Stipa purpurea biomass initially increased and peaked after 6 years of exclusion, followed by a gradual decline. In contrast, long‐term exclusion (≥ 13 years) significantly increased the proportion of soil macroaggregates and their associated organic carbon, nitrate nitrogen, and available phosphorus contents. Spearman correlation analysis revealed that nitrate nitrogen stored in macroaggregates was negatively correlated with plant productivity. These results indicate an asynchronous response between vegetation recovery and soil aggregate nutrient dynamics during ecological restoration. Plant productivity recovered rapidly in the short term but did not synchronize with improvements in soil structure and nutrient pools. Although prolonged enclosure enhanced total soil nutrient stocks, nutrients became increasingly physically protected within stable macroaggregates, reducing their accessibility to plant roots. Soil aggregate‐scale nutrient distribution regulates alpine steppe productivity under grazing exclusion. These findings deepen our understanding of alpine steppe ecosystem restoration dynamics and the coordination of ecological conservation with sustainable pastoral development.

papers.title: Eternal chattel? Or, how to live in a moveable house when liberal time isn’t enough
papers.abstract: Examining the ways that a redistributive politics of possession is haunted by Lockean moral claims regarding land, this paper is a conceptual exploration of the entanglement of land possession and race as mercurial artifacts of colonialism. Thinking from the Caribbean reveals the need for a mode of storying that exposes and undoes the colonial boundary-making on land and bodies that produced these artifacts. I explore this first through the contradictory capacity of moveable houses in Jamaica to stay put because they can move. Rejecting the habitually truncated narration of Caribbean histories and places, I then put the wood house in relation to deeper timescales and broader geographies of archipelagic placemaking. In doing so, I consider the wood house as a guide towards the commensurability of anticolonial projects to live land otherwise. Ultimately, the house’s capacity for motion signals not merely the power of (dis)possession, but an ongoing relational potentiality.
papers.journal_name: Environment and Planning C: Politics and Space

papers.title: Terrain, visibility and temporalities of mountain autonomy
papers.abstract: This article explores the role of terrain in configuring political boundaries among local communities, market forces, and the state. Built upon fieldwork conducted between 2021 and 2024, the article addresses the role of terrain volume as a constitutive agent shaping, particularly in the central mountain areas of Chile, a layer of political negotiation between practices carried out by residents—especially drovers or cowboys (arrieros) of smaller livestock and landowners—and the state’s mandate. This article pays attention to residents' practices of space navigation and their use of terrain to create temporary autonomy from the state. Autonomy here is attained by people keeping themselves at the edge of the state, thus eluding public officials as illustrated by new forms of visibility arising from the interaction between pumas and cattle breeders. Local spatial practices and terrain knowledge are key to modulating whether residents interact with state's heteronomy or enact autonomy. We conclude by showing how mobility is a defining feature in the creation of alter-spaces and regulating the affordance that people have in the face of the state and market’s presence and their environmental effects.

papers.title: Motivating job seekers. A field experiment
JUE insight: Soft infrastructure and the location choice of multinational firms: Evidence from Japanese investment in the United States in the 1980s
EXPRESS: The Humanizing Power of Accents in Voicebots: When Accent-Based Humanization Increases User Engagement
papers.abstract: Given that consumers often exhibit resistance toward algorithmic systems, firms face challenges in encouraging engagement with voicebots. In this paper, we find that users’ engagement with voicebots may be enhanced by endowing these tools with non-standard accents that deviate from “standard” pronunciation. Across a range of accents, languages, genders, and contexts, our data suggest that voicebots communicating with non-standard accents make the concept of human diversity salient in the users’ minds. As a result, voicebots communicating with non-standard accents are more readily anthropomorphized. This effect translates into greater preference for the non-standard accented voicebot in customer service settings, stronger support for startups leveraging accented vs. unaccented voicebots, higher willingness to pay for monthly subscriptions, and a greater likelihood of opting in to receive future updates and communications. Consistent with our theory, however, these effects do not hold when the anthropomorphism effect is either overridden by other cues or is undesirable for the consumer. Together, this work highlights the benefits of accented speech in improving human-AI interactions. We also hope that it sparks further investigation into factors that make technology more readily accepted by consumers.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Infinite-Scrolling vs. Pagination: The Impact of Interface Layouts on Product Returns
papers.abstract: Interface layout, although a fundamental and prominent aspect inherent to online interfaces, has received limited attention in consumer research. This paper explores how the two major types of interface layout (infinite scrolling and pagination) influence consumers’ product return behavior in the context of free returns, a standard policy on e-commerce sites. Across five studies featuring real websites, we show that an infinite-scrolling (versus paginated) layout increases consumers’ tendency to return purchased products. This effect occurs because infinite scrolling dampens consumers’ perceived navigational control over the website, which impairs their choice closure after making decisions, thereby increasing product return intentions. We also identify both theoretically relevant and managerially important moderators and interventions to mitigate this adverse effect of infinite scrolling, such as incorporating navigational aids (e.g., displaying sequence numbers alongside), providing affirmative feedback, and accounting for the cost of product returns. This research not only contributes to the literature on interface effects, website navigation, and product returns but also provides applied insights for marketing practitioners.

papers.title: Why Design Thinking Needs a Responsibility Reboot
papers.abstract: User-centered design methods focus on giving users what they seem to want. But approaches like design thinking can lead practitioners to ignore potential harms or fail to adequately consider ethical design principles. Companies can be innovative while minimizing such risks by putting mission and values at the forefront of the design process, being mindful of how KPIs or other incentives may influence design choices, and pausing to consider a product’s potential broad impact before scaling.

papers.title: Peer Versus Top Management Communication and Energy‐Saving Behavioural Intentions in the Workplace: The Moderating Role of Personalised Framing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Employee engagement is pivotal for corporate sustainability, yet the role of information design in internal employee communication remains under‐specified. Drawing on Construal Level Theory, this study examines whether the effect of information sender (peer vs top management communication) on employees' energy‐saving behavioural intentions depends on information framing (personalised vs generic information). In a 2 × 2 experiment with UK employees ( N = 264), personalisation significantly increased energy‐saving behavioural intentions relative to generic information. Sender differences alone were not statistically reliable, and the sender × framing interaction was not significant. A theory‐driven preplanned contrast showed that personalised peer information produced the highest behavioural intentions. Sender and framing are both theoretically social‐distance cues, yet they do not function equivalently: framing reliably shifted intentions on its own, whereas sender did not, potentially because sender is confounded with other variables such as organisational legitimacy. Practically, the findings indicate that lightweight personalisation offers a modest but scalable lever for strengthening energy‐saving behavioural intentions at work.

papers.title: Digital Pathways to Net Zero: Dissecting the Nonlinear Dynamics Between Digital Transformation and Urban Decarbonization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Effectively managing urban decarbonization in rapidly developing economies is a critical environmental governance challenge of our time. Failing to integrate digital transformation with sustainability strategies exposes structural inefficiencies in urban planning, demanding strategic foresight and institutional resolve to align economic activity with global climate targets. This study examines the dynamic, nonlinear impacts of digital transformation on urban carbon mitigation. Building on ecological modernization theory, it advances a digital ecological modernization perspective, conceptualizing information and communication technology (ICT) as both technological and institutional capital that supports data‐driven environmental governance. To provide actionable insights for environmental managers and policymakers, the empirical strategy employs advanced machine‐learning‐based models to evaluate ICT‐driven CO 2 mitigation across a comprehensive panel of 285 Chinese cities from 2005 to 2023. The results indicate that ICT diffusion significantly and robustly mitigates CO 2 emissions. Mechanism analysis reveals that ICT lowers emissions through three core channels: Improved energy efficiency, stronger green technological innovation, and enhanced green human capital, consistent with scale, composition, and technique effects. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis reveals that the CO 2 mitigation effect of ICT is stronger in high‐resource‐intensive cities; in terms of development level, ICT significantly reduces CO 2 emissions in highly developed and emerging cities, but its mitigation effect in less‐developed cities is statistically insignificant. Although the empirical focus on China limits cross‐national comparison, it provides granular intra‐regional insights. Strategically, the findings necessitate expediting digital infrastructure in less‐developed cities to unlock mitigation potential and designing region‐specific policies that reflect local industrial structures. This study makes a significant contribution by empirically validating the digital ecological modernization framework. It demonstrates how digital transformation acts as a strategic catalyst for low‐carbon development, providing a scalable blueprint for managing urban decarbonization in emerging economies.

papers.title: From Green Human Resource Management to Green Creativity: Exploring the Influences of Pride, Meaningfulness, and Environmental Support
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The climate crisis is forcing organizations to adopt strategies that mitigate environmental impact. This makes green human resource management (GHRM) essential. However, GHRM does not necessarily translate directly into employees' green creativity (GC), and further research is needed to explain when and how employees internalize green HR practices as a basis for sustainability‐oriented creativity. Drawing on social identity theory and self‐determination theory, this article examines how GHRM promotes GC through the dual mediating roles of organizational pride (OP) and meaningfulness through work (MTW), conceptualized as two psychosocial routes of internalization. It also investigates how green organizational culture (GOC) and green mindfulness (GM) moderate these relationships in different organizational contexts. Two studies were conducted using dual data sources, comprising 214 supervisor–employee dyads from ISO 14001 certified companies in Study 1 and 201 supervisor–employee dyads from noncertified companies in Study 2, totaling 415 dyads. The findings show that GHRM was not directly associated with GC, but operated indirectly through OP and MTW. GOC strengthened the effects of GHRM on these psychosocial mechanisms in certified companies, whereas GM did not moderate the relationships between OP, MTW, and GC in noncertified companies. These results refine current understanding of GHRM by showing that its creative potential depends on employees' psychosocial internalization and on coherent organizational support.

papers.title: From Awareness to Ecosystemic Transformation: How Artificial Intelligence Enables Firms' Transition to a Circular Economy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to aid firms' transition toward a circular economy ( CE ). However, empirical research on how small and medium‐sized enterprises use AI to support this transition is limited. Using the Gioia methodology, we analyze 25 in‐depth, semi‐structured interviews with top managers of companies within a local ecosystem. The findings reveal a five‐stage pathway through which companies use AI in transitioning to a CE : circular awareness and reflection, lean optimization, partial circularity, organizational CE strategic embeddedness, and CE (eco)systemic shift. These stages represent an evolutionary process, with the first stage indicating limited use of AI and the final stage full AI integration. Companies in our sample were unable to reach the fourth and fifth stages (representing the highest integration levels). Our research extends CE and digital transformation literature by revealing how AI adoption shapes firms' strategic, operational, and ecosystemic shifts toward circularity and ecosystem collaboration.

papers.title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Conditions and Sustainable Value Creation: Predictive Evidence From Knowledge‐Intensive Ventures in São Paulo, Brazil
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Entrepreneurial ecosystems (EEs) are systems shaping innovation and sustainable development, yet limited evidence exists on the relative predictive contribution of their components to sustainable value creation. This study examines associations between six EE dimensions and environmental, social and economic value creation among 245 knowledge‐intensive ventures supported by the PIPE programme of the São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP), Brazil. Using cross‐sectional, self‐reported survey data, composite indices were constructed through the CRITIC method and analysed with machine‐learning models, Monte Carlo repeated holdout validation and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Regression performance was modest, and classification performance was moderate. Within the selected predictors and this sample, cultural conditions showed the highest mean absolute SHAP importance across all outcomes, whereas the remaining dimensions varied. These results provide context‐bound predictive evidence, not causal inference or a universal hierarchy. The study contributes an interpretable framework for comparing ecosystem dimensions in a specific Brazilian regional and institutional setting.
authors: Gustavo Hermínio Salati Marcondes de Moraes

papers.title: From bad to worse: customer mistreatment and service sabotage across encounters
papers.abstract: Purpose Customer mistreatment is a significant issue in both practical and academic contexts, especially in the service industry. Drawing on the stressor–emotion model, this study aims to use a sequential two-encounter field design to test the lagged effects of customer mistreatment on service sabotage at Time 1 and Time 2. The study also explores the moderating effects of personal controls (i.e. conscientiousness and emotional stability) and situational control (empowerment) on the above relationships. Design/methodology/approach The analytical sample consisted of 190 frontline employees matched with 380 customer evaluations across two consecutive service encounters. Data were gathered in multiple stages: frontline employees first completed questionnaires on demographics and personal traits, and then, immediately after service encounters. This procedure was repeated for a subsequent service encounter with a second customer to capture multiple interactions for each employee. Findings The findings indicate that emotional exhaustion mediates the relationship between customer mistreatment and service sabotage at both Time 1 and Time 2. Furthermore, empowerment weakens the positive relationship between customer mistreatment and emotional exhaustion, whereas conscientiousness and emotional stability attenuate the indirect effect of customer mistreatment on service sabotage through emotional exhaustion. Practical implications The findings underscore the importance of safeguarding frontline employees from the detrimental effects of customer mistreatment. Hospitality managers should foster employee empowerment and provide adequate organizational support to help employees cope with demanding customer interactions. At the same time, managers should recognize conscientiousness and emotional stability as valuable personal resources that may buffer the effects of emotional exhaustion and reduce the risk of subsequent service sabotage. By integrating these organizational and individual-level approaches, hospitality organizations can mitigate the adverse spillover of customer mistreatment across successive service encounters and, ultimately, preserve service quality. Originality/value This study advances understanding of boundary conditions by simultaneously examining individual traits and an organizational factor. The findings reveal that conscientiousness and emotional stability significantly buffer the indirect effects of mistreatment through emotional exhaustion, whereas empowerment primarily mitigates the direct impact of mistreatment on exhaustion but does not alter the exhaustion–sabotage pathway. By integrating temporal dynamics, emotional processes and multilevel moderators, this research provides a more comprehensive and realistic account of how customer mistreatment unfolds in frontline service contexts.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: Too little time, too much to do: how time poverty undermines employees’ proactive service behavior
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the relationship between time poverty and hotel employees’ proactive service behavior by identifying future self-continuity as a mediator and competitive climate as a moderator. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a multimethod design to test the hypotheses. Study 1 uses a recall-based experiment with 220 hotel employees to establish causality. Study 2 draws on a two-wave field survey of 298 employees from five hotels in China to enhance ecological validity and test the boundary conditions. Findings The findings reveal that time poverty significantly undermines hotel employees’ proactive service behavior, thereby establishing the mediating role of future self-continuity. Furthermore, competitive climate moderates this effect such that the indirect negative effect becomes stronger when competitive climate is high. Practical implications This study helps hotel managers understand the impact of time poverty on employees and offers practical guidance for monitoring and alleviating it through employee-centered scheduling, workload redistribution and protected time, thereby sustaining employees’ proactive service behavior. Originality/value This study examines hospitality employees’ time poverty by shifting attention from the tourists’ temporal experiences, which have dominated prior research, to employees’ chronic scarcity. Moving beyond the affective and cognitive reactions emphasized in earlier studies, it reveals an identity-based mechanism grounded in self-control theory. It further identifies competitive climate as an organizational boundary condition that managers can redesign or reduce to contain the behavioral costs of time poverty.

papers.title: Entrepreneurial bricolage in the branding efforts of international new ventures
Fueling service initiative: how AI assimilation shapes employees' proactive service behavior through AI crafting
papers.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping how employees engage in service work. However, few studies have examined how AI assimilation (i.e. the extent to which AI technology is integrated and routinized in work activities and processes) affects employees' proactive behaviors. This study investigates how the breadth and depth of AI assimilation shape proactive service behavior, examines the mediating roles of approach and avoidance AI crafting, and tests job autonomy as a moderator. It further examines whether employees exhibit higher proactive service behavior when these two crafting strategies are used in a more balanced way. Design/methodology/approach Based on Conservation Of Resources (COR) theory, this study uses paired-sample survey data from 234 employee-manager pairs in China's service industry. Stepwise regression, polynomial regression, and response surface analysis are applied to test the hypotheses. Findings The results show that both the depth and breadth of AI assimilation positively influence proactive service behavior. Approach AI crafting mediates both relationships, while avoidance AI crafting only mediates the relationship between the breadth of AI assimilation and proactive service behavior. Employees exhibit the highest level of proactive service behavior when using both crafting strategies in balance, indicating that approach and avoidance AI crafting are complementary. Furthermore, job autonomy strengthens the positive effect of AI assimilation on approach AI crafting, while weakening its positive effect on avoidance AI crafting. Originality/value This study advances service operations management research by shifting attention from AI adoption to AI assimilation and specifying the mechanism through which AI assimilation shapes frontline employees' proactive service behavior. It also challenges the traditional dichotomous view in job crafting by proposing that approach and avoidance AI crafting may be complementary.

When Bad Feels Better: How Negative Online Brand Engagement Transforms Into Consumer Happiness
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Brands are increasingly prioritizing consumer happiness alongside profit, yet research offers limited guidance on fostering this in negative consumer‐brand contexts. Drawing on the broaden‐and‐build theory, this work models consumer pathways from anti‐consumption and disidentification to negative cognition and affection, to constructive and destructive online behaviors and ultimately happiness. Perceived brand functional underperformance moderates these relationships. The two‐phase exploratory sequential design has a qualitative phase for model development (Studies 1 & 2) and a quantitative phase for model testing through multigroup analysis (Study 3). The findings reveal that anti‐consumption solely predicts negative cognition, while disidentification predicts both negative cognition and affection. Cognition drives constructive and destructive behaviors, whereas affection primarily fuels destructive behaviors. Both behaviors predict happiness, with destructive behaviors being stronger. The study advances understanding of the psychological mechanisms that paradoxically turn negative interactions into enhanced life happiness and identifies severity‐based boundary conditions with implications for recovery design.

Small Polity, Hybrid Administration, International Research: Public Administration in Switzerland
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Switzerland presents a most peculiar political system whose institutional idiosyncrasies shape not only the practice of public administration but also the scientific study thereof. This country study presents the development and state of both public administration as practice and Public Administration as a scholarly discipline. It argues that both are largely determined by three properties of Switzerland as a political context and field of study: Semi‐direct democracy turns the administration into an important political actor. The “Milizsystem” (Switzerland's tradition of non‐professionalized, part‐time public engagement) enables hybrid careers between the public and private sectors and produces a structurally weaker political class that the professional administration regularly outmaneuvers. And the small size of the country has pushed the discipline toward international orientation while simultaneously entangling researchers with their object of study. Taken together, the Swiss case illustrates how political institutions do not merely constrain public administration but fundamentally constitute it.

papers.title: From cross-border power links to a digitalized regional market: A critical review of the ASEAN power grid as a catalyst for decarbonization
papers.abstract: This article presents a critical review of the ASEAN Power Grid (APG) and its evolving role in supporting regional electricity integration, renewable energy deployment, energy security, and decarbonization across Southeast Asia. The study examines the transition from bilateral cross-border interconnections toward multilateral electricity trading and a more digitally integrated regional electricity market. Based on a PRISMA-guided review of 108 publications, the paper integrates infrastructure development, renewable energy potential, institutional coordination, financing, and digitalization within a unified analytical framework. It introduces the reliability–sovereignty trade-off, a three-layer digitalization architecture, and a dual-pillar energy security framework based on climate resilience and strategic autonomy. The review also compares ASEAN with European and African regional electricity integration models and proposes a phased strategic roadmap toward deeper regional market integration through 2050. The findings highlight the importance of geographic renewable-energy complementarity, cross-border transmission expansion, digital market coupling, AI-based forecasting, HVDC technologies, regulatory coordination, and innovative financing mechanisms for transforming the ASEAN Power Grid into a flexible, resilient, and low-carbon regional electricity system. Published in: Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, Volume 244 (2027), Article 117533.DOI: 10.1016/j.rser.2026.117533.

papers.title: A Continuous Virus Aerosol-into-Liquid Sampler (VAiLS) Integrating Twin-Vortex Condensation Growth and Wet-Cyclone Enrichment
papers.abstract: Abstract Airborne virus surveillance requires sampling methods that efficiently transfer nanoscale virions into a small-volume liquid while preserving infectivity. Here, we develop a continuous Virus Aerosol-into-Liquid Sampler (VAiLS) that integrates a twin-vortex condensation growth unit (CGU) with a wet cyclone (w-Cyc) to enlarge virus-sized aerosols into micrometer droplets and continuously concentrate them into a hydrosol sample, defined here as the particle-containing aqueous suspension produced by transferring aerosol particles into the w-Cyc liquid film. The CGU combines a low-temperature preconditioner (∼5 °C) with a wick-wetted growth chamber (Tg = 20–60 °C) to generate supersaturation at a high sampling flow rate (16 L/min), and the downstream w-Cyc collects the grown droplets via a stable liquid film. Using KCl nanoparticles as model aerosols, the number-weighted total collection efficiency increased from 7.3% (w-Cyc only) to 31.0, 64.4, and 70.4% at Tg = 20, 40, and 60 °C, respectively, with no appreciable dependence on inlet relative humidity (16.8–71.8%). For airborne viruses, VAiLS achieved maximum collection efficiencies at Tg = 40 °C (MS2: 93 ± 0.6%; phi 6: 90 ± 2.1%) and produced much higher infectious concentrations than a BioSampler (3.9 × 103-fold for MS2 and 1.2 × 103-fold for phi 6). Relative virus viability remained >92% for most conditions, decreasing only for phi 6 at Tg = 60 °C (5.8 ± 4.37%). These results demonstrate that VAiLS enables high-flow, high-enrichment, infectivity-preserving sampling compatible with plaque assays and qPCR.

papers.title: Nitration of Urban PM2.5: A Hidden Driver of Enhanced Human Inflammation
papers.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen oxides (NOx) are well-established air pollutants that have been epidemiologically linked to adverse outcomes. However, their complex chemical reactivity obscures the mechanisms through which specific nitrogenous species are responsible for observed health risks. We hypothesize that NOx-driven nitration processes generate nitrated aromatic compounds (NACs) as potential health threat contributors. To test this, we performed a longitudinal, population-based exposomic study in Beijing. ∼1000 NACs were characterized from personal PM2.5, with median concentrations higher than those of traditional polycyclic aromatics (PACs, represented by PAHs). Remarkably, secondary NACs, particularly those formed via aqueous-phase nitration and represented by 3-/5-nitrosalicylic acids, accounted for over 70% of total NAC exposure in summer. Their associations with lung and systemic inflammatory biomarkers of IL-6 were 2.1–232 times stronger than those of PAHs and gaseous NOx. Our findings provided a new perspective for considering secondary nitration transformations in urban air quality standards.
