papers.title: High-growth firms and their habitats
papers.abstract: Abstract We examine how the geography of entrepreneurial quality differs from the geography of entrepreneurial quantity by analyzing spatial variation in high-growth firms (HGFs) across Swedish municipalities during 2002–2022. Using longitudinal firm-level data matched to survey measures of local business climate, we compare the determinants of start-up rates and firm scaling. Standard supply- and demand-side factors — population size, human capital and economic structure — are associated with both outcomes, though not uniformly. In contrast, local business climate, capturing entrepreneurs’ assessments of how local authorities function in practice, is a substantially stronger predictor of HGFs than of start-ups. The association is economically meaningful and varies with local economic structure. The findings point to a micro-level mechanism that may link local framework conditions to aggregate outcomes: interactions between growth-oriented firms and local institutions during scaling. These patterns suggest that local institutional conditions are related not only to how many firms are created, but to which firms are able to grow.

papers.title: Collective sensemaking as a mechanism of sustainable entrepreneurial ecosystem emergence under institutional fragility
Distributed signal production in entrepreneurial ecosystems: evidence from Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa
papers.abstract: Abstract Entrepreneurial ecosystem research has established that ecosystems influence venture development through networks, institutions, and support organizations, yet it offers limited explanation of how ecosystems shape the evaluative processes through which ventures gain access to finance and markets. This limitation is particularly consequential in emerging economies, where institutional conditions make conventional indicators of venture quality difficult to interpret, increasing uncertainty for resource gatekeepers. We address this gap by examining how entrepreneurial ecosystems shape venture credibility when the institutional conditions that normally make entrepreneurial signals legible, enforceable, and consequential are weak. Drawing on an abductive qualitative analysis of 174 semi-structured interviews with entrepreneurs, commercial banks, development finance institutions, corporate buyers, incubator and accelerator leaders, university entrepreneurship programmes, mentors, and public agencies across Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa, we develop a process model of distributed signal production. We show that entrepreneurial ecosystems function as distributed evaluative infrastructures that construct the evidentiary basis through which venture quality becomes credible to resource gatekeepers. Ecosystem actors accomplish this through three mechanisms: institutional signal substitution, structured signal amplification, and signal brokerage and conversion. These mechanisms explain how ecosystems construct, strengthen, and coordinate venture credibility while revealing why credible signals do not always translate into resource access under conditions of institutional weakness. Our findings advance entrepreneurial ecosystem literature by explaining how ecosystems shape evaluative processes rather than simply providing resources, extend signaling theory by demonstrating that signal production is distributed across heterogeneous ecosystem actors, and show how institutional conditions influence the conversion of credible signals into entrepreneurial opportunities.

papers.title: Discovering early signals of technological opportunities: Insights from interdisciplinary innovation
Objects as Means of Sustainability Knowledge Co-Creation: Working on Value-Laden Issues Across the Research-Practice Boundary
papers.abstract: Abstract The negative sustainability impacts of business keep escalating despite the profusion of research-based evidence regarding problems and solution pathways. Sustainability knowledge is complex and value-laden, thus often difficult to act upon. Co-creation between researchers and practitioners stands as a fruitful means of making sustainability knowledge more actionable, yet we lack insight into what motivates and facilitates sustainability knowledge co-creation. Boundary objects, which assist collaboration among diverse groups, can facilitate knowledge co-creation between researchers and practitioners, but little is known of their workings in the context of tackling value-laden sustainability issues. Based on rich qualitative data from two empirical cases, we examine how boundary objects motivate and facilitate knowledge co-creation between practitioners and researchers, helping to make sustainability knowledge more actionable. Our analysis illuminates three main dynamics whereby boundary objects do so: boundary objects initiate dialogue on complex issues through conveying clarity, provide a physical realm for co-creation in a value-laden domain, and motivate participation despite ethical vulnerability. These insights elaborate and challenge previous research regarding the boundary object ambiguity-clarity tension in the context of sustainability knowledge co-creation among diverse actor groups. Specifically, our findings foreground boundary object clarity, rather than ambiguity, in helping to initiate dialogue on complex sustainability issues. Furthermore, our analysis extends understanding of participant motivations to engage in sustainability knowledge co-creation, indicating that objects provide instrumental value and more intrinsic learning value, as well as help parties be with ethical vulnerability induced by knowledge co-creation around value-laden issues.

papers.title: Explaining user-orientation in public service delivery networks: configurations of network structure, process, and context
papers.abstract: This study explores configurations of structural, process, and contextual conditions associated with high user-orientation in public service delivery networks. Drawing on Public Service Logic, we conceptualize user-orientation and connect it with interorganizational network research. We examine six conditions and apply fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis to data from sixty networks. We identify five pathways. Across these pathways, collaboration intensity and organizational simplicity consistently emerge, underscoring the importance of process factors alongside structural conditions. Network size clarifies the distinct roles of centralization and density. One pathway combines high centralization and high density with high user-orientation, nuancing prevailing views about their simultaneous presence.

papers.title: Fertility-related knowledge and childbearing attitudes among female survivors of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a cross-sectional study
Spatial organization and coordinated development of offshore wind industrial chains under governance decentralization: evidence from China's coastal provinces
papers.abstract: Offshore wind industrial chains, encompassing upstream component manufacturing, midstream project development and operation, and downstream grid integration, underpin large-scale utilization, yet their spatial organization, structural linkages, and coordinated development remain underexamined. This study examines offshore wind industrial chains in China's 11 coastal provinces during 2010 − 2023, a period characterized by globally leading capacity expansion and governance transition from national centralization to provincial decentralization, through a stepwise analytical framework integrating GIS-based spatial mapping, Entropy-TOPSIS evaluation, fixed-effects spatial Durbin modeling, coupling coordination degree assessment, and BCa-bootstrap fractional logit regression with event-window interactions. Results reveal that the spatial organization of major manufacturing and supply activities reflects their techno-economic characteristics and logistics requirements under decentralization-induced incentives, fostering province-embedded industrial development. Although cross-provincial spatial spillovers and competitive interactions are observed, segment performance remains primarily anchored in within-province adjacent-segment linkages. Provincial industrial chains exhibit distinct coordinated development patterns, with Jiangsu and Guangdong achieving high coupling − high development, Shandong, Liaoning, and Shanghai maintaining high coupling − low development, and late-entrant provinces gradually transitioning beyond low coupling − low development. These patterns are associated with provincial industrial foundations, economic capacity, and accumulated deployment experience, while governance decentralization tends to reinforce pre-existing industrial advantages in better-endowed provinces rather than facilitating cross-provincial convergence. The findings extend industrial organization theory by highlighting governance transition as a critical institutional context and provide practical insights for addressing China's industrial coordination bottlenecks, with broader applicability to emerging offshore wind markets with dispersed coastal resources, uneven port infrastructure, and fragmented manufacturing capacity.

papers.title: Fast, safe and low energy consumption charging for lithium-ion batteries via dynamic safety boundaries and adaptive SOC control
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles necessitates lithium-ion batteries capable of fast charging, yet this process inherently faces the risk of heat generation and lithium plating. Considering the common fast charging scenarios around room temperature and practical implementation feasibility, this study introduces an offline multi-stage charging optimization framework. This framework is based on an enhanced electrochemical-thermal coupling model, and the solid-phase diffusion coefficient for both electrodes varies with state of charge (SOC). Leveraging the high rates adaptability and precise dynamic lithium plating current boundary tracking at the negative electrode enabled by this high accuracy model, three systematic charging solutions are developed and thoroughly analyzed. There are two charging strategies based on uniform SOC intervals, corresponding to the fixed safety boundaries without critical charging current update and dynamic safety boundaries with critical charging current update, as well as a charging protocol with nonuniform SOC intervals based on energy consumption. Compared with using traditional fixed safety boundaries, the dynamic boundary strategy maintains negative electrode potential above 10 mV throughout charging to guarantee safety. Further, the energy-adaptive SOC interval division approach extra curtails energy consumption by 1.03% and mitigates power fluctuations, which can deliver substantial cumulative benefits when scaled to the massive electric vehicle market. For low temperature conditions, the batteries can be preheated to specific temperatures before applying the proposed strategy. This framework offers valuable insights into the design of next-generation charging protocols for lithium-ion batteries that are fast, safe, and economically viable.

papers.title: Operating area-dependent flexible ancillary service provision of electric vehicles: Capacity assessment and coordination
papers.abstract: The vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology enables electric vehicles (EVs) to provide ancillary services to the grid, but the service provision of EVs is challenged by the tradeoff between drivers’ traveling demands and the grid’s requirement for reliable support. Accurate assessment of schedulable capacities and grid requirement-adapted coordination of EVs has become a critical problem that needs to be addressed. This paper proposes an operating area-dependent capacity assessment and coordination strategy for EV clusters. First, considering the charging characteristics and traveling behavior of EVs, the state of charge (SOC)-time operating area of EVs is constructed. Based on the operating area, the schedulable capacity of EVs can be flexibly assessed under varying power amplitude and duration requirements. Then, a prioritization-based coordination strategy for EVs for ancillary service with certain power amplitude and duration is proposed with the objective of minimizing battery aging. To address the unexpected power deficit due to sudden disconnection of EVs during ancillary service, an emergency compensation strategy is proposed. The EVs outside the restricted boundaries are dispatched in such a case, and the stable and reliable ancillary service of EV cluster can be ensured. Case study results validate the proposed method in terms of ancillary service capacity estimation, battery aging reduction and stable service provision. In the studied case, the proposed method avoids a 13.3% decrease in the output power of the EV cluster due to inaccurate capacity estimation. Under the adopted aging assessment based on experimental degradation data, the proposed method substantially reduces battery aging costs compared with the conventional strategy. Furthermore, the proposed coordination strategy effectively maintains charging-discharging power stability during ancillary service provision.

papers.title: Incorporating extreme scenarios into multi-stage planning of multi-timescale energy storage
papers.abstract: City-scale integrated energy systems (CIESs) couple electricity and gas networks with heterogeneous multi-timescale energy storage (MTES) to balance renewable variability from hourly to seasonal timescales. Conventional representative-scenario methods, however, select days primarily from exogenous source-load profiles and may omit operation-critical conditions whose importance changes as multi-stage investments evolve, while directly solving the full-year electricity-gas mixed-integer linear program is also computationally demanding. This paper therefore develops a model-based extreme scenario aggregation (ESA) framework for multi-stage MTES planning in CIESs. A scenario-driven equivalent MTES model preserves the inter- and intra-scenario states of battery, compressed-air, and gas storage. Moreover, full-year posterior operation simulations provide load shedding, renewable curtailment, and upstream energy purchases for identifying operation-critical days. Based on the operational data, the spectral residual-convolutional neural network adaptively separates extreme and regular days, while a stage influence coefficient (SIC) transfers anticipated later-stage operating stress to earlier-stage scenario updating. Then, sequential rolling and iterative simultaneous aggregation reconstruct both scenario sets within a fixed representative-scenario budget, and iteration stops according to both objective change and scenario-set stability. In the 3-bus-3-gas-node case, rolling ESA reduces the average benchmark-relative cost gap from 13.42% for k-means and 7.51% for k-medoids to 2.41%, while reducing the annual and conditional extreme-period load-shedding ratios from 1.30% and 3.03% to 0.61% and 1.15%, respectively. Iterative ESA with SIC achieves a 2.77% average gap and annual and conditional extreme-period ratios of 0.69% and 1.36% in 10.57 h. The 39-bus-20-gas-node case achieves corresponding values of 2.57%, 0.23%, and 0.95% in 7.23 h, confirming scalability. Multi-day sensitivity analysis further shows that 5-day block provides the most favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. These results show that posterior cross-stage scenario updating improves planning accuracy and operational adequacy while preserving the complementary hourly, cross-day, and seasonal roles of MTES.

papers.title: Intercell nonuniformity and dominant mechanisms analysis in industrial-scale water electrolyzer stacks: a unified comparative multiphysics modeling across AWE, AEM and PEM
papers.abstract: Low temperature water electrolysis is a key route for converting renewable electricity into green hydrogen, but industrial-scale stacks are prone to intercell nonuniformity during scale up. The origins and dominant mechanisms of this nonuniformity remain unclear across different electrolyzer technologies. To address this issue, this study develops a unified stack-scale multiphysics lumped-parameter model for industrial-scale alkaline water electrolysis (AWE), anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM), and proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEM) stacks and uses it to compare the dominant mechanisms of intercell nonuniformity across the three technologies. The model is formulated on a common stack-level basis and couples flow distribution, shunt current, bubble coverage, temperature distribution, and electrochemical reaction under a common external flow network. The common stack-level framework is first validated using an AWE experimental platform. The model results show that AWE exhibits the strongest intercell nonuniformity, mainly due to shunt current induced redistribution of effective reaction current. AEM shows intermediate behavior governed by weak shunt current and gas-phase effects, whereas PEM is influenced mainly by bubble coverage and temperature development. Load dependent and layered physical field analyses further reveal that AWE is dominated by shunt current, causing a 12.38% rated current loss and a 7.21% energy-efficiency drop, whereas the responses of AEM and PEM are governed mainly by voltage efficiency degradation, driven by gas-phase and temperature effects. The proposed framework provides a unified basis for mechanism identification and differentiated optimization of industrial-scale low temperature electrolyzer stacks.

papers.title: Gaps in mind: Political and spatial cleavages in local onshore wind attitudes in Germany
papers.abstract: Public support for wind energy in Germany is high, yet local opposition can impede project delivery. This study examines which socio-demographic characteristics predict acceptance of onshore wind energy and whether effects differ between urban and rural residents in North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW). We analyze a representative survey of N = 6284 adults fielded in September 2021, using survey weights. We focus on wind-salient outcomes (support for local wind expansion and landscape evaluations) and situate preferences for information, participation, conflict handling, and benefit-sharing as actionable process levers. Analytically, we (i) report weighted mean differences by place; (ii) estimate weighted least-squares models in which place of residence, political orientation, education, and age enter jointly; and (iii) test moderated regressions to assess whether urban-rural context conditions the influence of trust and perceived fairness. Results show that political orientation is by far the strongest correlate of wind-salient attitudes; education and age contribute only weak gradients that are not consistently distinguishable from zero, and the direct urban-rural effect is small and statistically indistinguishable from zero once other markers are held constant. Trust in scientists and planning authorities and perceived procedural/distributive fairness are strongly and positively associated with support; moreover, context matters: in rural settings, higher trust and clearly governed fairness arrangements are especially consequential. We discuss planning implications, focusing on the need to: embed co-designed, face-to-face participation alongside transparent disclosures; route information through credible intermediaries; and make siting criteria and revenue-sharing explicit and enforceable. The study clarifies how classic acceptance drivers interact with place and provides actionable guidance for tailoring engagement to different constituencies in Germany.

papers.title: Energy infrastructure for AI data centers: A critical review of grid integration, techno-economic challenges, and future pathways
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) workloads are rapidly changing the energy landscape of today's data centers, both in terms of total electricity usage and power density at the facility level. The ongoing deployment of large-scale AI training and inference infrastructure is further driving and increasing the demand for electrical reliability, cooling capacity, power quality, grid interconnection, and low-carbon electricity supply. These interdependent issues require coordinated consideration of energy-infrastructure planning that takes into consideration renewable energy generation and storage, electrical architecture, operational flexibility, economic performance, and system resilience. The critical review combines 155 sources, mostly published between 2015 and 2026, identified and screened following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, which includes peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers, technical standards, agency and institutional reports, market analyses, and corporate disclosure. The resulting evidence is presented in a seven-component decision framework that includes site and resource assessment, technology selection, electrical architecture, control and dispatch, workload flexibility, economic evaluation, and resilience and sustainability. The reviewed evidence indicates that renewable generation, energy storage, grid-support technologies, and workload flexibility can support lower-carbon AI data-center operations; however, the technical and economic performance of these approaches remains highly dependent on project-specific resource conditions, market structures, reliability requirements, and system boundaries. Reliability assessment requires a chronological, site-specific evaluation of load, resource, and infrastructure conditions. Wind–solar complementarity and workload flexibility may improve renewable-energy utilization; however, their benefits remain strongly dependent on operational and geographic constraints. The proposed framework is intended as a screening and decision-support tool rather than a prescriptive design methodology or site-specific optimization model. Important research needs include reproducible techno-economic assessment methods, independently verifiable corporate metrics, improved workload-flexibility characterization, and integrated evaluation of energy, water, reliability, and sustainability impacts. The resulting framework provides a structured basis for evaluating renewable-powered AI data center infrastructure across technical, economic, operational, and sustainability dimensions.

papers.title: How does affordability shape behavioural intentions of consumers to purchase low water footprint food products? The polish context
Niche Divergence-Based Identification of Microbial Indicators Tracking Cyanobacterial Bloom Succession: A Metagenomic and Machine Learning Framework
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs) pose significant environmental and public health risks through toxin production, antibiotic resistance gene dissemination, and the disruption of biogeochemical cycles. Although extensive metagenomic investigations have explored microbial interactions between Cyanobacteria and coexisting members, the potential of incorporating functional indicators into early CyanoHAB monitoring systems remains underexplored. In this study, we employed metagenomic binning combined with machine learning approaches to analyze seasonal cyanobacterial succession and coexisting microbial communities across 19 sites in Erhai Lake across four seasons. We documented distinct niche shifts driven by the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in seasonal cyanobacterial succession alongside the formation of unique niches triggered by this asynchrony. Specialized microbial members (SN-MAGs) were identified as candidate bioindicators associated with early-stage cyanobacterial proliferation. Functional profiling showed r/K selection and metabolic adaptations in these SN-MAGs, including stress resistance and altered carbon metabolism, linked to cyanobacterial dynamics. Machine learning models leveraging these features were constructed and retrospectively evaluated. Cross-lake validation using an independent Lake Taihu dataset confirmed associations among these features and microbial community shifts preceding Microcystis proliferation. Our findings highlight the potential value of the dynamics of specific bacteria as a sensitive indicator of cyanobacterial dynamics. Moreover, we propose that these identified functional markers could potentially be developed into targeted molecular assays (e.g., qPCR assays), offering possible utility in predicting Microcystis population expansion.

papers.title: Persistent Desorption, Aging, and Secondary VOC Formation from Biomass-Burning Emissions on Indoor Surfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Biomass burning (BB) degrades indoor air quality both through direct emissions and via smoke sorption onto surfaces, resulting in persistent pollutant re-emission and transformation. However, the dynamics of this multiphase process remain unclear. This study investigates the re-emission, chemical aging, and secondary product formation of smoke residues on three representative indoor surfaces (glass, cotton, and gypsum). Smoke-contaminated surfaces re-emitted 120–180 distinct volatile organic compounds (VOCs). After 2 weeks of ventilation, the median emission rates of various VOCs from porous cotton and gypsum (3.3 and 4.2 μg m–2 h–1) far exceeded that from glass (0.06 μg m–2 h–1), reflecting their greater sorption capacity and longer pollutant persistence. The emission increased by factors of 7 and 4 on glass and cotton when relative humidity (RH) rose from 20% to 80%, attributed to enhanced initial sorption. Smoke-sorbed gypsum showed a strong ozone (O3) uptake coefficient ((1.6 ± 0.2) × 10–5 at 50 ppb O3, 20% RH), approximately 20 times that on glass, confirming its role as a key indoor O3 sink. Heterogeneous transformation of surface residues produced secondary VOCs, including aldehydes and carboxylic acids, further deteriorating indoor air quality. These findings demonstrate the critical and prolonged influence of surface-retained BB emissions on indoor air chemistry.

papers.title: Tensor product fusion of LIBS and acoustic emission signals for waste identification in recycling
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of recyclable waste is essential for efficient material recovery. However, existing spectroscopic studies have not fully addressed the combined challenges of integrating hierarchical identification requirements, representing subtle spectral differences, and effectively exploiting cross-modal complementarity. To address these gaps, this study develops a two-stage classification framework for recyclable waste, integrating laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and plasma acoustic emission signals (PAES). For coarse classification, a Difference–Summation Gramian Angular Field (DSGAF) encoding method transforms one-dimensional LIBS spectra into two-dimensional representations to enhance spectral discriminability. For fine subclassification, LIBS-derived elemental-composition information is combined with complementary physical-response information carried by PAES. Mutual information (MI) and Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) are used for feature selection, and a LIBS–PAES Tensor Product Enhancement (LPTE) method is introduced to explicitly exploit cross-modal interactions. The DSGAF-based 2DCNN increased the independent-test accuracy from 91.11% to 98.48% for classifying recyclable waste into paper–wood, glass, plastic, metal, and textile categories. For fine subclassification of plastic, metal, and textile waste, the MI_LPTE model achieved accuracies above 99% and outperformed unimodal and conventional fusion models. These results demonstrate the potential of hierarchical LIBS–PAES sensing for recyclable-waste sorting and material recovery.

papers.title: Thermodynamic analysis of biogas reforming for hydrogen production: A comparative investigation
papers.abstract: Organic solid waste (OSW) can be valorized through anaerobic digestion, producing biogas as a renewable energy carrier while enabling efficient resource recovery. As biogas is primarily composed of CH 4 and CO 2 , its conversion into hydrogen offers a promising pathway for both renewable energy production and greenhouse gas utilization. However, multiple thermochemical conversion routes have been proposed, and their relative advantages in terms of hydrogen production performance, carbon utilization, and energy consumption remain unclear. In this regard, three thermochemical pathways, namely methane decomposition (MD), dry reforming of methane (DRM), and combined steam and dry reforming of methane (CSDRM), are systematically evaluated using Aspen Plus to identify the most suitable process for hydrogen production from OSW−derived biogas. CSDRM represents the best comprehensive performance among the investigated pathways. In this process, the simultaneous steam and dry reforming reactions synergistically enhance methane conversion. The hydrogen concentration and hydrogen utilization efficiency achieve 57.9 vol % and 94.3 %, respectively, accompanied by the highest syngas yield of 127.9 kmol h −1 . The hydrogen production rate of CSDRM increases by 34.9 % and 35.5 % compared with MD and DRM, respectively.

papers.title: Thermodynamic, economic and environmental assessment of advanced transcritical CO2 supermarket refrigeration architectures with maintenance-cost sensitivity analysis
papers.abstract: Modern supermarket refrigeration systems are progressively transitioning toward low-global-warming-potential solutions, with transcritical CO 2 architectures emerging as promising alternatives to conventional synthetic refrigerants. However, the thermodynamically optimal refrigeration technology may not necessarily coincide with the most suitable solution for industrial implementation. This study compares a conventional booster cycle (BC), a parallel-compression system (PC), and a booster cycle with low-pressure ejectors (BLPE) through a thermodynamic, economic, environmental, and dual-layer multi-criteria assessment. Annual simulations are performed using location-specific outdoor dry-bulb temperature profiles for Berlin (Germany), Lisbon (Portugal), Albuquerque (United States), and Singapore under a fixed supermarket load profile, while LCC, TEWI, and the quantitative technical-MCDM assessment are restricted to the Lisbon reference case. Relative to BC, model-predicted annual electricity-consumption reductions range from 10.55% to 11.68% for PC and from 12.38% to 12.62% for BLPE. In Lisbon, PC and BLPE reduce LCC by 7.11% and 8.74%, respectively, and TEWI by 10.80% and 12.50%. BLPE therefore provides the best quantitative technical performance, although its baseline LCC advantage over PC is eliminated by an additional annual maintenance-cost premium of approximately 803 Euro/year. In contrast, the expert-informed adoption-readiness layer ranks PC first; PC occupies first position in 85.5% of bootstrap expert-resampling realizations and in 99.293–99.957% of Monte Carlo criterion-weight realizations across TOPSIS, VIKOR, and EDAS. These results indicate that thermodynamic superiority and industrial adoption readiness may diverge, and that maintenance-cost tolerance and implementation perceptions should be considered alongside modeled performance when selecting advanced CO 2 refrigeration architectures.

papers.title: Consumers' intentions to return PET bottles in a hybrid waste management system: evidence from Vietnam
papers.abstract: Despite the expansion of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) to reduce plastic waste in emerging economies, consumers’ return intentions in the hybrid formal–informal waste management systems remain insufficiently understood. This study extends the theory of planned behavior (TPB) by incorporating environmental concern, economic incentives, convenience of return, and perceptions of informal recycling to explain PET bottles return intentions. A dual-channel survey (online and face-to-face) was conducted in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, yielding 325 valid responses from January to March 2026. Employing covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM), several key findings emerge. Perceived behavioral control is the strongest predictor of return intention ( β = 0.307, p < 0.001), followed by subjective norms ( β = 0.219, p = 0.002) and attitude ( β = 0.141, p = 0.033). Perceptions of informal recycling positively influence return intention ( β = 0.129, p = 0.040). Rather than acting as a competitive barrier, positive perceptions of the informal sector serve as a complementary enabler that supports formal return intentions. These findings highlight the need for EPR policies to coordinate stakeholders across the entire value chain. It is essential to prioritize infrastructural accessibility and incorporate informal scrap dealers into official reverse logistics chains to achieve sustainable circularity.

papers.title: Synergy or crowding-out? How the superposition of mitigation and adaptation policies shapes firm green innovation in China
papers.abstract: Climate governance increasingly requires the simultaneous pursuit of mitigation and adaptation. However, whether their policy superposition promotes or constrains firm green innovation remains unclear. Drawing on Policy Mix Theory, this study applies a Double Machine Learning framework to analyze 11,012 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed firms (2005–2023), exploiting the overlapping implementation of the Low-Carbon City Pilot and the Climate-Resilient City Pilot. We find that the superposition of the two pilots generates policy synergy and significantly enhances firm green innovation ( β = 0.259, p < 0.01 ), with a stronger response for invention patents ( β = 0.319, p < 0.01 ) than for utility models. Mechanism analysis reveals that this dual-pilot superposition heightens managerial climate-risk attention ( β = 0.099, p < 0.01 ) and increases government environmental subsidies ( β = 1.300, p < 0.05 ). The synergy effect is concentrated among state-owned enterprises and financially unconstrained firms, is stronger in non-super-large cities and eastern regions, and is activated primarily when mitigation pressure is high but adaptation pressure is low. These heterogeneous responses across ownership types and regional conditions further suggest that the realization of such cross-objective policy synergies depends on firms’ absorptive capacity and the local institutional environment, factors largely overlooked in current policy-mix designs.

papers.title: A decision-support system for post-closure mine reutilization: Criteria-based ranking integrating technical and socioeconomic constraints
papers.abstract: Coal phase-out policies and the accelerating deployment of renewable energy are driving the progressive closure of underground coal mines, leaving large subsurface volumes and surface infrastructure that are commonly sealed and abandoned. Selecting an optimal reuse concept can be difficult because alternatives range from energy production and storage to underground research facilities, tourism, and industrial logistics, and each option is constrained by mine-specific geology, depth, hydrogeology, temperature and humidity, water inflow, and the surrounding market and community context. This study develops a transparent, mine-specific screening framework that prioritizes post-mining reuse options. A structured narrative review defines 15 reuse pathways and derives option-specific application criteria. For each pathway, “best-case” benchmark conditions are formulated to enable consistent scoring across mines. Site conditions are compared with these benchmarks and rated. Criterion weights were obtained using an expert survey, and aggregates were normalised for comparability. The approach is then demonstrated for the Pniówek hard-coal mine in Poland. The methodological contribution is a mine-level, option-specific benchmark architecture that places technically dissimilar underground reuse pathways in a common and auditable screening structure. Unlike regional land-use inventories or methods tailored to a single technology, the framework combines spreadsheet-based min–max normalisation of the technical and infrastructure branches, explicit missing-data and evidence-quality reporting, a non-compensatory safety gate, and transparent weighted aggregation. The Pniówek application is illustrative rather than a final feasibility assessment: Underground Gas Storage (UGS), Mine Water Geothermal (MWG) and Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) form the leading screening shortlist, while UGS and other pressure-storage options remain subject to site-specific verification of containment, fault connectivity and post-closure hydrogeological evolution. Sensitivity tests show that UGS remains first under the tested perturbations, whereas MWG and CAES should be interpreted as an effectively tied second group. The framework therefore supports transparent prioritisation but does not replace geomechanical, hydrogeological, legal, economic or stakeholder-specific feasibility studies.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal patterns and drivers of agricultural ammonia emissions in China (1990–2020)
papers.abstract: Agricultural ammonia (NH 3 ) is an important precursor for the formation of atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) in China. However, the long-term evolution and driving mechanisms of its emissions remain poorly understood, particularly at fine spatial scales. Based on the bottom-up emission factor approach, this study developed a county-level agricultural NH 3 emission inventory of China for 1990–2020. The logarithmic mean Divisia index (LMDI) method was applied to quantitatively decompose the drivers of changes in agricultural NH 3 emissions. From 1990 to 2020, total emissions rose from 6.15 Tg to 8.69 Tg. NH 3 emissions from livestock production increased from 3.08 Tg to 4.90 Tg and gradually became the dominant emission source. Meanwhile, NH 3 emissions from fertilizer application increased from 3.07 Tg to 3.79 Tg. Spatially, NH 3 emission hotspots were concentrated in major agricultural regions, including the North China Plain, the Northeast China Plain, and the Sichuan Basin, with relatively high emissions also observed along basin margins in Northwest China. Driving factor decomposition results indicated that agricultural structural adjustments, technological and management improvements, and emission control policies exerted significant mitigating effects on agricultural NH 3 emissions during different periods. For livestock production, promoting the development of intensive production systems is important. Regarding fertilizer application, sustained efforts are required to optimize fertilization practices. These findings provide scientific support for further exploiting the substantial potential for NH 3 emission reduction in China.

papers.title: Landscape ecological risk dynamics and scenario-based regulation in the Gannan Plateau, China: A coupled PLUS-LER-BRT-ABM framework
papers.abstract: Landscape ecological risk (LER) assessment is essential for sustainable land management in ecologically fragile alpine regions, yet existing approaches typically adopt one-way workflows that disconnect landscape simulation, risk assessment, driver analysis, and scenario optimization. This study developed a coupled PLUS–LER–BRT–ABM framework with closed-loop coupling between the landscape-simulation and agent-based modules, and applied it to the Gannan Plateau over 1985–2045. Results showed a persistent northeast–southwest risk gradient, with the high-risk (HighER) share rising from 35.2% in 1985 to 37.8% in 2024. Boosted regression tree (BRT) analysis attributed 38.8% of relative influence to socioeconomic factors and 8.7% to grazing intensity. By 2045, the ecology-priority (EP) and comprehensive-coordination (CC) scenarios reduced mean regional LER by 0.82% and 0.88% relative to the baseline (BL), whereas human-activity control (HC) achieved only 0.05%. In a matched open-loop control, agent actions could not modify the precomputed PLUS trajectory; open and closed paths remained identical before the first 2029 refresh, after which feedback supplied 15.0% and 21.3% of the total EP and CC reductions. Counterfactual separation further showed that FVC recovery dominated the normalized single-channel decomposition, accounting for 86.8% of the summed isolated-channel effects. These results show that five-year feedback changes the simulated risk pathway and that ecology-active regulation outperforms development control alone.

papers.title: Recovering bioactive components from waste sludge reinforces microbial interactions for resilient anaerobic wastewater treatment
papers.abstract: Anaerobic treatment is an energy-efficient technology for industrial wastewater management, yet its practical application is often constrained by poor stability under inhibitory perturbations. Here, we recovered bioactive components from waste sludge to develop a bioregulatory material for enhancing the resilience of anaerobic reactor. Bioactive signaling molecules and biopolymers recovered from sludge were integrated with sludge-derived biochar to construct a bioregulatory scaffold (BioReg-SC) capable of slow signal release and efficient electron transfer. In a continuous up-flow anaerobic reactor operated for 185 days under repeated Congo red shocks, the BioReg-SC system maintained stable performance and rapidly restored chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal to 85.7% within 5 days, while sustaining methane production. The sustained release of signaling molecules, enabled by the biopolymer matrix, stimulated extracellular polymeric substances secretion and microbial aggregation, facilitating the formation of compact and stable sludge granules within 80 days. Meanwhile, the conductive carbon framework facilitated direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET), promoting the enrichment of electrogen ( Geobacter ) and DIET-capable methanogens ( Methanothrix , Methanosarcina ). Collectively, these functions established a coupled bioregulation-electron transfer mechanism that stabilizes microbial metabolism under long-term inhibitory stress. This work demonstrates a circular strategy recovering bioactive components from waste sludge to create functional bioregulators, providing a sustainable approach for resilient anaerobic wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Resilience of centralized and distributed energy systems to grid outage in winter: a district-scale assessment in Colorado, USA
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the thermal resilience of a district composed of seventeen buildings located in Colorado (USA) during a 36-hour winter power outage. The thermal performance of each building was simulated using EnergyPlus combined with MATLAB®. Three winter scenarios were investigated. The first corresponds to a baseline case where power comes from the grid. The second considers a decentralized photovoltaic (PV) system operating with and without storage. Finally, the third scenario evaluates a centralized district-level configuration based on shared PV generation, with and without storage. The results show that if PV generation alone delays the decrease in indoor temperature following the power outage, the integration of storage extends the metric as much as 16 h, depending on the building. In addition, the recovery time indicates reductions of up to 69 % when PV generation is combined with storage. Furthermore, the centralized strategy is capable of sustaining the prioritized buildings for nearly the entire 36-hour outage period. Overall, the results suggest that coordinated energy-sharing strategies can substantially improve district thermal resilience while simultaneously reducing storage requirements.

papers.title: Evaluation of free lime content in cement kilns by physics-guided support vector regression using factory energy management system
papers.abstract: The cement industry is one of the most carbon-intensive industrial sectors owing to its high energy demand. In clinker production, free lime (F-CaO) is a critical quality indicator that reflects the adequacy of heat supply during high-temperature processing; excessive F-CaO indicates insufficient thermal energy and leads to deterioration of clinker quality and energy efficiency. Accurate prediction of F-CaO is therefore important for effective quality control and energy-efficient plant operation. Previous data-driven studies have selected input variables mainly from statistical correlations, often neglecting the underlying heat-transfer and reaction mechanisms of the pyro-process. To address this limitation, the energy flows and airflow distribution in the pre-heater, kiln, and cooler were quantified using a factory energy management system (FEMS) combined with a heat and mass balance model. Based on this analysis, physically meaningful input variables governing F-CaO formation were derived and incorporated into a support vector regression (SVR) model. Under an identical chronological train/test split and hyperparameter optimization protocol, the physics-guided inputs showed improved prediction performance compared with conventional correlation-based inputs, achieving MSE = 0.03, TIC = 0.07, and R = 0.73 on the hold-out test set. These results indicate that deriving input variables from physical principles can improve F-CaO prediction consistency within the studied operating window, providing a rational framework for physics-guided soft sensor development.

papers.title: Raman spectroscopy resolves nitrogen-driven metabolic acclimation to urban air pollution in Quercus ilex
papers.abstract: Urban air pollution may alter plant metabolism long before visible damage becomes apparent. Raman spectroscopy was evaluated as a rapid, non-destructive approach to resolve these biochemical adjustments. Mature Quercus ilex L. trees were sampled along a well-defined pollution gradient in Tuscany (Italy), spanning high, intermediate, and low levels of NO₂ and PM₁₀. Leaf Raman spectra revealed coordinated modulation of primary and secondary metabolism. Pigment-related bands (chlorophylls and carotenoids) increased toward the most polluted site, while inducible flavonoid signals showed site-dependent variation consistent with oxidative pressure in superficial tissues. These patterns were consistent with destructive biochemical analyses and chlorophyll fluorescence measurements, which indicated acclimation rather than photoinhibition damage. A composite Raman index showed a close site-level association with NO₂ exposure, suggesting that nitrogen-related urban pollution was the main exposure component linked to the observed metabolic response. Overall, Raman spectroscopy captures the chronic metabolic imprint of urban air pollution in Q. ilex, resolving coordinated pigment reinforcement and defensive activation without sample destruction. This approach provides a rapid and scalable framework for linking atmospheric chemistry to plant functional status in biomonitoring applications.

papers.title: Species-specific effects of microplastic-contaminated pollen on larval development in two wild bee species (Apidae, Megachilidae; Apiformes)
papers.abstract: Plastic production has increased for centuries, with a similar increase in the amount of microplastics released into and accumulating in soils and water bodies, detrimentally affecting organisms. One common transition is via air, during which microplastic particles likely also sediment onto plant parts, e.g., flowers, potentially contaminating floral resources and exposing pollinators to microplastics. In the laboratory, the detrimental effects of such contaminations in sugar water were shown in adult bees, usually honeybees (Apis mellifera), while corresponding experiments with larvae are still scarce. In this study, we tested the effect of pollen contaminated with a microplastics mixture in two concentrations (Low 0.5 mg/kg, High 50 mg/kg) on the development and survival of larvae of two wild bee species (Osmia bicornis and Bombus terrestris). Results indicate that Bombus terrestris larvae fed low microplastic concentrations consumed up to 20% less pollen and developed into significantly fewer pupae (up to 26%) as compared to larvae fed high microplastic concentrations and non-contaminated control pollen. Similarly, Osmia bicornis larvae fed low concentrations of microplastics developed more slowly, hatched later, and showed higher body mass and a higher conversion of pollen to body mass than larvae fed high concentrations of microplastics or the control. Responses differed between treatments and species, suggesting a non-monotonic pattern that warrants confirmation across a broader dose range. A possible explanation might be that higher concentrations activate immune and protective reactions not triggered by lower concentrations. The effects of microplastics on pollinators and other terrestrial organisms clearly warrant further research, as we are only beginning to understand the magnitude of the impacts these pollutants have on our ecosystems.

Spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear drivers of MSW carbon emissions from the perspective of consumption and industrial structure upgrading: An explainable machine learning approach
papers.abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) carbon emissions pose a major challenge to urban sustainable development, yet nonlinear drivers across different urban development contexts remain insufficiently understood. Based on consumption upgrading and industrial structure upgrading, this study classifies 284 prefecture-level and above cities in China into four development types, estimates MSW carbon emissions from treatment processes during 2010–2023, and constructs an XGBoost–SHAP model to identify key drivers, nonlinear thresholds, and interaction contributions. The results show that MSW carbon emissions followed an overall trajectory of “growth–decline–slight rebound,” with comprehensive upgrading cities, despite being the smallest group, maintaining the highest long-term emission levels. Urban construction scale and population size are identified as core drivers, whereas waste treatment structure upgrading shows a negative contribution. Comprehensive upgrading cities are characterized by joint drivers related to scale agglomeration, economic activity, and governance capacity; household consumption is a more prominent driver in consumption-led upgrading cities; environmental sanitation infrastructure emerges as a more prominent driver in industry-led upgrading cities; and scale-related factors remain the primary drivers in foundational cities. From the combined perspective of demand-side consumption changes and supply-side industrial structure adjustment, this study reveals heterogeneous drivers of MSW carbon emissions and provides insights for city-type-specific low-carbon MSW governance strategies.

papers.title: Towards a new generation of science-policy interfaces for biodiversity: Contributions from the State Biodiversity Strategies Initiative in Mexico
papers.abstract: Science-Policy Interfaces (SPIs) are increasingly recognized as mechanisms for linking knowledge generation with biodiversity decision-making. However, little is known about how institutionalized SPIs operate at subnational levels, particularly in megadiverse countries of the Global South, a region characterized by political institutional weaknesses and significant socio-environmental challenges. Mexico offers an illustrative case for examining these dynamics through its State Biodiversity Strategies Initiative (SBS-Initiative), one of the most extensive subnational biodiversity planning experiences worldwide promoted by the Convention on Biological Diversity. This study analyzes the institutional design of the SPIs established through the SBS-Initiative, the barriers and enablers shaping their development, and their contributions to the credibility, relevance, and legitimacy of this planning process. Using the CRELE framework as an analytical lens, we conducted a qualitative analysis of 34 institutional documents and 31 semi-structured interviews with national and subnational government officials and researchers involved in these interfaces. Three main findings stand out: the initiative combines two complementary SPI configurations, a predominantly linear model for biodiversity diagnostics and a co-productive model for strategies and action plans; barriers and enablers are context- and phase-dependent; and credibility, relevance, and legitimacy emerge dynamically from the interaction among institutional arrangements, diverse stakeholders, and multiple governance conditions. We conclude that SPIs do not depend on choosing between linear or co-production models, but on developing adaptive and hybrid institutional arrangements capable of responding to dynamic and diverse subnational contexts. These findings offer practical insights for strengthening biodiversity planning and other sustainability governance processes.

papers.title: Central bank digital currencies, financial subordination and the quest for infrastructural autonomy: the introduction of the eNaira in Nigeria
papers.abstract: Political economists have only recently begun to grapple with the question of how to conceptualise and systematically explain the responses of states in lower-income countries to the rise of digital money. This article connects scholarship on financial infrastructures and international financial subordination to conceptualise the factors that explain the investments of central banks in lower-income countries in the development of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). My main contention is that limited control of infrastructure is an important dimension of international financial subordination. I illustrate this argument focusing on the case of Nigeria, the second country in the world which launched a CBDC. My analysis suggests that Nigeria introduced her CBDC, the eNaira, to enhance her autonomy in the context of a subordinated position in the global financial and monetary system. Nigerian authorities considered the eNaira as a state-controlled financial infrastructure which they envisaged to reduce the reliance on externally controlled payment infrastructures. As such, this paper contributes to broader debates about how lower-income countries navigate the disruptions associated with FinTech. This includes the questions of how much sovereignty they have in the governance of digital financial infrastructures and how much influence foreign players have over their digital financial infrastructure.

papers.title: Reconceptualizing Advertising Measurement in the Age of Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming advertising by enabling large-scale creative automation, dynamic personalization, and AI-mediated consumer decision journeys. Existing measurement systems were developed for human-authored and relatively stable communication environments and do not capture how GenAI systems cocreate brand touchpoints with advertisers or mediate consumer evaluations of brands. In this study, we develop an integrated triadic framework for understanding the GenAI-mediated advertising landscape and reconceptualizes the action–mindset–behavior–finance measurement architecture to reflect an advertising process that is increasingly recursive, nonlinear, and adaptive. In doing so, we distinguish between traditional metrics that remain relevant but require reconceptualization and novel metrics unique to GenAI-assisted advertising systems. In addition, we extend the framework beyond firm-centered outcomes to incorporate stakeholder-oriented metrics relevant to employees, regulators, investors, and society. The framework offers guidance for scholars and managers seeking to evaluate GenAI advertising while maintaining transparency, trust, and competitive integrity. The study concludes with a future research agenda and crosscutting priorities addressing measurement, governance, accountability, and methodological challenges associated with GenAI-assisted advertising.

papers.title: Was I Scammed? Understanding Consumer Scam Reporting Behavior Through Cognitive Appraisal
Detransition, Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, and Moral Injury
papers.abstract: There are increasing reports of individuals who, after undergoing medical gender-affirming treatments (GAT) for gender incongruence/gender dysphoria, subsequently detransition and/or express regret regarding these interventions. Although detransition experiences are heterogeneous, some individuals who detransition describe substantial adverse physical consequences and psychological distress resulting from the GAT they received. The purpose of this article is to assist mental health professionals in their understanding and conceptualizing of detransition experiences within the existing Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) framework. It is posited that a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder, as delineated in the most recent text revision of the DSM (DSM-5-TR) (American Psychiatric Association, 2022), may be applicable for some individuals who have detransitioned. Furthermore, the relevance of the moral injury concept-recently incorporated into the DSM-5-TR under code Z65.8 (American Psychiatric Association, 2025)-as it pertains to this population, is discussed.

papers.title: Cohort Change in Attitudes About Adolescent Gender Transitions Between 2018 and 2025
papers.abstract: Abstract Medical gender transition for adolescents who identify as transgender is a contentious topic. The previous research evaluated data from respondents interviewed in 2018 and examined predictors of support for adolescent hormonal and surgical transitioning. Nevertheless, much has changed in public debates since that time. The present study evaluates data from a 2025 nationally representative survey which fielded a series of questions identical to those posed in 2018 in order to examine changes in attitudes among English-speaking American adults about gender dysphoric adolescents medically transitioning for the purpose of gender affirmation. Results indicate significant decreases in support between 2018 and 2025 for such medical transitioning. We examine cross-sectional, period changes, and changes within birth cohorts. Significant increases in disagreement with medical transitioning appear for all age cohorts born in 1988 or earlier. Given this changing landscape, we reexamine predictors of support for adolescent medical transition.

The information relevance of GAAP-based aggregate spending measures for state economic growth
papers.abstract: This study investigates the relevance of state governments' aggregate spending, as reported in audited GAAP-based financial statements, to state economic performance. Utilizing a dynamic panel model to address endogeneity and heterogeneity concerns, the study examines the informativeness of full-accrual and modified-accrual accounting measures for governmental activities and full-accrual accounting measures for business-type activities. The results reveal a negative and statistically significant association between GAAP-based spending measures and state economic growth, suggesting that these measures contain information about economic performance. Additionally, controlling for state-specific heterogeneity enhances the model's explanatory power by 18%, underscoring the importance of accounting for cross-sectional differences in state economies. The findings do not provide evidence that full-accrual measures offer incremental informational relevance beyond modified-accrual measures in explaining state economic growth, consistent with the Governmental Accounting Standards Board's (GASB) view that modified-accrual accounting is more relevant for evaluating short-term fiscal performance. This study highlights the advantages of audited, GAAP-based financial statement data over fiscal data sources that are not independently audited, emphasizing the credibility and consistency of audited reports. The research contributes to the literature by demonstrating the critical role of governmental financial reporting in explaining economic outcomes and promoting public accountability. The results offer important implications for policymakers and standard-setters, suggesting that GAAP-based financial reporting facilitates more informed decision-making regarding resource allocation in state governments.

Effective Worker Resistance and Realist Ideology Critique
papers.abstract: Abstract When do workers have good reasons to endorse a specific resistance strategy against managerial injustice? The answer partly requires clarifying whether that form of resistance is effective. But how should we understand efficacy? Political theorists cannot simply refer this question to empirical researchers. There is conceptual unclarity on what counts as efficacy. This paper shows that efficacy is a complex concept with multiple politically relevant dimensions. We illustrate this complexity by developing an epistemic notion of efficacy through a method of ideology critique, articulating a distinct dimension of effective resistance. A practice of resistance is epistemically efficacious if it reliably disrupts the mechanisms of ideological legitimation in the workplace by creating opportunities for egalitarian and collective contestation. Epistemic efficacy is a distinct evaluative lens that can assess the effectiveness of a resistance practice. After presenting the main argument, we apply our framework to the case of gossip as workplace resistance.

The cool façade paradox: Balancing urban climate regulation and outdoor thermal stress – A systematized review
papers.abstract: Cool façades — building walls with high solar reflectance and high thermal emittance — are promoted as a passive urban cooling strategy. However, their effects on outdoor thermal strain remain insufficiently understood. This systematized review synthesizes evidence from 77 studies to quantify the effects of increased façade solar reflectance on air temperature and outdoor thermal stress in urban environments. Based on façade-only interventions, each 0.1 increase in solar reflectance was associated with an air temperature reduction of 0.04 °C and a mean radiant temperature (MRT) increase of 1.63 °C, as derived from origin-constrained linear regression slopes ( β ). Studies that isolate façade-only interventions remain comparatively scarce, underscoring the need for further research to refine these estimates. The air-temperature response was highly context-dependent, whereas MRT increased in every study in the dataset. This asymmetry reveals what this review terms the cool façade paradox: during daytime hours, the MRT increase outweighs the air-temperature benefit, worsening pedestrian heat exposure despite cooler air. Air temperature reductions were consistently larger when façade modification was combined with complementary strategies, such as cool roofs, cool roads, and urban greening, than when applied alone. These findings indicate that cool façades should be assessed for their pedestrian-level radiative effects, not only for their air temperature benefits, before being adopted as a heat mitigation strategy.

A robust optimization method for integrating on-site medical waste treatment in rural areas with centralized treatment in urban areas
papers.abstract: Rural healthcare facilities generate medical waste (MW) and current practice routes this waste to centralized treatment plants in urban areas. Advances in on-site equipment have made local treatment of rural MW feasible, but no systematic framework exists for coordinating on-site and centralized treatment in an integrated urban–rural system. This study is the first to formulate on-site treatment as a mode-choice decision jointly optimized with centralized treatment across urban and rural areas under transportation cost uncertainty. A multi-objective robust optimization model is developed to minimize cost, risk, and carbon emissions, evaluating three centralized technologies and two on-site treatment options. Results show that on-site treatment reduces system risk and carbon emissions. The robust model yields more conservative cost estimates than its deterministic counterpart while achieving lower risk and emissions by retaining more on-site treatment selections. Combining centralized and on-site treatment withstands larger surges in MW generation than centralized treatment alone, offering resilience for public health emergencies. Incineration is the most cost-effective centralized technology despite the highest emissions, while microwave sterilization is the cheapest on-site option and high-temperature steam sterilization yields the lowest emissions. This study offers a practical decision-making tool for the integrated management of urban–rural MW systems with centralized and on-site treatment under uncertainty.

papers.title: Informing pharmaceutical regulation in China: Risk-based priority ranking across nine river basins
papers.abstract: Pharmaceuticals are widely detected in surface waters, posing significant ecological and human-health risks. China is a major producer and consumer of pharmaceuticals, and widespread contamination has been reported in its surface waters. Regional differences in topography, hydrology, land use, and socioeconomic conditions can shape patterns of pharmaceutical exposure and risk, calling for priority lists tailored to individual river basins. However, previous studies mainly focused on national-scale assessments, selected river basins, or specific pharmaceutical classes. In this study, we systematically reviewed 226 peer-reviewed articles and compiled 8628 occurrence records for 158 pharmaceutical compounds. A multi-criteria prioritization framework that integrated both hazard and exposure potential was used to identify priority pharmaceuticals across nine river basins. Antibiotics were the most frequently detected class of pharmaceuticals, although most had low or moderate priority scores. Erythromycin, roxithromycin, and azithromycin were notable exceptions and ranked highly. Among nonantibiotic pharmaceuticals, estrone and ibuprofen ranked highly in all nine basins. Beyond these shared priorities, several pharmaceuticals showed distinct basin-specific priority pattern. Psychotropic medicines, including diazepam, fluoxetine, sertraline, and citalopram, were identified as priorities in highly urbanized basins, particularly the Haihe and Yangtze River basins. In the Yellow River Basin, the lipid modulator gemfibrozil was prioritized, while in the Pearl River Basin, the veterinary antibiotic salinomycin was prioritized. Combining the rankings with uncertainty estimates showed that high-priority compounds with low uncertainty should be considered for stringent monitoring and control, whereas compounds with high uncertainty require additional occurrence and toxicity data. These findings underscore the importance of basin-scale prioritization in capturing regional differences and provide a basis for tiered monitoring and management in China.

papers.title: Sowing vegetation islets enhance plant diversity and habitat heterogeneity in Mediterranean long-established road verges
papers.abstract: Halting biodiversity loss requires innovative conservation approaches, and road verges offer opportunities for biodiversity-friendly measures. Although native seed mixes are increasingly used in post-disturbance revegetation, long-established road verges outside urban areas are often overlooked for proactive conservation. To promote species-rich and heterogeneous vegetation, we established vegetation islets by sowing a specifically designed seed mix of native herbaceous species along long-established road verges in a semi-arid Mediterranean agricultural landscape across two experimental blocks with different sowing years. Over four years, we conducted an integrated assessment of seed mix performance and plant diversity, composition, and structure, comparing vegetation islets and control plots and exploring the influence of local edaphoclimatic conditions. The establishment of vegetation islets had the strongest observed effect on plant composition and diversity, locally adding sown and spontaneous species absent from controls, and increasing species richness and compositional heterogeneity. Although seed mix persistence and relative cover declined over time, composition remained distinct from controls, shifting from annual to perennial dominance. Vegetation islets supported denser, shorter vegetation, enhancing local structural heterogeneity without compromising road safety. Higher rainfall, lower temperatures, and lower soil nutrient levels were associated with higher seed mix persistence and species richness. Experimental block affected only species composition and seed mix relative cover. An appropriate bespoke native seed mix, applied to stable long-established plant communities, helped support reliable conservation outcomes under semi-arid Mediterranean conditions. Vegetation islets may offer a resource-efficient approach to promote plant diversity and habitat heterogeneity in long-established road verges, highlighting their potential for proactive conservation.

papers.title: The composite acidifier of superphosphate and sulfuric acid for swine slurry storage treatment: Assessment of gases emission reduction and stabilization
Maternal PM2.5 exposure induces preeclampsia-like phenotypes in mice through placental angiogenic dysfunction and lncRNA–RUNX1 dysregulation
papers.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is an idiopathic gestational disorder defined by placental structural abnormalities, systemic inflammatory activation, angiogenic factor imbalance, and endothelial dysfunction. While existing epidemiological studies have established a correlational association between maternal fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) exposure and elevated PE risk, the specific underlying molecular mechanisms driving this association have not been fully elucidated. Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of maternal PM 2.5 exposure via intranasal instillation (3 mg/kg body weight, every other days from gestational day 0.5 to 17.5), we investigated the mechanisms underlying PE-like phenotypes induced by heating-season PM 2.5 from northern China. Exposed pregnant mice exhibited significantly elevated blood pressure at E13.5 and E17.5, accompanied by reduced vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and placental growth factor (PLGF) levels, increased urinary protein, and elevated serum levels of the tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 ( sFLT-1). Conversely, the endothelial markers endothelin 1 (ET-1) and nitric oxide (NO) remained unchanged. Placentas from PM 2.5 -exposed mice exhibited abnormal architecture and impaired angiogenesis in the labyrinth region. These phenotypes were consistent with key features of PE. Through transcriptomic profiling, bioinformatics analyses, immunofluorescence, quantitative reverse transcription PCR ( RT-qPCR), and chromatin/RNA immunoprecipitation assays, we identified the long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) NONMMUT087808.1 and NONMMUT044449.2 as potential regulators of placental development and function that are associated with runt-related transcription factor 1 (RUNX1) dysregulation, suggesting a possible contribution to PE-like phenotypes. Taken together, our findings provide experimental evidence linking exposure to heating-season PM 2.5 from northern China with adverse gestational outcomes and highlight the critical need for targeted air pollution mitigation strategies and population-specific health interventions for vulnerable subgroups, including pregnant women.

papers.title: Integrating structural and functional connectivity to optimize ecological security patterns at multiple levels in the Yellow River Delta, China
Stocking density shapes phytoplankton community stability in rice-crayfish integrated systems
papers.abstract: The rice-crayfish integrated system (RCIS) has expanded rapidly across China, yet its ecological impacts on phytoplankton remain inadequately understood. To fill this gap, we conducted a 40-d field experiment with five crayfish ( Procambarus clarkii ) stocking densities (0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 ind./m 2 ; CK, T1–T4) in replicated paddy plots. Water samples were collected weekly, and phytoplankton were identified and enumerated under light microscopy. Community structure, diversity indices (Margalef, Pielou, and Shannon–Wiener), co-occurrence networks, neutral community model (NCM), and Spearman correlations were analyzed. One-way ANOVA with Tukey tests was used for treatment comparisons, and network stability was assessed by robustness and vulnerability. Our results showed that crayfish stocking significantly reduced species richness and total biomass relative to CK ( P < 0.05) and shifted dominant taxa. Diversity indices declined to their lowest values at T2 and then recovered: Margalef decreased from 2.67 ± 0.05 in CK to 1.40 ± 0.10 in T2 ( P < 0.001), Pielou from 0.88 ± 0.01 to 0.80 ± 0.02 ( P < 0.05), and Shannon–Wiener from 2.91 ± 1.03 to 2.11 ± 0.10 ( P < 0.001), corresponding to reductions of 47.57%, 9.09%, and 27.49%, respectively. Co-occurrence networks were simplest and least stable at T2, with the highest vulnerability, whereas T3 had the lowest vulnerability among stocked treatments. NCM fitting showed higher stochasticity in stocked treatments (Rsqr = 0.683–0.806) and lower migration rates (Nm = 3–4) than CK (Nm = 11). Spearman correlations (significance at P < 0.05) identified dissolved oxygen, water temperature, and total nitrogen as key drivers in CK, whereas stocked treatments showed more complex nutrient-phytoplankton relationships. From a phytoplankton-based perspective, a stocking density of 3 ind./m 2 appears ecologically favorable, but this recommendation requires integrated testing with production, water quality, and multi-trophic indicators.

papers.title: Status hope: the conceptualisation of the status game
papers.abstract: Purpose This study develops a sociological conceptualisation of status hope to explain how the status game is produced and sustained across international marketplaces. It addresses the tension between status pursuit as joyful and autonomous and status as a field-structured struggle over symbolic power and uncertain recognition. Design/methodology/approach The research is conceptual and theory-building. It synthesises Bourdieusian theory, consumer culture theory research on status consumption and the conception of hope. It develops a tri-construct framework comprising belief in status, desire for status and perceived potential for status attainment. Findings Status hope is an illusive yet compelling pursuit of status under field constraints. Belief in status operates at the field level, where sociocultural ideologies generate tensions between ideals and realities. Desire for status operates at the habitus level through reference group selection and discrepancy management. Perceived potential for status attainment functions at the meso level through legitimation and enactment infrastructures. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual research, the framework requires empirical testing across international markets. It encourages research beyond national-culture typologies towards ideological field configurations explaining cross-market convergence and local variation. Practical implications The framework helps status brands refine segmentation beyond country-level cultural traits by identifying consumers according to ideologies they embody and internalise, and habitus-shaped changing referents as life unfolds. Originality/value The study reframes the status game as status hope: a field-structured, market-mediated and socioculturally sustained pursuit of uncertain recognition. It organises fragmented status consumption research across field/macro, meso and habitus/micro levels. Counterfeit consumption is treated as one illustrative application of our framework within the status consumption literature.

papers.title: Predicting leadership emergence in global virtual teams: machine learning applications in algorithmic HRM
papers.abstract: Identifying leadership talent early remains a persistent challenge for organizations, particularly in distributed and multicultural settings. Responding to calls for predictive approaches in algorithmic HRM, this study evaluates the relative performance and interpretability of supervised machine learning models for predicting leadership emergence in non-hierarchical global virtual teams (GVTs). Using data from 8,112 individuals nested in 2,371 GVTs, we benchmark five supervised algorithms (Artificial Neural Networks, Naïve Bayes, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression) on out-of-sample classification performance using demographic, psychological, motivational, behavioral, and team climate features collected across multiple time points. All models demonstrate strong predictive validity, with XGBoost achieving modestly superior overall performance (79% accuracy; AUROC = 0.87), consistent with its ability to capture nonlinear relationships in complex, high-dimensional data. Explainable AI analyses using SHAP identify the features that contribute most strongly to leadership emergence predictions (help with coordination, effort, friendliness (inverse), English language proficiency, and perceived team efficacy (inverse)) and reveal nonlinear predictive patterns that are difficult to detect with traditional statistical approaches. By framing leadership identification as a predictive talent analytics problem, this study advances algorithmic HRM research while illustrating how interpretable machine learning models can generate theoretically informative insights for leadership research in global and virtual contexts.
