Information design in cheap talk
papers.abstract: Abstract An uninformed sender publicly commits to an informative experiment about an uncertain state, privately observes its outcome, and sends a cheap talk message to a receiver. We provide an algorithm valid for arbitrary state-dependent preferences that will determine the sender’s optimal experiment and his equilibrium payoff under a binary state space. We provide conditions for informative information transmission to occur or to fail. These conditions depend more on marginal incentives—how payoffs vary with the state—than on the alignment of the sender’s and the receiver’s rankings over actions within a state. The algorithm can be easily modified to study the canonical cheap talk game with a perfectly informed sender.

Money Creation for Crypto Space: Stablecoins or Central Bank Digital Currencies?
papers.abstract: Stablecoins are the current go-to digital money to settle transactions on the blockchain. We explore the implications of introducing competing tokenized public digital monies (i.e., tokenized central bank digital currencies (CBDCs)). When they pay a moderate interest rate and guarantee users’ anonymity, tokenized CBDCs crowd out stablecoins. However, when they pay a high interest rate and have low anonymity features, stablecoin issuers could use tokenized CBDCs as collateral, promoting the creation of stablecoins. We identify conditions under which introducing a CBDC to compete with stablecoins in the crypto sector would be socially optimal. This paper was accepted by Will Cong for the Virtual Special Issue on Digital Finance. Funding: Support from Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) [Grant 100018 219835].

papers.title: Trading Off Business and Family Investments: Evidence from U.S. Entrepreneurial Households
papers.abstract: Investing in children’s human capital reduces business investments for U.S. entrepreneurial households. Using financial account data of 90,000 small businesses linked to their owners and a regression discontinuity design that compares the business performance of households with college-aged dependents (18–22) to those with near-college-aged dependents (14–17), I show that business revenues and expenses decline sharply when owners’ children reach age 18. Despite the declines, profitability and productivity remain largely unaffected, suggesting a general downsizing rather than a loss in efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows that downsizing is concentrated among highly indebted owner households and businesses with volatile cash flows. For each dollar increase in household spending associated with a child turning 18, business expenses decline by $2.26. These findings are consistent with entrepreneurial parents reallocating capital from business investments toward their children’s human capital, as both compete for the same pool of internal family financial resources. This paper was accepted by Camelia Kuhnen, finance. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04789 .

papers.title: Assessment of the Relationship Between Circular Supply Chain Management Practices and Sustainable Performance: A Meta‐Analysis of Empirical Evidence
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Given the growing economic, social, and environmental challenges, sustainable performance (SUSP) offers firms a viable pathway to overcome them and gain long‐term, meaningful business value. Several mechanisms, including the circular supply chain management (CSCM), are proposed to firms to achieve SUSP. However, some empirical findings have challenged this, prompting scholarly debate about the actual direction and strength of the relationship between CSCM and SUSP, thereby leaving prospective firms in a state of strategic ambiguity. To clarify the relationship, 55 empirical studies comprising over 15,000 observations and 109 effect sizes are synthesized through a psychometric, mixed‐model random‐effects meta‐analysis. The results show a positive and significant relationship, with the effect strongest in economic performance, followed by environmental performance, and weakest in social performance. A significant effect is established in most CSCM practices with SUSP dimensions. Economy type, firm size, sector, and innovation are established as significant moderators of the relationship. Findings guide managers on the CSCM practices to prioritize and inform policymakers on the contextual conditions under which the CSCM‐SUSP relationship is strongest. It advances the supply chain management (SCM) theories by clarifying the contingent and multidimensional performance effects of CSCM and resolving inconsistencies in prior findings.

papers.title: Confronting Biodiversity Risk: Its Role in Shaping Corporate External Financing Choice
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates how biodiversity risk shapes corporate financing decisions. We propose a Financing Hierarchy Distortion framework, arguing that biodiversity risk amplifies information asymmetry and legitimacy costs, thereby pushing firms toward debt‐heavy adjustments. To empirically test this, we introduce a novel firm‐level Biodiversity Risk ( Brisk ) measure derived from textual analysis of corporate disclosures and link it to objective ecological data via Biological Diversity Endowment ( BDE ). Using Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2009 to 2023 and excluding those in financial and real estate sectors and with ST designations, we find that higher biodiversity risk increases reliance on both formal and informal debt, particularly short‐term debt. These findings are robust to quasi‐causal identifications using difference‐in‐differences and instrumental variable strategies. Mechanism and heterogeneity analyses further corroborate the proposed framework and show that this distortion is more pronounced among firms in biodiversity‐dependent industries and those facing stronger institutional pressures. These adjustments, however, impose tangible economic costs, raising debt financing costs and depressing returns on assets. Overall, our findings highlight the unintended financial consequences of biodiversity risk, with policy implications for biodiversity disclosure standards, biodiversity‐linked financing instruments and the development of alternative credit channels to strengthen firm resilience under escalating ecological pressure.

papers.title: Self-enhancement or self-protection? How artificial intelligence awareness shapes taking charge behavior
papers.abstract: Purpose Drawing on self-enhancement and self-protection theory, this study aims to examine how artificial intelligence awareness (AIA) shapes hotel employees’ taking charge behavior (TCB), as well as the mediating effects of self-enhancement motivation (SEM) and self-protection motivation (SPM) and the moderating role of locus of control (LOC). Design/methodology/approach Using two-wave survey data from 428 hotel employees and their direct supervisors in China, hierarchical regression and bootstrapping procedures were used for data analysis. Findings AIA had a positive indirect effect on TCB through SEM and a negative indirect effect through SPM. LOC positively moderates the relationship between AIA and SEM and negatively moderates the relationship between AIA and SPM. Moreover, LOC significantly moderates the indirect effects of AIA on TCB via SEM and SPM. Practical implications Hotel managers should address employees’ motivational responses to AIA by enhancing SEM and reducing SPM through tracking artificial intelligence (AI) capability development and alleviating social comparison pressure in AI use. They should also tailor support to employees’ LOC and strengthen internal control beliefs. Originality/value By revealing two motivational mechanisms and highlighting the boundary role of LOC, this study extends research on employees’ TCB in the context of AI-driven technological change.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: Perception of artificial intelligence and intrinsic work motivation: evidence from Vietnam
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how sales staff’s perceptions of AI (i.e. perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) drive their intrinsic work motivation through AI use experience (AUE) and how internal training (IT) moderates this process within tourism and hospitality business. Design/methodology/approach Rooted in the technology acceptance model (TAM), flow theory and self-determination theory (SDT), this study used exploratory sequential mixed-method design. Scale purification (EFA) and scale validation (CFA) were conducted using SPSS and AMOS and hypothesis testing results were validated using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results revealed that PU and PEOU positively influence AI-specific intrinsic work motivation (AI-IWM) indirectly, through the mediating role of AUE. Furthermore, IT positively moderates the relationships between perception of AI and AUE, which ultimately improves AI-IWM. Practical implications The findings offer valuable insight into service and hospitality management sectors aiming to enhance work motivation among sales staff through AI. Given the significant influence of intrinsic motivation among sales staff in tourism and hospitality businesses, organization with a focus on AI adoption at workplace must be mindful of negative influence of AI on employees’ work motivation and outcome. Originality/value This study enriched the understanding of the motivations underlying the perception of AI and intrinsic work motivation by integrating insights from the TAM, SDT and flow theory. This study provided valuable implication for research and practices in the service business sector.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: Consumption value in GenAI travel photography: a mixed-methods study from an affordance–constraint perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose This study develops an affordance–constraint–value framework to explain how GenAI travel photography shapes consumption value and behavioral intentions. It aims to examine how perceived affordances and constraints relate to functional, emotional and social value, and how these value dimensions influence continuance and sharing intentions. Design/methodology/approach A three-phase mixed-methods design was used. Phase 1 applied topic modeling to 40,543 user-generated posts. Phase 2 surveyed 485 GenAI travel photography users and tested the structural model with PLS-SEM. Phase 3 used fsQCA to identify affordance–constraint configurations associated with high consumption value. Findings Phase 1 showed that public discourse centered on enabling conditions, value evaluations and behavioral tendencies. Phase 2 indicated that trialability, aesthetic creation and self-congruence were central to value formation, and that all three value dimensions increased continuance and sharing intentions. Phase 3 showed that high-value outcomes appeared through multiple sufficient configurations, with low AI hallucination risk recurring across solutions. Originality/value This study contributes to digital tourism and destination visual marketing by conceptualizing GenAI travel photography as generated self-in-place consumption. Integrating technology affordances and constraints theory with the theory of consumption value offers a more balanced explanation of how value is created, qualified and suppressed. Methodologically, it combines big-data exploration, net-effect testing and configurational analysis to explain value formation and its behavioral consequences.

papers.title: Visualizing myself there: affordances of GenAI travel selfies for engagement and visit intention
papers.abstract: Purpose Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) travel selfies have emerged as a novel pre-trip tourism touchpoint, yet their role in shaping user responses remains underexplored. Drawing on three-phase affordance actualization theory, this study aims to examine how GenAI travel selfie affordances are associated with user engagement and visit intention. Design/methodology/approach A three-study mixed-methods design was used, combining 32 photo-elicitation interviews, a survey of 526 users analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) of affordance configurations. Findings Three affordances were identified: visual creation, generative controllability and self-presentation. All three were positively associated with cognitive, affective and behavioral engagement, except for one nonsignificant path. User engagement was positively associated with visit intention. The fsQCA results further indicated that high engagement can be associated with multiple affordance configurations. Practical implications GenAI travel selfies can serve as a soft, user-driven promotional touchpoint for destinations and hospitality brands. Designers and marketers could consider identity-relevant design, controllable and reliable generative functions and visually appealing outputs to encourage engagement and stimulate early-stage destination interest. Originality/value The research is among the early empirical studies of GenAI travel selfies in tourism. It extends affordance-based research to a visual, identity-centered GenAI context and combines net-effect and configurational evidence to explain how these affordances are linked to user engagement and visit intention.

papers.title: Generativity and corrosion during scaling: How firms balance core and adjacent ecosystems to enable growth
papers.abstract: There is rising theoretical and practical interest in entrepreneurial scaling beyond traditional linear growth models. Recent scholarship highlights ecosystem management as a promising alternative to understand scaling, but it remains unclear how firms can use ecosystem strategies for scaling up, particularly after hitting growth plateaus. Through an in-depth case study of a Brazilian logistics firm based on rich empirical material consisting of 53 interviews and supported by internal documents, this paper investigates how entrepreneurial firms use adjacent ecosystem strategies to overcome growth plateaus and sustain scaling. We introduce the concepts of generativity and corrosion to explain this phenomenon. Our findings reveal that overcoming growth plateaus by scaling through adjacent ecosystems is a dual process: firms must promote generativity by using core assets to create novel value in adjacent markets, while simultaneously preventing corrosion by protecting the mature core from resource competition and misaligned interests. This research provides a nuanced framework demonstrating that successful scaling requires balancing different ecosystem maturities and orchestrating cross-ecosystem synergies.

papers.title: Beyond psychology and environment explanations: a linguistic microfoundation approach to entrepreneurs’ anxiety
papers.abstract: We offer a novel theoretical account of why entrepreneurs experience anxiety and how entrepreneurs cope with anxiety. We integrate insights from linguistic theories into entrepreneurship literature to propose that entrepreneurs’ linguistic architecture—particularly the vocabulary their language provides for identifying and describing emotions (i.e., its emotion lexicon)—is an essential linguistic microfoundation that systematically shapes how entrepreneurs process and experience anxiety. As moderators, we examine how bilingualism and entrepreneurial experience can systematically alter how entrepreneurs’ linguistic architecture influences their anxiety. Our final sample was 1,251 entrepreneurs speaking 14 different languages, supplemented by an experimental study with 202 bilingual entrepreneurs in Hong Kong. We find that entrepreneurs with a richer vocabulary for identifying and describing emotions (i.e., a richer emotion lexicon) heighten anxiety due to more precise and vivid emotional processing, and bilingualism weakens, yet prior entrepreneurial experience strengthens the positive effect of emotion lexicon on anxiety.

papers.title: CSR focus under competitive pressure: The role of national institutions
papers.abstract: How does competitive pressure shape CSR strategy, and does this relationship vary across national institutional contexts? We challenge the prevailing binary framing that competitive pressure either promotes or suppresses CSR by arguing that competition reshapes how firms configure their CSR portfolios, not merely how much they engage. We introduce CSR focus strategy: a firm's selective emphasis on specific CSR dimensions while deliberately de-emphasizing others, allowing simultaneous differentiation and cost-economization through CSR under some conditions. Employing multilevel linear modeling (MLM) on a global dataset of 41 countries comprising 2294 firms from 2002 to 2020, we demonstrate that competitive intensity drives adoption of CSR focus strategy. Critically, this effect is contingent on national market-supporting institutions and firm size, where CSR focus strategies are most pronounced in institutionally weaker environments characterized by limited property rights protection and among smaller firms with limited stakeholder relational capital and opportunities. Further analyses reveal two subtypes, namely CSR excellence and CSR distinction , reflecting different portfolio configurations under competition. By establishing that institutional context shapes firms' CSR portfolio configuration under competition, our study advances international business research and reconciles opposing theoretical positions in the competition-CSR debate. Collectively, these findings extend the emerging portfolio-based view of CSR into the cross-country competitive domain.

papers.title: The Bamboo Ceiling in the UK: Ethnicity–Gender Intersectionality, Risk Tolerance, and Leadership Attainment
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In the UK, Asians are often perceived as the “model minority” who face few hardships due to their strong educational performance and economic success. We question this perception by uncovering a “Bamboo Ceiling” in leadership attainment for certain Asian subgroups in the UK. Whereas many researchers and practitioners treat Asians as a monolith, we recognize heterogeneity among Asian subgroups and focus on comparing ethnic Chinese (the largest East Asian group) and ethnic Indians (the largest South Asian group). In Study 1, we analyzed CEOs and CFOs of the Financial Times Stock Exchange (FTSE) companies—the largest publicly listed companies in the UK—over a 14‐year period (2011–2024). There were virtually no ethnic Chinese CEOs or CFOs, whereas the representation of ethnic Indians in these positions did not differ significantly from that of Whites. In Study 2, we analyzed a large, nationwide dataset from the UK Biobank ( N = 322,734) to further investigate the moderating role of gender and the mediating role of risk tolerance. While ethnic Chinese overall experienced a Bamboo Ceiling (thus confirming Study 1's results), this main effect was moderated by gender: Ethnic Chinese men were significantly less likely than ethnic Indian and White men to attain leadership positions, a pattern partly mediated by ethnic differences in risk tolerance; by contrast, ethnic Chinese, Indian, and White women did not differ significantly and were each disadvantaged relative to their male counterparts. These effects were robust across survey‐based and polygenic measures of risk tolerance. Together, these findings underscore the importance of distinguishing among Asian subgroups and examining how ethnicity and gender intersect in leadership attainment.

papers.title: Firm-specific trade policy effect uncertainty and the bullwhip effect
papers.abstract: Purpose In an era of increasingly volatile trade policies, firms confront heightened uncertainty in demand forecasting and production planning, raising the potential for amplification of the bullwhip effect (BWE). Drawing on the BWE literature and on regulatory focus theory, which distinguishes between a promotion focus oriented toward gains and a prevention focus oriented toward loss avoidance, this paper investigates how firm-specific trade policy effect uncertainty (TPEU) influences the BWE, and how managerial regulatory focus moderates this effect. Design/methodology/approach Based on a sample of 37,017 firm-year observations from 4,104 publicly listed Chinese firms between 2002 and 2022, we employ ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings We find that TPEU significantly amplifies the BWE. This effect is exacerbated in firms led by promotion-focused top management teams (TMTs) and attenuated in firms led by prevention-focused TMTs. Mechanism analyses reveal that TPEU affects the BWE primarily through firms' operational adjustments on both the demand and production, as well as through broader supply chain restructuring. These results are robust to a series of empirical strategies designed to address potential endogeneity concerns. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on publicly listed Chinese firms and relies partly on textual measures derived from corporate disclosures. Accordingly, the findings may not fully generalize to firms operating in other institutional and trade policy environments, and the measures may partly reflect managerial disclosure choices. Future research could test and extend the proposed relationships through cross-country comparisons, alternative measures of trade policy effect uncertainty and managerial regulatory focus, and more granular operational data. Practical implications The findings suggest that firms should treat TPEU as an important source of operational instability. Managers should strengthen demand forecasting and policy monitoring, avoid excessive ordering and inventory adjustments, and manage customer and supplier restructuring carefully. Firms should also consider how TMT regulatory focus shapes operational responses to uncertainty and balance opportunity-seeking with risk-avoidance in supply chain decision-making. Social implications The study shows that trade policy uncertainty can generate operational consequences that extend beyond individual firms by amplifying demand and production variability and disrupting customer and supplier relationships. Such amplification can propagate through interconnected supply chains, potentially weakening overall supply chain stability during periods of trade policy change. The findings therefore highlight the broader social and economic value of improving firms’ ability to absorb policy-related uncertainty, maintain stable supply chain relationships and avoid unnecessary operational overreaction, thereby supporting more resilient supply chains in an increasingly uncertain global trade environment. Originality/value We contribute to the emerging literature on the intersection of operations and supply chain management and trade policy uncertainty by documenting the operational consequences of trade policy-induced uncertainty, and by underscoring the critical role of managerial regulatory focus in shaping operational responses to TPEU.

papers.title: External Governance Shocks and Legitimacy Repair Through CSR
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This study examines how firms adjust their corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance when product market competitors experience forced chief executive officer (CEO) turnover. Specifically, this study investigates whether peer CEO dismissals, as governance shocks signaling intensified board monitoring, trigger strategic CSR responses among rival firms. Research Findings/Insights Using US firm‐year observations from 2003 to 2020, this research documents that peer dismissals significantly increase firms' CSR performance, with effects concentrated in the social dimension rather than the environmental or governance dimensions. The positive relationship is stronger for firms with greater analyst coverage and for firms operating in more competitive markets, indicating that external scrutiny and competitive pressure strengthen strategic CSR adoption. Value‐creation tests demonstrate that CSR engagement in response to peer dismissals is associated with improved subsequent accounting performance, particularly in the social dimension. Theoretical/Academic Implications The findings support legitimacy theory over agency theory in explaining CSR motivations under governance pressure. This research demonstrates that CSR serves as an active legitimacy‐building mechanism rather than being constrained by governance discipline when firms face institutional pressures from peer governance failures. This research enriches the peer spillover literature by moving the focus from passive information transfer to active legitimacy management and extends executive turnover research by identifying CSR as a strategic response channel to external governance shocks. Practitioner/Policy Implications Boards and executives should recognize that peer governance failures create reputational risks requiring strategic stakeholder engagement. The evidence suggests that CSR practices can effectively mitigate legitimacy threats following industry‐wide governance shocks. Policymakers should recognize that governance failures in one firm create industry‐wide legitimacy threats that extend beyond the affected company and that the information environment plays a critical role in shaping how these threats spread across product markets.

papers.abstract: This study examines how organizational goals, leadership styles, and organizational culture influence employee outcomes in the Korean public sector. Using Structural Equation Modelling, data from 6,170 public servants were analysed. Organizational goals positively influenced commitment and performance efforts. Transactional leadership positively affected organizational culture and commitment but negatively affected performance efforts, whereas visionary leadership showed positive effects across all three outcomes. Organizational culture enhanced commitment and performance efforts, while organizational commitment positively influenced performance efforts and perceived organizational performance. Performance efforts also enhanced perceived organizational performance. These findings highlight how goals, leadership, and collaborative culture jointly shape employee and organizational outcomes.

Macro-level geospatial determinants of E-bike crash risk: town-level analysis
papers.abstract: Electric bicycles have become a dominant mode of transportation in many Chinese cities, including Guangzhou, raising growing concerns about traffic safety resulting in fatalities and injuries among riders. This study performs a macro-level geospatial analysis to explore the spatial variability of factors influencing town-level counts of fatal and injury (FI) and property damage only (PDO) e-bike crashes across 170 towns in Guangzhou, which in this study represent spatial patterns in crash risk at the town level. One year of e-bike crashes and traffic violation data, integrated with environmental and infrastructural variables, such as population density, road network characteristics, land use diversity, and public facility densities, was used to examine spatial associations with FI and PDO crash counts. Spatial autocorrelation and Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) analysis revealed significant clustering, with 64 towns (37.6%) identified as high-risk hotspots. To explore spatial heterogeneity in predictor associations, three models were applied: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR), and Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR). Within this exploratory Gaussian comparison, MGWR yielded the lowest AICc and highest adjusted R 2 ; however, most predictors exhibited near-global, spatially stationary associations, with localized variation observed only for selected predictors. Count-data diagnostics confirmed substantial overdispersion; therefore, geographically weighted negative binomial regression with a global dispersion parameter (GWNBRg) was applied, yielding deviance pseudo-R 2 values of 0.356 for FI and 0.251 for PDO crashes. Positive Gaussian associations for population density, traffic violations, and intersection density were not consistently corroborated by the negative binomial analyses. By contrast, higher school and healthcare facility densities were negatively associated with FI crashes in the global log-transformed negative binomial analysis (p = 0.014 and 0.027) and received greater nominal local GWNBRg support (29.4% and 17.1% of towns, respectively). These associations are observational and noncausal. These exploratory findings provide a preliminary data-driven basis for evidence-informed e-bike safety planning while highlighting that most predictors exhibit spatially stationary associations across towns.

papers.title: Beyond Legal Recognition: Parental Acceptance and Couple-Level Minority Stress on Same-Sex Couples’ Well-Being in Chinese Societies
papers.abstract: Abstract Previous studies in the Global North suggest that same-sex marriage brings positive impacts on the well-being of lesbian, gay, bisexual, queer, and plus (LGBQ+) individuals. Parental acceptance is challenging yet important for LGBQ+ individuals, especially in Chinese societies, which strongly emphasize harmony and heteronormative family relationships. This paper examines the association between the legal recognition of same-sex couple relationships and one’s individual and relational well-being, and how it is mediated by parental acceptance and couple-level minority stress. We surveyed 812 LGBQ+ respondents in committed same-sex relationships in two Chinese-majority societies, Taiwan (with legal recognition of same-sex couple relationships) and Hong Kong (without such policy). We found that Taiwan respondents reported higher levels of parental acceptance and a lower level of couple-level stigma and discrimination than their counterparts in Hong Kong. While Taiwan respondents reported better relational well-being, there was no significant difference in individual well-being between the two societies. Experience of couple-level stigma and discrimination was associated with higher levels of depression. We argue that parental acceptance explains much of the significant variation in relationship satisfaction, beyond living in societies with or without legal recognition of same-sex couple relationships. As such, we underscore the importance of parental acceptance for LGBQ+ individuals in their relationship with their same-sex partners in Chinese societies. Furthermore, as same-sex couples continue to encounter couple-level minority stress and challenges in gaining parental acceptance, there is a need for mental health and social services to provide targeted support to enhance their well-being.

papers.title: Union Strength, Collective Bargaining, and Strike Activity: Insights From Chile's 2017 Labor Reform
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We study the causal impact of Chile's 2017 labor reform—which banned the replacement of striking workers and restricted unilateral extension of collective benefits—on strike activity, wages, and employment. Using administrative data on all regulated collective negotiations from 2008 to 2024 in a difference‐in‐differences framework that exploits pre‐reform variation in union density, we find no increase in strike incidence and modest decreases in strike voting and actual stoppages among more unionized firms. Effects on wages are negligible; effects on employment are positive but display pre‐reform trends. The pattern is consistent with the joint cost model and with the institutional‐context literature.

Parametric assessment of urban rooftop photovoltaic potential: Threshold calibration and spatial differentiation by city scale classification
papers.abstract: Assessing the potential of urban rooftop photovoltaic (URPV) is fundamental for promoting energy transition and urban sustainability. However, existing research is often confined to potential assessments, failing to reveal the driving mechanisms and critical parameter thresholds at the city scale. To address this gap, this study systematically calculates the URPV application potential for 330 cities using a potential estimation framework, incorporating sequential corrections for solar irradiation at optimal tilt angles, rooftop availability factor, ambient temperature, and rooftop area density. Multiple linear regression is applied to deconstruct factor influences on annual generation, while XGBoost is introduced to diagnose whether linear model failure for small cities stems from nonlinearity or scale confounding. A parametric method calibrates thresholds of key factors, leading to an optimized generation model tailored to city size, validated on five representative cities. Results indicate that the total URPV power generation potential is approximately 70,691 GWh, with a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.36 CNY/kWh and a net carbon emission reduction (NCER) of about 7.83 × 10 8 t. Rooftop area density is the most critical driver across all city sizes. More importantly, city scale systematically moderates the effects of all drivers, with XGBoost confirming that small-city linear failure is attributable primarily to confounding by urban area, not inherent non-linearity. This moderation further manifests as distinct parameter threshold patterns. The optimized model, incorporating these scale-specific thresholds, yields an average midpoint relative error of 8.92% across the five validation cities, confirming internal consistency. The study provides a scientific methodological reference and data support for estimating power generation in cities of different sizes.

papers.title: A single safe policy for fast charging control of multi-chemistry and multi-size battery packs using contextual reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion battery (LIB) packs is constrained by thermal runaway risk, cell state-of-charge (SOC) imbalance, and accelerated capacity fade, challenges compounded by spatial temperature gradients and the diversity of cathode chemistries and configurations across electric vehicles and stationary storage. Existing reinforcement learning (RL) approaches address fast charging for a single chemistry and fixed pack size, requiring complete retraining when the battery type or configuration changes, which represents a critical barrier to scalable battery management system (BMS) deployment. This paper proposes a contextual Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework that encodes battery chemistry and pack size as explicit episode-level context variables. A single proximal policy optimisation (PPO) agent thereby generalises across three cathode chemistries, namely nickel manganese cobalt oxide (NMC), lithium cobalt oxide (LCO), and lithium iron phosphate (LFP), as well as five pack layouts (4–16 cells) without retraining. Seven neural surrogate models: three electro-thermal surrogates, three degradation models, and one thermal-runaway safety classifier, are trained on publicly available datasets and drive a configurable pack simulator, eliminating proprietary equivalent-circuit model identification. LFP’s near-flat open-circuit voltage plateau, rendering SOC unobservable from terminal voltage over 20–80% SOC, is resolved via Coulomb-counting state augmentation. A novel entropy-clipping mechanism prevents catastrophic PPO policy degradation in long-horizon episodes, and a two-phase progressive curriculum reduces LFP training cost by threefold. Evaluation across all 15 chemistry–layout combinations achieves 100% charging success (SOC: 0.20 → 0.80 , 75/75 episodes). Relative to 1 C CC–CV, the policy reduces charging time by 44% for NMC, 60% for LFP, and 79% for LCO, while peak temperatures remain below the corresponding chemistry-specific safety limits. Code and implementation details are available at GitHub repository .

papers.title: From coast to cost: Mispricing and reform scenarios in Italy’s coastal concession system
papers.abstract: Many governments allocate access to high-rent natural resources through long-term concessions rather than competitive auctions. In Italy, coastal concessions for beach tourism have historically been renewed administratively, in tension with the EU Services (“Bolkestein”) Directive and recent European Court of Justice rulings. We provide an empirical assessment of this system, focusing on how concession fees relate to firms’ performance and local market conditions. We combine administrative data on maritime concessions with balance-sheet information from AIDA at the province and municipality levels, and exploit firm-level identifiers for the Campania region. First, we document strong spatial disparities: fees co-move with revenues but are weakly related to profits, while labor input is the main operational driver. Second, using a Pareto-based framework, we show that the nationally administered fee grid implies substantial under-pricing in high-inequality areas. Third, we construct firm-level valuation proxies in Campania using machine learning and use them to simulate exploratory auction scenarios. The results show that auction-based mechanisms can raise payments among allocated concessions, but aggregate fiscal gains depend critically on reserve prices, competition intensity, and fallback rules for non-allocated lots.

papers.title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
Challenges in the decarbonization of the UK electrical power system by 2030: A techno-economic analysis of current and alternative policies
papers.abstract: Forecasts indicate that the UK will miss its Clean Power 2030 targets. This study evaluates the techno-economic barriers and limitations in terms of infrastructure, demand, and resources of Clean Power (2030) Action Plan policies by conducting thorough discussions with power sector experts. Identified limitations in the literature together with interview findings allow us to suggest actionable policies. Even though there have been previous works on the techno-economic barriers pertaining to achieving Clean Power by 2030, this paper presents a fresh systematic approach, by applying a meta-theoretical framework to analyse holistically the techno-economic barriers in this energy transition. While previous works on this topic focus mostly on near-term market intelligence, and policy- or investor-oriented insights, the novelty of this work provides operational insights from industry experts. Results reveal a gap between ambitious policy objectives and ground-level implementation concerns; such as unrealistic milestones, and conflicting local authorities and government timelines. This paper outlines the following policies to facilitate UK's transition to a zero-carbon power system: (1) reform the planning and permitting system with new amendments, (2) assess the NESO project applications in batches, (3) mandate community benefits sharing, (4) run an independent board to facilitate effective communication amongst various stakeholders, (5) undertake market integration of demand-side response and flexibility providers, (6) offer technology-specific incentives, and (7) address supply chain contingency agreements.

papers.title: Green hydrogen promotion in Cameroon: Implications for sustainable development
papers.abstract: This paper argues that green hydrogen could be a driver of the technological transformation of a small open economy well integrated into the global energy market. Green hydrogen development is key to a sustainable transition of the economy. It can replace CO 2 -intensive technologies, e.g., in the transport sector, water cleaning facilities, and the steel industry. As the renewable energy potential is particularly high in Sub-Saharan Africa, it appears to be promising to install green hydrogen production facilities there, where they can contribute to “greening” the domestic economy while excess hydrogen production can be exported to generate revenue. In this paper we introduce a normative recursive growth model to investigate the case of Cameroon and demonstrate that the establishment of a green hydrogen sector can contribute to sustainable development where economic development goes hand in hand with environmentally friendly technological change. An essential precondition is education because the accumulation of human capital is necessary for implementing and distributing new, innovative technologies, as well as for building market institutions to lower the cost of capital and attract FDI to support the transformation of the Cameroonian economy.

papers.title: Thermoacoustic systems for electrical power generation: Review of conversion technologies, performance characteristics, and practical applications
papers.abstract: Despite their potential to convert waste heat into electricity with no moving parts in the thermoacoustic core, thermoacoustic electricity generators (TAEGs) remain underutilized in industrial energy-recovery applications. Industrial processes collectively reject 20-50% of the input energy as waste heat, representing an electricity-generation potential equivalent to 15-20% of current global electricity consumption, yet commercial TAEG deployment remains constrained by manufacturing barriers, reliability validation gaps, and insufficient cross-laboratory reproducibility. TAEGs offer a versatile conversion approach compatible with industrial, solar, and biomass heat sources, with an inherent combined cooling-and-power (CCP) capability that organic Rankine cycle (ORC) and thermoelectric generator (TEG) systems cannot architecturally provide. This review examines TAEG research from its fundamental thermodynamic principles to commercial deployment, categorizing systems into standing-wave and traveling-wave configurations and evaluating four acoustic-to-electric conversion technologies: electromagnetic linear alternators, piezoelectric transducers, magnetohydrodynamic generators, and bidirectional turbines. Each technology is assessed in terms of its operating principles, performance, and application suitability, with findings synthesized into a comparative framework benchmarked against ORC and TEG systems, including explicit treatment of cross-study comparison limitations and uncertainty in synthesized metrics. TAEGs demonstrate competitive advantages in three niches: sub-150°C low-grade heat sources, distributed scales below 20 kW, and combined cooling-and-power applications. To improve cross-laboratory reproducibility further, we propose the Minimum Thermoacoustic Experimental Reporting Framework (MTERF), a voluntary 11-parameter reporting checklist. Near-term deployment is conditionally achievable for rural biomass electrification and small-scale marine waste-heat recovery, pending field validation of reliability beyond 20,000 operating hours; multi-kilowatt industrial-scale systems require a 5–10-year deployment horizon contingent on reliability validation, manufacturing scale-up at competitive cost, and resolution of bidirectional-turbine blade fatigue limitations.

papers.title: Analysis of Multiple Tire Rubber-Derived Chemicals in Fish Bile and Plasma: Analytical Method and Field Assessment in Puget Sound, WA, USA
papers.abstract: Abstract Tire rubber-derived chemicals (TRCs) are known to be highly toxic to fish, but understanding of their environmental levels and fate is still limited. This study presents a new method for the analysis of 18 TRCs, including phenylenediamines (TRC-PDs), their quinone derivatives (TRC-Qs), and rubber vulcanizing and curing-related chemicals (TRC-VCRs) in fish bile and plasma samples. We applied this method in bile and plasma samples from English sole collected in urban, near-urban, and nonurban sites in Puget Sound, WA, USA. TRCs were detected in 100% of bile and 96% of plasma samples from English sole collected from all nine sites in Puget Sound. Mean TRC levels in bile samples per site ranged between 0.8 and 18 ng/mL, while plasma levels ranged between 0.22 and 0.63 ng/mL, with total summed reaching up to 31 ng/mL in bile and 1.3 ng/mL in plasma. TRC-PDs were the most abundant group of TRC in both bile and plasma. Higher levels of TRCs in bile suggests this matrix to be more valuable for environmental monitoring, providing more sensitive detection of TRC during low exposures. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first data set reporting environmental levels of 18 TRCs in the bile and plasma of field-caught fish.

papers.title: Bridging Exposure and Mechanism: A Mechanism-Weighted Ecological Risk Assessment Reveals Divergent Priorities for Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals in China
papers.abstract: Abstract The proliferation of novel entities in the Anthropocene threatens aquatic biodiversity, yet traditional ecological risk assessment (ERA) may rank chemicals primarily by exposure and effect concentration, despite chemicals exhibiting widely differing receptor-mediated toxicity. To address this limitation, this study developed a mechanism-weighted ERA (mw-ERA) framework that integrates molecular docking-derived binding free energies of six key endocrine-related receptor targets (e.g., estrogen and thyroid hormone receptors) with exposure data for 139 endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) in surface water around 234 Chinese cities. Docking outputs were standardized using z-scores and transformed into a mechanism weight factor (MW) to summarize relative docking-derived receptor-binding potential and refine exposure-based ecological risk prioritization. The mw-ERA framework identified 31 EDCs with MW > 1, indicating above-average docking-derived interaction potential across the selected receptors. Among these, 20 chemicals were prioritized as candidates for endocrine-relevant testing, including bisphenols, estrogens, several phthalate esters, and antibiotics that were underestimated via exposure-only ranking. Conversely, most per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances showed MW < 1, reflecting weaker predicted binding potential with the selected receptors relative to the study data set. By integrating receptor-mediated mechanism information with exposure data, this framework provides a biologically grounded, near-term actionable, and computationally efficient approach for prioritizing EDCs for ecological risk management.

papers.title: Prototyping Chain-Elongation-Mediated Dehalogenation for Groundwater Bioremediation
papers.abstract: Abstract Chlorinated ethenes are widespread groundwater contaminants. Microbial reductive dehalogenation can detoxify chlorinated ethenes but requires sustained H2 delivery to organohalide-respiring bacteria. In enrichment cultures, microbial chain elongation was shown to reliably provide H2 for dehalogenation from the conversion of ethanol and acetate to butyrate and caproate and subsequent fermentation of these carboxylates. Supported by robust laboratory testing, here, we document the first field-scale application of chain elongation-mediated dehalogenation in chlorinated ethene-contaminated groundwater. Native groundwater communities produced mainly propionate from ethanol and acetate in microcosms and the field, whereas bioaugmentation with a chain-elongating enrichment culture redirected microbial metabolism toward butyrate production and supported dehalogenation to ethene. Dehalogenation was favored at a lower organic carbon loading (900 mg C L–1 either as ethanol + acetate, butyrate, or caproate). Chain elongation was more strongly stimulated at higher ethanol to acetate molar ratios and organic carbon loadings (3500 mg C L–1). Bioaugmentation with chain-elongating bacteria in groundwater produced detectable butyrate concentrations, increased the molar ratio of ethene and ethane from 0.20 to 0.51 during monitoring, and did not stimulate methanogenesis. This study positions chain elongation-mediated dehalogenation as an effective strategy for groundwater bioremediation of chlorinated ethenes.

papers.title: Synergistic Approaches in PFAS Remediation: Outlook for Sustainable In Situ Mitigation by Combined Adsorption and Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent organic pollutants with widespread environmental occurrence. Their toxicity and resistance to degradation pose serious risks to ecosystems and human health. While existing separation (e.g., adsorption, filtration) and degradation (e.g., photochemical, electrochemical, thermal) technologies can achieve partial PFAS removal, limitations such as high energy demand, poor cost-efficiency, and harsh operating conditions hinder their in situ application. In this context, a synergistic approach, a system in which adsorption and degradation are functionally coupled rather than applied as independent sequential unit operations, has emerged as a promising route. This review critically examines the coupling of biopolymer-based adsorption and photocatalytic degradation as a sustainable and effective solution for PFAS remediation. Biopolymers such as lignin, chitosan, and cellulose offer a renewable alternative to conventional sorbents, exhibiting adsorption capacities of ∼50–500 mg g–1 and beyond in advanced systems and removal efficiencies of up to 99% in dilute conditions, while photocatalytic platforms, such as semiconductor-based systems, reach ∼32–100% degradation efficiencies, with up to 92% defluorination in optimized systems. When combined functionally, these systems enhance PFAS degradation through interfacial preconcentration and reduce secondary waste. The review critically evaluates recent advances in material development, mechanistic understanding, and system integration, alongside the roles of Life Cycle Assessment and Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning, as complementary tools guiding the design and deployment of sustainable PFAS-remediation strategies.

papers.title: Kinetic Aerosol Trapping Drives Arctic Enrichment of Organophosphate Flame Retardants
papers.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) are emerging contaminants posing significant risks to the Arctic environment and human health. Concerns have been raised about the origins of Arctic OPFRs because atmospheric models have failed to reproduce the high Arctic OPFR levels due to unresolved phase-partitioning dynamics and atmospheric chemistry. Here, we implement a kinetic gas-particle accumulation scheme, in which particle-bound OPFRs do not re-equilibrate to the gas phase, into the atmospheric chemistry model GEOS-Chem High Performance (GCHP) v14.5.0. A 2 × 2 factorial design crossing the partitioning mechanism with hydroxyl radical (OH) chemistry isolates the importance of each process. In the Arctic, kinetic accumulation reduces the apparent OH removal efficiency from 79% under equilibrium partitioning to 64%. The corresponding atmospheric lifetime of ΣOPFRs is extended from 1.0 day under gas-phase-only conditions to 9.8 days under the kinetic accumulation framework. Sulfate and hydrophilic organic carbon together carry over 90% of the Arctic particulate OPFR burden. This kinetic scheme increases the simulated Arctic annual mean ΣOPFR concentration from 82 pg m–3 under gas-phase-only conditions and 145 pg m–3 under instantaneous equilibrium to 353 pg m–3, representing 4.3-fold and 2.4-fold increases, respectively, consistent with field measurements across the Arctic.

papers.title: Breaking the Rigid-Locking Effect: Unlocking Efficient Fenton-Like Reactions for Water Decontamination
papers.abstract: Abstract Overcoming the kinetic bottleneck of Fe(II) regeneration has always been a top priority for enhancing Fenton/Fenton-like processes to degrade emerging contaminants (ECs). In conventional iron-based catalysts (e.g., Fe2O3, FeOOH), the iron center is tightly locked inside a rigid cage of hexa-oxygen coordination ([FeO6] unit) that is resistant to geometric distortion and electron transfer. This phenomenon, termed “Rigid Locking Effect”, hinders the Fe(III)-to-Fe(II) conversion. To break this, we propose a ligand-engineering strategy by partially replacing oxygen coordination with chlorine, featuring a unique [O-FeCl4–O] motif in laminated reduced graphene oxide (rGO) nanochannels. DFT calculations and Fe XAS spectra reveal that the active [O-FeCl4–O] unit exhibits “Rigid” breaking, including low reorganization energy, strong electron delocalization, and enhanced spin–orbit coupling (SOC). This tailored motif significantly promotes Fe(II)/Fe(III) cycling, resulting in a turnover frequency per iron site (TOFFe) of 43.66 h–1, which is a 1091-fold enhancement compared to that of the conventional [FeO6] motif in Fe2O3. This enhancement leads to a 30.7-fold increase in HO• yield, enabling efficient removal of diverse ECs in complex water matrices and during long-term continuous operation. This study establishes a proof-of-concept paradigm for designing efficient heterogeneous catalysts and advances practical Fenton-based water decontamination.

papers.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Issue Publication Information
Spatiotemporal Magnetic Decoupling Directs Spin-Dependent Cascade ROS Evolution for Electro-Fenton Water Decontamination
papers.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous electro-Fenton (HEF) systems hold great potential for decentralized water purification, yet concurrently achieving high catalytic activity, structural stability, and controlled reactive oxygen species (ROS) selectivity remains challenging. Herein, we propose a spatiotemporal magnetic decoupling strategy to concurrently address these design objectives. The carbon shell spatially separated exterior Fe0 satellites from the FeNx core, eliminating deleterious short-range magnetic quenching and altering the local magnetic environment to modulate the internal Fe(III) spin state. The resulting low-spin Fe(III) sites suppressed electron back-donation into the H2O2 σ∗ antibonding orbital, favoring an additional 1O2 generation pathway. Spatial decoupling also enabled a gradient cascade activation of H2O2 across the Fe0 and FeNx domains, synergistically boosting the evolution of both •OH and 1O2, with steady-state concentrations reaching 18.25 and 5.27 μM, respectively. Consequently, the FeNx@C–Fe0-based HEF achieved complete naproxen degradation within 60 min with significantly suppressed Fe leaching (0.85 mg L–1), outperforming all comparative systems. Comprehensive characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations established a definitive relationship between topological engineering and spin-state dynamics. Furthermore, the system demonstrated proof-of-concept applicability in real hospital wastewater, highlighting the potential of spatiotemporal spin-state engineering for regulating ROS evolution in HEF systems.

papers.title: Capturing the Organic Fluorine in Aqueous Film-Forming Foam (AFFF)-Impacted Groundwater: Suspect Screening, Extractable Organofluorine, and the Total Oxidizable Precursor Assay
papers.abstract: Abstract The widespread use of aqueous film–forming foam (AFFF) for firefighting and firefighter training has led to extensive per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) contamination in the environment, yet the mass budget for PFASs in AFFF-impacted groundwater across diverse sites remains uncertain. Here, we integrated targeted analysis, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS)-based suspect screening, extractable organofluorine (EOF), and the total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay to evaluate total organic fluorine in 23 groundwater samples collected from 12 AFFF-impacted sites. Across all samples, total targeted PFAS concentrations ranged from 0.35 to 980 μg/L, and the highest summed PFAS concentrations, including suspect PFASs, reached 1,000 μg/L. EOF levels ranged from 5.9 to 670 μg F/L. Targeted PFASs explained 0.82–93% of the EOF (median: 44%), whereas targeted and suspect PFASs contributed 0.82–100% (median: 50%). Targeted PFASs together with oxidizable precursors quantified by the TOP assay accounted for 5.7–100% of the EOF (median: 54%). Importantly, the majority of EOF (>50%) could be explained by targeted and suspect PFASs or precursors from the TOP assay in groundwater where EOF concentrations were high (e.g., ≥50 μg F/L). These results demonstrate that combining suspect screening, EOF, and the TOP assay provides a more comprehensive assessment of PFAS contamination in AFFF-impacted groundwater, while the unresolved organofluorine indicates the presence of unidentified fluorinated compounds not captured by current workflows.

Latent versus sensible thermal storage for load-shifting energy management in medium-deep U-type geothermal heat pump systems: A comparative performance analysis
papers.abstract: Thermal energy storage can enhance load shifting and extend heat-pump shutdown periods in medium-deep U-type borehole heat exchanger (MDUBHE) heating systems. However, latent and sensible thermal energy storage are commonly evaluated separately, and their differences in heat-supply capability, operating performance, and storage-volume requirements under unified conditions remain unclear. In this study, PCM-based latent storage and water-tank-based sensible storage were integrated with an MDUBHE heat-pump system and compared using consistent boundary conditions and control strategies. Seven PCM materials were first evaluated, followed by analyses of storage volume, dynamic charging and discharging, seasonal heat supply, building-load regulation, volumetric utilization, and marginal benefits. A system without thermal storage was also considered as the baseline. PCM47 achieved a seasonal energy recovery ratio of 99.68%, a heat-supply contribution of 17.50%, and an independent heating duration of 778.65 h, showing the best combined performance among the candidate materials. As the PCM volume increased from 10 to 50 m 3 , its seasonal contribution and independent heating duration increased from 4.65% to 20.46% and from 186.20 to 899.62 h, respectively. At the same volume of 50 m 3 , the PCM tank supplied 605.29 MWh of heat and provided 899.62 h of independent heating, compared with 175.68 MWh and 241.08 h for the water tank. The average heat-pump COP values of the latent-storage, sensible-storage, and no-storage systems were 5.48, 5.53, and 5.62, respectively, while the corresponding seasonal performance factors (SPFs) were 4.36, 4.52, and 4.78. Although latent storage caused stronger ground-side thermal disturbances and a moderate efficiency penalty, its heat supply per unit volume was 3.45–3.92 times that of sensible storage. Under equivalent heat-supply performance, PCM storage reduced the required volume by 72.34–74.78%. These results quantify the trade-off between load-shifting capability, operating efficiency, and storage compactness, providing guidance for storage-technology selection and capacity sizing in MDUBHE heating systems.

A Land-Sea integrated ecological compensation framework based on carbon sequestration service flows: Evidence from a Coastal City
papers.abstract: Ecological compensation (EC) is an important policy instrument for coordinating ecological conservation and economic development and promoting carbon neutrality. However, existing EC policies in coastal regions remain largely terrestrial-oriented, making it difficult to identify cross-regional dependence on land-sea carbon sequestration services (CSs) and the corresponding compensation responsibilities. Using Qingdao, China, as a case study, this study develops a land-sea integrated EC framework that combines random forest, the IPCC inventory method, and a spatial interaction model to identify land-sea CSs supply-demand patterns and carbon sequestration service flows (CSF), and to allocate EC responsibilities accordingly. The results show that: (1) from 2004 to 2023, the imbalance between CSs supply and demand continuously intensified, with pronounced spatial mismatches; (2) CSF exhibited clear land-sea coupling, with the sea area and coastal mountainous area (Laoshan District) serving as the major CSF sources. CSF outflows from the sea area accounted for 29.02%–47.81% of the total positive regional CSF and primarily flowed to the rapidly urbanizing area of Huangdao District; and (3) actual EC payments differed markedly from ideal responsibilities across county-level administrative units, while the sea area received 78.10% of total inter-county compensation receipts. The Ecological Compensation Priority Index (ECPI) further indicated that the sea area and key terrestrial CSs supply areas should be prioritized for compensation. By integrating land-sea ecological contributions, external CSs dependence, compensation responsibilities, and implementation priorities into a unified analysis, the framework can support more equitable and efficient EC decision-making in coastal regions.

papers.title: Simulated Trampling Disturbance Alters Biocrust Microbial Communities and Soil Functions: A Container‐Based Mesocosm Experiment
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological soil crusts (biocrusts) are crucial components of dryland ecosystems; however, they are highly vulnerable to anthropogenic disturbances, particularly trampling caused by grazing. To evaluate the impacts of trampling on biocrust structure, microbial communities, and soil functions, we conducted a mesocosm‐based simulated disturbance experiment (D1: moderate; D2: severe) on cyanobacteria‐ and moss‐dominated biocrusts, respectively, in Qubqi desert, China. After 1‐year natural recovery, results indicated that disturbance significantly reduced biocrust thickness, soil carbon and nitrogen content, with more pronounced effects under D2 treatment. Regardless of biocrust type, bacterial communities were dominated by Cyanobacteria, Proteobacteria, and Actinobacteria, with their relative abundances varying across disturbance gradients. Notably, stress‐tolerant taxa such as Actinobacteria tended to increase in both biocrust types under D2 treatment, although these changes were not statistically significant. Compared to cyanobacteria‐dominated biocrusts, moss‐dominated biocrusts had lower Cyanobacteria abundance, with Proteobacteria becoming the more dominant phylum; however, the relative abundance of Proteobacteria declined significantly under D2 treatment. In contrast, fungal communities remained relatively stable across all treatments in both biocrust types, with Ascomycota consistently dominating. Mantel tests further revealed community structures of Proteobacteria, Actinobacteria, Cyanobacteria, and Ascomycota were strong associations with the soil nutrient profiles. Overall, microbial community restructuring and soil functional degradation became evident with increasing disturbance intensity. Distinct microbial responses and resilience to disturbance further suggest that restoration strategies based on microbial manipulation may represent an important pathway for maintaining biocrust ecosystem functioning in dryland regions.

papers.title: Identity politics, partisan sentiment and household spending
The impact of comprehensive student support on crime: Evidence from the pathways to education program
Aim high or play safe? Commitment, prosocial incentives, and goal setting
papers.abstract: Abstract We examine how behavioral incentives affect goal setting and performance when individuals choose their own goals. Using a model with reference-dependent preferences and effort cost uncertainty, we predict that commitment mechanisms improve performance by inducing more conservative goal selection to increase goal attainability, whereas prosocial incentives enhance performance by increasing motivation. Two experiments confirm these predictions. In an online real-effort task, soft commitment reduced goals relative to controls but significantly increased performance, whereas prosocial incentives, in the form of charitable donations contingent on goal achievement, preserved goal ambition and improved performance without lowering goals. A four-week field experiment in which students set daily exercise goals yields similar results: commitment lowered goals while increasing performance, whereas prosocial incentives maintained ambitious goals and improved outcomes. These effects persisted throughout the experiment. These findings highlight that, under effort cost uncertainty, commitment and prosocial incentives improve performance through distinct mechanisms.

papers.title: Revitalizing Leadership Research: Three Directions
papers.abstract: Abstract The contributions in this Point‐Counterpoint present divergent directions for revitalizing research on leadership. All three pieces express concerns with the current state of behavioral leadership research but place varying weight on those problems. How the three contributions define the most pressing issues with this literature and how they conceive of leadership itself leads to distinct agendas for the future of leadership studies: leadership as relationships in action, a theory‐based view of leadership, and a many‐valued logic approach. The introduction to this collection summarizes these perspectives, highlights where they converge and diverge, and considers their implications for the future of leadership scholarship. It concludes that leadership research is unlikely to advance by converging on a single paradigm. Rather, advances will more likely come from dialogue and debate, just like that occurring among the contributions to this Point‐Counterpoint.

papers.title: The Real Reasons Why Digital Projects Fail
papers.abstract: Digital tools meant to improve business processes don’t always deliver value when implemented on the front lines, but efforts to identify what’s behind such failures often don’t get at the real cause. One reason is that leaders simply blame poor adoption on user resistance to change, for example. A new framework can help them take a closer look at data quality issues and system usability issues, both of which can cause problems for users.

papers.title: Constructing Green Organizational Identity: Cultural Meanings, Sustainability Discourse, and Identity Work in Vietnam's Logistics Industry
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite growing interest in green organizational identity (GOI), existing research has largely treated it as a relatively stable organizational attribute or an antecedent of environmental outcomes, with limited attention to how it is socially constructed within emerging economy contexts. This study examines how GOI is constructed and enacted within Vietnam's logistics industry. Drawing on an interpretive qualitative approach, this study is based on semistructured interviews with nine managers and executives from logistics organizations in Vietnam. The findings show that participants understood sustainability not merely as a managerial or environmental objective but as a culturally embedded process through which they interpreted responsibility, legitimacy and organizational identity. The findings indicate that GOI is understood through organizational culture, sustainability discourse, institutional context, and identity work, as participants described translating global sustainability expectations into locally meaningful narratives and practices. The study contributes to GOI scholarship by conceptualizing GOI as a negotiated and culturally situated process rather than a stable organizational attribute, demonstrating how organizational actors translate external sustainability expectations into locally meaningful identity claims and practices. It further highlights the importance of cultural context in shaping sustainability meanings and responsible organizing within emerging economy settings.

papers.title: Effects of Executive Sustainability Compensation on Nonexecutive Employee Behavior
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In response to growing awareness of climate change and increasing regulatory sustainability requirements, many companies now link executive compensation to specific sustainability criteria. Although prior research has examined the effects of such incentives on executive behavior, this study explores how executive sustainability‐linked compensation and leadership tone influence the sustainable behavior of nonexecutive employees. Using an online experiment, I find that informing nonexecutive employees about executive bonuses tied to sustainability targets significantly increases their likelihood of making sustainable decisions. In contrast, tone from the top information does not have a statistically significant effect. The results have important implications for theory, practice, and policy by highlighting transparent communication of sustainability‐linked executive incentives as a simple yet powerful tool for fostering sustainable change among nonexecutive employees as well. Ultimately, this study contributes to advancing the understanding of employee‐level sustainability efforts and offers practical strategies to support the sustainable transformation of business and society.

Toward an Audience‐Based View of Incumbent Adoption of Potentially Discontinuous Technologies: Evidence From Fintech
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We advance an audience‐based view of incumbent adoption of potentially discontinuous technologies. Drawing on theories of discursive institutional processes and categorical legitimacy, we model how incumbents navigate mixed judgments from external groupings in their environment, that is, audiences, when adopting prospective discontinuous technologies. We argue that incumbents filter this noisy discursive environment by factoring in audiences' credibility and authority. We develop contextualized hypotheses and test them on a longitudinal sample of 149 incumbent financial firms responding to the emergence of financial technology in Europe from 2000 to 2016, distinguishing industry insiders, support experts, the general public, and regulators. Uniform engagement across audiences has a non‐linear influence on adoption. Incumbents respond most visibly to judgments from the general public and resist positive engagement from support experts. Industry insiders' and regulators' engagement did not have robust direct linear effects. Our findings reveal a preparadigmatic legitimacy puzzle wherein conventional institutional predictions systematically fail or reverse when legitimacy signals remain contested across audiences. We develop four propositions theorizing the expertise penalty, democratic legitimacy under uncertainty, authority without clarity, and temporal heterogeneity of audience influence, establishing the need to differentiate between audiences to understand incumbent responses in the preparadigmatic phase of technology evolution.

Species‐Specific Shrub Encroachment Drives Divergent Soil Fungal Assembly Processes and Network Structures in Alpine Meadows
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Shrub encroachment is rapidly transforming alpine meadow ecosystems worldwide, yet its consequences for belowground microbial organization remain insufficiently understood, particularly when different shrub species exert contrasting ecological effects. Here, we investigated how three dominant shrub species— Rhododendron capitatum , Salix oritrepha , and Dasiphora fruticosa —influence soil fungal communities across encroachment gradients in an alpine meadow on the northeastern Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Using a space‐for‐time substitution approach combined with high‐throughput sequencing and network analysis, we analyzed soil fungal community composition, inferred functional guild structure, community assembly processes, and correlation‐based co‐occurrence network topology. Shrub encroachment was associated with changes in soil fungal community composition. Across species, the inferred relative abundance of putative saprotrophic fungi declined with encroachment, and taxa putatively identified as ectomycorrhizal fungi were consistently enriched in interspaces. Fungal community assembly showed species‐specific patterns. Under R. capitatum , stochastic processes dominated (ecological drift: 66.7%–80% of assembly), with reduced co‐occurrence network complexity. In contrast, encroachment by S. oritrepha and D. fruticosa suggested increased habitat homogenization and a shift toward stronger deterministic assembly: ecological drift declined by 46.67% and 60.03%, respectively, while homogeneous selection and network complexity increased. Notably, only severe D. fruticosa encroachment showed higher robustness in node‐removal simulations, whereas network robustness did not differ significantly among encroachment stages for R. capitatum or S. oritrepha plots. Collectively, these results suggest that shrub encroachment does not exert uniform effects on soil fungal communities; instead, shrub identity is associated with divergent community organization patterns and inferred assembly pathways.

papers.title: Aerial Seeding for Forest and Landscape Restoration: A Systematic Review of Technology, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Land degradation is a critical global challenge, threatening biodiversity, food security, and livelihoods. Ecological restoration has therefore become a priority, with aerial seeding emerging as a key method to address issues of scale, accessibility, and efficiency. By dispersing seeds from aircraft or drones, aerial seeding complements ground‐based approaches and is especially effective in remote or degraded areas. First applied in agriculture during the 1940s, its role has expanded with technological advances that allow greater precision, though challenges such as seed predation and uneven distribution remain. A systematic literature review (SLR) of studies published between 2000 and 2024 synthesized current evidence and identified research gaps. A total of 34 articles were analyzed, showing increased interest since 2017, with China contributing 29% of publications. Highly cited studies emphasized unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications in forest regeneration. The literature was stratified into two primary domains: environmental constraints and associated mitigation strategies, and technological innovations designed to overcome technical barriers in aerial seeding. Findings show that aerial seeding is an effective, low‐cost method for large‐scale restoration. It is particularly valuable for degraded and postfire landscapes, where it enhances carbon recovery and reduces costs compared to manual planting. However, outcomes depend on seed traits, site conditions, timing, and predation pressure. Future success will rely on technological advances, ecosystem‐specific strategies, and adaptive responses to climate change. By enhancing seed resilience and precision delivery, aerial seeding could become a cornerstone of global reforestation and restoration efforts.
